nodes.label: WATCH_VTICK virtual clock
nodes.rationale: Cut from v0.2.0 to v0.2.5 because de-flaking the wall-clock watch tests is a multi-layer refactor, not a drop-in: integer bash arithmetic crashes on fractional WATCH_TICK, and the WD_AGE virtual-clock add must cover both the latched wd_sample path and the unlatched real-time fallback.

nodes.label: Host-wide gate mutex (one bats run at a time)
nodes.rationale: Concurrent bats runs corrupt wall-clock tests and orphaned auditor runs caused MSYS2 fork exhaustion that flaked unrelated gates; doctrine became no agent runs bats unless it is the sole gate, with a pueue gate group at parallelism 1.
nodes.norm_label: host-wide gate mutex (one bats run at a time)

nodes.label: MSYS2 fork-resource exhaustion (errno 11)
nodes.rationale: Observed as a single el_emit taking 10.4s versus about 100ms and gates stretching from 45min to 2h; keep host concurrency low and serialize gates.

nodes.label: Background-and-stop attractor
nodes.rationale: Dominant failure across three vendors (12 occurrences): agents background a long task and end their turn, orphaning it. Prompt prohibitions provably do not hold, so the fix must be structural: artifact-defined completion plus a launcher that owns the whole round including gate and report, plus an auto-resume primitive.

nodes.label: Content and process-aware watchdog liveness
nodes.rationale: Scaffold-existence keys produced three false-alert modes (stale-report existence, no dispatch grace, gate-phase blind spot where a lane writes only to /tmp); final form is size-gated report freshness OR a live worktree process.

nodes.label: wt-cleanup drops versioned audit reports
nodes.rationale: Only fixed FOREMAN_REPORT.md names are archived, so V2/V3/V4 reports were lost; fix is to glob FOREMAN_REPORT star dot star plus DIFF star dot patch.

nodes.label: SC-A agent-stop survivability
nodes.rationale: Proven live: a --round unit enqueued through lane-queue.sh completed with the dispatching shell already exited, and the event log alone showed prompt, ownership, state and round_done with zero manual resumes.

nodes.label: SC-B whole-round ownership
nodes.rationale: Killing the launcher pid must reap the whole tree including grandchildren and the gate, so the gate runs under the launcher and the POSIX group-kill targets the gate's own pgid.

nodes.label: SC-C bounded auto-resume
nodes.rationale: Resume is bounded by durable.resume_max_attempts and ends in exactly ONE terminal abandoned alert, so a never-completing round cannot loop forever.

nodes.label: SC-D stale-report immunity
nodes.rationale: A report older than this round's prompt event must never satisfy the terminal predicate; it raises an alert instead of round_done.

nodes.label: SC-E no concurrent writers on resume
nodes.rationale: A lane with a live pid or a held .harness/lane.lock is never resumed (ALIVE noop), and a per-run .supervise.lock serializes sweepers.
nodes.norm_label: sc-e no concurrent writers on resume

nodes.label: SC-F completion provable without the agent
nodes.rationale: Every classification derives from the event log, checkpoint refs and heartbeat file alone; SUCCEEDED requires round_done with gate_rc 0.
nodes.norm_label: sc-f completion provable without the agent

nodes.label: Watch v2 lane classifier
nodes.rationale: Classifies a killed round WAITING_CHILD/AGENT_ABANDONED and never SUCCEEDED; log-silent plus heartbeat-advancing is VERIFYING, both-quiet is STALLED.

nodes.label: pgid reaper rule
nodes.rationale: The POSIX build has no kernel cascade equivalent to Windows job objects, so killing by process group is doctrine and is enforced in code wherever lane-run owns the kill.

nodes.label: Five-part spec contract
nodes.rationale: Subagents do not share chat context, so delegation must be context-free: the spec alone has to determine the outcome.

nodes.label: Decorrelated cross-family review
nodes.rationale: Different model family review beats same-family self-review because model families share blind spots; also never trust a worker's own 'tests passed' claim, the orchestrator re-runs checks.

nodes.label: Schema-forced auditor verdict JSON
nodes.rationale: Structured output beats free-form prose for audits; the verdict schema was aligned to add the summary field agents already emitted and the auditor agent gained --output-schema per the Codex cookbook.

nodes.label: Foreman hard mode
nodes.rationale: Shipped only partially at QA time: INIT/CHECK/EVIDENCE/GATE present, AUDIT added as audit-run.sh, IMPLEMENT and PR only stubs, Docker adapters still missing.

nodes.label: audit-run.sh host Codex Sol audit stage
nodes.norm_label: audit-run.sh host codex sol audit stage

nodes.label: Recommended default soft pipeline
nodes.rationale: Claude architect on Fable routes to grok-implementer, verifies the diff itself, then codex-auditor reviews read-only with an output schema and foreman-advisor is consulted only at commitment boundaries; no separate Grok TUI window is needed because Claude shells out.

nodes.label: foreman-advisor agent
nodes.rationale: Distinct from Anthropic's server-side advisor API tool: same 'commitment guidance' purpose, different surface.

nodes.label: CHECK stage fail-closed fix
nodes.rationale: CHECK had an always-green bug; audit infrastructure must fail closed when missing rather than silently pass.

nodes.label: Live CLI flag validation (not flag fiction)
nodes.rationale: Flags claimed in docs were confirmed against the installed binaries on this machine (grok --prompt-file, --permission-mode acceptEdits; codex exec --output-schema, --sandbox read-only, codex exec review) so the harness never depends on invented flags.
nodes.norm_label: live cli flag validation (not flag fiction)

nodes.label: Explore agent cost pin for Fable sessions
nodes.rationale: Built-in Explore inherits the session model, so on a Fable session broad exploration is a cost risk unless a cheap model override is pinned.
nodes.norm_label: explore agent cost pin for fable sessions

nodes.label: Agent Skills open format
nodes.rationale: Packages procedural knowledge and org-specific context into portable, version-controlled folders agents load on demand, giving domain expertise, repeatable workflows and cross-product reuse.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure (discovery, activation, execution)
nodes.rationale: Only name and description load at startup so many skills can be on hand with a small context footprint; full instructions load only when a task matches.

nodes.label: Agent Skills open-standard governance (Anthropic-originated, Apache-2.0)
nodes.rationale: Originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard, code Apache-2.0 and docs CC-BY-4.0, open to ecosystem contributions.

nodes.label: advisor_20260301 server tool
nodes.rationale: Server-side beta tool (advisor-tool-2026-03-01) letting a cheaper executor model consult a stronger advisor model mid-turn; there is no conversation-level cap, callers must count calls client-side.

nodes.label: Executor and advisor model split
nodes.rationale: A cheap executor (Haiku/Sonnet) does the volume work while an expensive advisor (Fable) supplies judgment, so premium tokens are spent only where design decisions live.

nodes.label: pause_turn resume protocol
nodes.rationale: A response can end with stop_reason pause_turn while an advisor call is pending; resuming means resending the assistant message unchanged with the server_tool_use block and the same beta header, and omitting the tool returns 400 invalid_request_error.

nodes.label: Mid-conversation advisor nudge
nodes.rationale: Model-dependent: a plain-text reminder at NUDGE_TURN 2 raised Haiku executor pass rates about 7 percentage points, had no measurable effect on Sonnet, and slightly LOWERED pass rates on Opus, so it must not be applied uniformly.

nodes.label: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions
nodes.norm_label: orchestrate teams of claude code sessions

nodes.label: Claude Code agent teams
nodes.rationale: Experimental and disabled by default behind CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS; best for research, review, competing-hypothesis debugging and cross-layer work, and worst for sequential tasks or same-file edits because coordination overhead and token cost are high.

nodes.label: Teammate session
nodes.rationale: Each teammate is a separate Claude instance with its own context window that can be addressed directly without going through the lead, unlike a subagent which only reports back.

nodes.label: Orphaned tmux sessions (agent-teams failure mode)
nodes.rationale: Documented troubleshooting case alongside 'lead shuts down before work is done' — the same lost-ownership class Foreman's launcher work targets.

nodes.label: Give Claude a way to verify its work
nodes.rationale: A checkable signal (tests, build, lint) is what turns generation into convergence; without it the model cannot tell done from plausible.
nodes.norm_label: give claude a way to verify its work

nodes.label: Explore, plan, code, commit workflow
nodes.rationale: Planning pays off when the approach is uncertain or the change spans files; if the diff fits in one sentence, skip the plan because plan mode adds overhead.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md persistent project context
nodes.rationale: Loaded every session, so it should hold only broadly applicable rules; sometimes-relevant domain knowledge belongs in skills instead.

nodes.label: Specific context in prompts
nodes.rationale: Scope the task, point at sources, reference existing patterns and describe the symptom; vague prompts are only useful when exploring and able to course-correct.

nodes.label: --bg background session
nodes.rationale: Returns immediately with a session id and management commands; cannot be combined with -p/--print, and --exec runs a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude session.

nodes.label: --advisor model flag
nodes.rationale: Enables the server-side advisor tool for a session with an alias (opus, sonnet, fable) and takes precedence over the advisorModel setting.

nodes.label: --bare minimal mode
nodes.rationale: Skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster.

nodes.label: --agents dynamic subagent JSON
nodes.rationale: Defines subagents inline using the same field names as frontmatter plus a prompt field, so a harness can inject lane agents without writing files.

nodes.label: Flag absence from --help is not unavailability
nodes.rationale: claude --help does not list every flag, so capability checks must consult the reference or probe the binary rather than grepping help output.
nodes.norm_label: flag absence from --help is not unavailability

nodes.label: Managed Agents multiagent orchestration (capture incomplete)
nodes.rationale: The fetched extract contains only navigation chrome and repeated 'Loading...' placeholders, so the page body was never captured; any claim sourced to this file is UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Skill discovery from parent and nested directories
nodes.rationale: Project skills load from every .claude/skills up to the repo root and nested ones load on demand, so starting in a subdirectory still picks up root skills and monorepo packages can own their own.
nodes.norm_label: skill discovery from parent and nested directories

nodes.label: Directory-qualified nested skill names
nodes.rationale: Name collisions resolve by scope rather than by shadowing: the nested variant appears as apps/web:deploy and Claude picks the variant matching the files being worked on.

nodes.label: Live skill change detection
nodes.rationale: Covers SKILL.md text only; hooks, .mcp.json, agents and output-styles changes in a skill-as-plugin need /reload-plugins, and a brand-new top-level skills directory needs a restart to be watched.

nodes.label: Skill as plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json)
nodes.rationale: Lets one folder bundle agents, hooks and MCP servers alongside the skill; in a project .claude/skills this requires accepting workspace trust first.

nodes.label: Claude Code subagent
nodes.rationale: Runs within a single session with its own context window and reports results back to the main agent only, which is why delegation must be context-free.

nodes.label: Subagent YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, model)
nodes.rationale: Subagents are plain Markdown files with frontmatter; as of v2.1.198 /agents no longer opens a creation wizard, so authoring is file-editing or asking Claude to write the file.
nodes.norm_label: subagent yaml frontmatter (name, description, tools, model)

nodes.label: Subagent scope (user-level vs project-level)
nodes.rationale: A file in ~/.claude/agents is available in every project; moving it to a project .claude/agents scopes it to that repo.

nodes.label: Description-driven auto-delegation
nodes.rationale: The description field is what makes Claude route work to a subagent unprompted, so it carries the routing contract and must state when to use the agent.

nodes.label: Read-only tool restriction for reviewers
nodes.rationale: Restricting a reviewer to Read/Grep/Glob and pinning a cheap model keeps a review lane incapable of mutating the tree it is judging.

nodes.label: Architect pattern (smartest model runs the show)
nodes.rationale: The session runs on the most capable model and owns requirements, decomposition, specs and verification, routing every implementation task to the cheapest adequate lane.
nodes.norm_label: architect pattern (smartest model runs the show)

nodes.label: Lane routing table (routine, cross-vendor, judgment)
nodes.rationale: Routine work goes to Grok when the spec fully determines the outcome, correctness-critical work to Codex GPT-5.6 Sol or races both lanes, and commitment boundaries to the Fable advisor.

nodes.label: Token cost discipline (tokens route by volume)
nodes.rationale: Implementation mechanics are about 90% of a session's tokens and cheap lanes handle them at near-parity, so the expensive model must emit judgment not volume: reason once, then hand off.
nodes.norm_label: token cost discipline (tokens route by volume)

nodes.label: Vendor diversity (cross-vendor review for free)
nodes.rationale: Models from one family share blind spots; keeping the architect Claude while the producers are Grok and GPT means every diff is reviewed across lineages by construction, not as a bolted-on step.

nodes.label: grok-implementer agent (Grok 4.5 via Grok CLI)
nodes.rationale: Drives grok headlessly with --prompt-file and -m grok-4.5; without an installed authenticated CLI it reports STATUS: unavailable and never silently falls back to a Claude model.

nodes.label: codex-implementer agent (GPT-5.6 Sol high reasoning)
nodes.rationale: Optional second independent implementation lane; fails loudly with STATUS: unavailable when the CLI, auth or model access is missing so the other lanes stay unaffected.

nodes.label: fable-advisor agent (read-only skeptic)
nodes.rationale: Consulted before architecture decisions, migrations, API designs and after a problem resists two attempts; returns a verdict under 300 words, never implements, and pays off even from a Fable session because it sees the code without the conversation's accumulated assumptions.

nodes.label: Quiet Claude model-pin fallback hazard
nodes.rationale: If a pinned Claude model is unavailable on the account, Claude Code silently falls back to the session model so the pattern degrades quietly instead of erroring; the grok and codex lanes by contrast always fail loudly.

nodes.label: Model resolution order in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL env var, then per-invocation model parameter, then agent frontmatter, then session model.
nodes.norm_label: model resolution order in claude code

nodes.label: Advisor-only mode (cheap session, expensive consult)
nodes.rationale: The inverse arrangement for keeping the session cheap: one agent file, Sonnet session, advisor consulted only at commitment boundaries for cents per consult.

nodes.label: Codex CLI (terminal coding agent)
nodes.rationale: Three pillars: work against the local repository, stay in control of model/reasoning/permissions, and compose with scripts and CI via codex exec.

nodes.label: codex exec (non-interactive run)
nodes.rationale: Stable maturity, alias codex e, streams to stdout or JSONL and can resume previous sessions — the supported headless surface for a harness lane.

nodes.label: --sandbox policy (read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access)
nodes.rationale: Selects the sandbox for model-generated shell commands; read-only is the correct posture for a reviewer that must not mutate or exfiltrate.

nodes.label: CODEX_HOME state and profile isolation
nodes.rationale: --profile layers $CODEX_HOME/profile-name.config.toml over the base user config, so a per-lane CODEX_HOME gives each lane its own state and config root.

nodes.label: --strict-config (error on unknown config fields)
nodes.rationale: Fails closed when config.toml contains fields this Codex version does not recognize, instead of silently ignoring them.

nodes.label: codex app-server (experimental local server)
nodes.rationale: Stands up a local endpoint over stdio, WebSocket or a Unix socket — the mode that can race on a port, which one-shot codex exec avoids entirely.

nodes.label: Feature maturity labels (Experimental, Beta, Stable)
nodes.rationale: Lets a harness depend only on Stable surfaces (codex, exec, review, resume) and treat Experimental ones such as app-server and cloud as non-load-bearing.

nodes.label: Build code review with the Codex SDK (cookbook)
nodes.norm_label: build code review with the codex sdk (cookbook)

nodes.label: Structured review output schema (findings, overall_correctness, confidence)
nodes.rationale: Forces every finding to carry title, body, priority, confidence_score and an exact code_location line range, plus one overall correct/incorrect verdict — machine-consumable instead of prose.
nodes.norm_label: structured review output schema (findings, overall_correctness, confidence)

nodes.label: Cold diff in the prompt
nodes.rationale: The review prompt embeds repository, PR number, base/head SHAs, changed-file status and the unified diff, so the reviewer judges the change itself with no session history to bias it.

nodes.label: Read-only sandbox for the reviewer
nodes.rationale: The CI action runs with sandbox read-only so a reviewer can never write the tree it judges or hold credentials it could exfiltrate.

nodes.label: openai/codex-action GitHub Action
nodes.rationale: Takes prompt-file, output-schema-file, output-file, sandbox and model, which is the same shape as a Foreman audit lane invocation.

nodes.label: Inline review comment publishing
nodes.rationale: jq maps each schema finding to a GitHub pulls/comments payload keyed on the exact line range, which is why the prompt insists citations be exactly correct or comments get rejected.

nodes.label: Severity discipline (actionable findings only)
nodes.rationale: Flag only actionable issues introduced by the change, prioritize severe ones and avoid nit-level comments unless they block understanding of the diff.

nodes.label: Codex sandboxing doc fetch (404 page not found)
nodes.rationale: The captured extract is OpenAI's 'Page not found' shell, so this file documents a broken source URL rather than sandbox behavior; sandbox facts must come from the developer-commands reference instead.
nodes.norm_label: codex sandboxing doc fetch (404 page not found)

nodes.label: Grok Build coding agent
nodes.rationale: Usable three ways — interactive TUI, headless in scripts or bots, and over the Agent Client Protocol in other apps.

nodes.label: ~/.grok/config.toml custom model config
nodes.rationale: Any custom model can be registered with model id, base_url, name and env_key, and grok inspect reveals which config sources, instructions, skills, plugins, hooks and MCP servers were discovered in the current directory.

nodes.label: grok -p headless mode
nodes.rationale: Flags that matter for a worker lane: -p single prompt, -m model, --cwd explicit working directory, --output-format plain/json/streaming-json, --always-approve, --no-alt-screen.

nodes.label: Headless session ids (--session-id, --resume, --continue)
nodes.rationale: Headless sessions persist under ~/.grok/sessions, which is what makes per-lane session keying (and per-lane GROK_HOME) meaningful.

nodes.label: --no-auto-update in automation
nodes.rationale: Background update checks are nondeterminism inside a gated pipeline; suppress them per-invocation or persistently with auto_update=false under [cli].

nodes.label: ACP agent over JSON-RPC (grok agent stdio)
nodes.rationale: session/prompt returns only completion metadata while assistant text arrives as session/update chunks, so a client must accumulate chunks rather than expect a single reply.
nodes.norm_label: acp agent over json-rpc (grok agent stdio)

nodes.label: Grok Build parallel subagents with worktrees
nodes.rationale: Launch-post claim of specialized subagents running in parallel and launchable in their own worktrees; marketing-level evidence of intended concurrency, not a guarantee about N independent CLI processes on one host.
nodes.norm_label: grok build parallel subagents with worktrees

nodes.label: Plan, review, approve mode
nodes.rationale: A plan can be approved, commented on per-step or rewritten before execution, and every post-approval change shows up as a clean diff.

nodes.label: Works with existing AGENTS.md, plugins, hooks, skills and MCP
nodes.norm_label: works with existing agents.md, plugins, hooks, skills and mcp

nodes.label: Foreman orchestration options deep-research report
nodes.rationale: Central finding: most workflow engines solve durable state better than they solve OS-process ownership, so the winning plan is to keep the orchestration core in-house and stop relying on Bash to be the process owner.

nodes.label: Windows Job Objects with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE
nodes.rationale: Closing the last job handle terminates every associated process, which is exactly the tree-ownership invariant the timeout/wrapper stack was missing; it is the only primitive that solves F1 and F2 by construction on this host.

nodes.label: Native Windows lane launcher
nodes.rationale: A tiny launcher (Rust, Go or .NET) creates the job object, spawns the vendor CLI as its child, forwards stdio, emits heartbeats, and on timeout performs a graded stop: cancel/CTRL_BREAK, then close the job handle, then terminate. Every alternative platform still needs this same component.

nodes.label: pueue (persisted local queue and supervisor)
nodes.rationale: Gives persisted queues, logs, per-group parallelism, kill/restart/pause, JSON status and crash recovery with full Windows support; its deliberate refusal to be a distributed scheduler is a feature for a single-host harness, and it is the natural place to enforce per-vendor lane admission control.

nodes.label: GNU timeout is not tree ownership
nodes.rationale: In --foreground mode children of the command are not timed out, and even coreutils 9.10's improved signal propagation does not give Windows-native tree ownership.
nodes.norm_label: gnu timeout is not tree ownership

nodes.label: Event log plus git checkpoint architecture
nodes.rationale: Keep events.jsonl plus refs/checkpoints as the source of truth, distinguishing run, lane, attempt and checkpoint entities, with monotonic sequence numbers and cursor semantics for replay from a given attempt/checkpoint; compact non-structural chatter while keeping structural milestones immutable.
nodes.norm_label: event log plus git checkpoint architecture

nodes.label: Typed lane state machine
nodes.rationale: QUEUED, STARTING, RUNNING_IMPL, RUNNING_AUDIT, VERIFYING, WAITING_CHILD, STALLED, DEAD, SUCCEEDED, FAILED replaces 'mtime plus vibes': queued is not running, verifying is not stalled, and silence alone must never classify a lane.

nodes.label: WAITING_CHILD state
nodes.rationale: Exists specifically to kill F2: a wrapper may not transition to any terminal state until the native launcher reports child exit AND the required report artifact is present.

nodes.label: Phase-aware heartbeat protocol
nodes.rationale: Heartbeat every 15-30s carrying PID, job id, exit code if known, cumulative stdout/stderr byte counters and a phase enum; stall is computed from heartbeats plus phase, never from file writes. Suggested phase-aware thresholds: STARTING 90s, RUNNING_IMPL 5min, RUNNING_AUDIT 15min, VERIFYING 10min, then a 10s graceful cancel before job-close kill.

nodes.label: CI liveness prior art (Buildkite, GitHub Actions, GitLab Runner)
nodes.rationale: Mature systems use multiple channels: Buildkite marks an agent lost after 3 missed heartbeat minutes and gives a 10s cancel grace; GitHub Actions uses explicit background/wait semantics instead of inferring done from silence; GitLab Runner has stage-specific timeouts and a 5-minute boot_verify canary.
nodes.norm_label: ci liveness prior art (buildkite, github actions, gitlab runner)

nodes.label: F2 wrapper stops while subprocess runs
nodes.norm_label: f2 wrapper stops while subprocess runs

nodes.label: F3 vendor CLI serializes parallel lanes
nodes.rationale: No candidate platform fully solves it; the report treats it as evidence that git worktrees alone do NOT imply vendor-CLI concurrency.
nodes.norm_label: f3 vendor cli serializes parallel lanes

nodes.label: F4 file-mtime watchdog false alarms
nodes.rationale: Root cause is inferring process liveness from a single signal (worktree writes).

nodes.label: F5 mid-response deaths lose lane context
nodes.norm_label: f5 mid-response deaths lose lane context

nodes.label: F6 remote lane history drifts from main
nodes.norm_label: f6 remote lane history drifts from main

nodes.label: Merge-base freshness gate
nodes.rationale: F6 is not a VCS problem but a freshness problem: record the dispatch merge-base, re-check it before final verification, fail fast when ancestry is lost, and respawn from a fresh base rather than automating salvage — modeled on GitHub required up-to-date checks and merge queues.

nodes.label: Per-lane vendor config-dir isolation
nodes.rationale: Ranked lowest-risk workaround for F3: unique GROK_HOME/CODEX_HOME and redirected Claude memory per lane; medium risk is per-vendor queue caps outside the CLI; highest risk is assuming worktrees imply CLI concurrency.

nodes.label: GROK_HOME per-lane config root
nodes.rationale: Supported by the layered config path model but UNVERIFIED as a concurrency remedy, so xAI stays at a pueue group of 1 until destructive tests prove otherwise.

nodes.label: CODEX_HOME per-lane state isolation
nodes.rationale: Officially supported for local state isolation, but app-level 'run many agents in parallel' marketing is not CLI-level proof, so high parallelism stays UNVERIFIED pending tests.

nodes.label: Shared per-project Claude memory across worktrees
nodes.rationale: Auto memory lives under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ and every worktree of the same repo shares it, so worktree-only isolation is insufficient for Claude lanes.
nodes.norm_label: shared per-project claude memory across worktrees

nodes.label: Prefect (runner-up adaptation target)
nodes.rationale: Best full orchestrator with first-class Windows support and a SQLite-backed self-hosted server, but it orchestrates runs rather than arbitrary CLI subprocess trees, so it fixes F4/F5 immediately and F1/F2 only if you build the same launcher; 20-35 dev-days.

nodes.label: Temporal (durable execution benchmark)
nodes.rationale: Conceptually aligned with append-only history, replay and resumability, but its deployment story is Linux/Kubernetes-shaped and the activity worker would still need to own the subprocess tree; 35-60 dev-days, so strategic rather than immediate.

nodes.label: Hatchet (Docker/Postgres durable task platform)
nodes.rationale: Closest in shape to Foreman (background tasks, retries, rate limits, replay) but self-hosting requires Docker or Kubernetes, conflicting with the Windows-no-Docker baseline; 25-40 dev-days.

nodes.label: Windmill (Bash/PowerShell scripts and flows)
nodes.rationale: Speaks Bash and PowerShell natively, but native Windows workers are a self-hosted Enterprise feature, so the Docker-free Windows path is not the open-source path — a non-finalist under the stated constraints.

nodes.label: LangGraph (checkpointers, threads, time travel)
nodes.rationale: Best source of design ideas for checkpoints, thread ids and replay/fork semantics, but its durability is about graph state, not owning a Windows process tree; borrow the concepts rather than rebuilding the control plane.

nodes.label: Claude Code process and session primitives
nodes.rationale: Worktree-native parallel sessions plus a background-session supervisor (claude agents/attach/daemon status/stop/respawn) prove these behaviors are already normal in a modern harness, but they govern Claude sessions only, not arbitrary third-party CLI trees.
nodes.norm_label: claude code process and session primitives

nodes.label: Migration cost matrix (dev-day estimates)
nodes.rationale: Harden in place 12-18 dev-days versus Prefect 20-35, Hatchet 25-40, Temporal 35-60, LangGraph-as-core 15-25 — and every alternative still buys the same launcher.

nodes.label: 30/60/90-day adoption plan
nodes.rationale: Day 30 ship the launcher, replace Bash-owned timeouts, add explicit lane states, put vendor lanes behind conservative pueue groups; day 60 checkpoint/resume from git refs, event cursors, merge-base gates, mandatory config-dir isolation; day 90 decide whether to prototype Prefect around the hardened launcher.

nodes.label: vendor-concurrency-test.sh destructive harness
nodes.rationale: Spins N same-vendor lanes each with its own config dir, throwaway workdir and own $HOME (exported as USERPROFILE too, for runtimes that resolve home via the Windows API), runs them concurrently and checks all four abort monitors before printing a verdict. Real-CLI only, never in CI or an automated gate.

nodes.label: Four EARS abort monitors
nodes.rationale: Containment snapshot, config-JSON validity, lock-acquisition freeze / forced kill, and cross-lane auth invalidation — a green verdict requires all four, and caps rise only on a green reproducible row.

nodes.label: Per-lane $HOME isolation
nodes.rationale: Rework round 1 finding: the first harness shared the ambient $HOME, so a vendor writing $HOME-relative state (exactly the shape of Claude's ~/.claude.json) would have been invisible to the containment scan.

nodes.label: Pre/post auth re-probe (non-billing)
nodes.rationale: Uses the same non-billing commands as tool-check.sh's vendor_authed (grok models with a fail-closed positive-signal check, codex login status); a lane authenticated before but not after the run is an abort.

nodes.label: Credential-staging classifier blocker
nodes.rationale: Copying real auth.json into isolated config dirs was denied twice by the host safety classifier and no lower-tier API key existed, so the first attempt recorded NO GREEN rather than faking a verdict or routing around the denial.

nodes.label: Unauthenticated auxiliary evidence (never a green basis)
nodes.rationale: Empty-config runs exercise containment and real-CLI robustness but cannot exercise cross-lane auth invalidation or 429-versus-shared-quota, so per EARS they must not justify any cap raise.
nodes.norm_label: unauthenticated auxiliary evidence (never a green basis)

nodes.label: Live user-authorized shared-account run
nodes.rationale: The user explicitly authorized all lanes sharing one real logged-in identity and its quota, path-isolated by cwd plus a unique session id, since separately-staged credentials were blocked.

nodes.label: grok pueue cap raised 1 to 3
nodes.rationale: GREEN at N=2 then N=3: all lanes rc=0 with exact expected replies, no 429 under shared quota, ~/.grok changes benign and keyed by cwd plus UUID, auth intact on the post-run re-probe. N=3 was only attempted after N=2 came back clean.

nodes.label: codex pueue cap raised 1 to 2
nodes.rationale: GREEN at N=2 only, and the cap rises only to the proven-green N. No port collision because codex exec is one-shot and never stands up the app-server the collision class needs; codex keeps session state in SQLite which serializes concurrent writers natively.

nodes.label: Claude REQUIRES-SEPARATE-HOME ruling
nodes.rationale: Ruled from the public issue record with no local run: .claude.json is written non-atomically so concurrent instances race and truncate it, and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does not cover top-level session state — a safe Claude lane needs a genuinely distinct $HOME.

nodes.label: False containment RED from Windows MAX_PATH
nodes.rationale: codex's bundled-plugin cache nests deep enough to exceed the 260-character MAX_PATH, so jq.exe could not open a valid JSON file and the harness misreported corruption; fixed by feeding jq via stdin instead of a path argument.
nodes.norm_label: false containment red from windows max_path

nodes.label: False 429 rate-limit signal
nodes.rationale: A bare substring match on 429 fired on a codex thread_id UUID containing 9429; fixed with a word-bounded match that still catches genuine status 429.

nodes.label: grok promoted to eligible default implementer
nodes.rationale: Follows from the recorded green rows; Sonnet nonetheless remains the standing default this era.
nodes.norm_label: grok promoted to eligible default implementer

nodes.label: REPORT_compile — bun build --compile for foreman-launch
nodes.rationale: Verdict GO-WITH-CAUTIONS: ship foreman-launch as a bun-compiled Windows x64 exe because the critical path was verified live, accepting a ~94MB binary, non-reproducible builds and SmartScreen friction.

nodes.label: bun build --compile single-file executable
nodes.rationale: Cross-compiles in both directions via --target, embeds files under /$bunfs/, and supports Windows metadata/icon/console flags; incompatible with --outdir, --public-path, --target=node and --no-bundle.

nodes.label: bun:ffi dlopen of system DLLs inside a compiled binary
nodes.rationale: Verified live on Bun 1.3.14: kernel32.dll and user32.dll dlopen and call correctly from the compiled exe. The scary issue reports concern a different path — dlopen of a bundled /$bunfs/ library — which was fixed by PR #30720 and never affected on-disk system paths.
nodes.norm_label: bun:ffi dlopen of system dlls inside a compiled binary

nodes.label: ~94MB compiled binary size floor
nodes.rationale: 93.9MB measured with --minify; a minimal-runtime option is a long-standing open request (#14546), so the floor stands. Startup measured 47-70ms, idle RSS ~46-49MB.

nodes.label: Post-build Authenticode signing
nodes.rationale: Since Bun v1.2.23 Bun strips its own signature so signtool can sign the exe afterwards; signing plus an RFC3161 timestamp is the mitigation for SmartScreen friction on a large unsigned novel binary, and reputation accrues per certificate.

nodes.label: Non-reproducible compiled builds
nodes.rationale: Verified: two back-to-back identical builds produced different SHA256 hashes and no determinism guarantee exists, so two developers cannot produce identical binaries — build once in CI and treat that artifact plus its published hash as canonical.

nodes.label: --bytecode cross-compile segfault (#18416)
nodes.rationale: Cross-compiled bytecode exes segfault on the target OS, so use --bytecode only when host equals target — or skip it, since a tiny launcher's parse time is negligible.

nodes.label: Runtime frozen at compile time (pin plus startup assertion)
nodes.rationale: The exe embeds the whole Bun runtime of the compiling Bun, so behavior is baked in and a stray bun upgrade silently changes the shipped runtime; pin via .bun-version and packageManager, build in CI, and assert the version at startup.
nodes.norm_label: runtime frozen at compile time (pin plus startup assertion)

nodes.label: REPORT_ecosystem — Bun ecosystem and ops research
nodes.rationale: Verdict GO-WITH-CAUTIONS: Bun is a sound stack bet because Claude Code itself is bun-compiled, but pin a proven 1.3.x and do not adopt 1.4.x until weeks of post-GA soak.
nodes.norm_label: report_ecosystem — bun ecosystem and ops research

nodes.label: Anthropic acquisition of Oven/Bun
nodes.rationale: Strengthens long-term viability because Claude Code ships as a bun-compiled binary so Anthropic must keep --compile working on Windows, but it introduces roadmap-capture risk with no foundation-governance backstop; license stayed MIT and release cadence did not slow.

nodes.label: Bun Zig-to-Rust core rewrite
nodes.rationale: About 535k lines rewritten in 11 days using 64 parallel Claude instances and 6,502 commits, motivated by recurring memory-safety bugs from Zig's manual memory management interacting with GC'd JavaScriptCore values; v1.4.0 is canary-only, so the stable channel is mid-transition and the first 1.4.x stables likely carry novel regressions.

nodes.label: LGPL-2 obligation on redistributed compiled binaries
nodes.rationale: Bun's runtime is MIT but it statically links LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore/WebKit, so publicly redistributing a compiled exe requires a relink path (oven-sh/webkit) plus attribution; local or in-team builds carry negligible exposure.
nodes.norm_label: lgpl-2 obligation on redistributed compiled binaries

nodes.label: Version-coupling risk in compiled binaries
nodes.rationale: The real failure mode of bun-compiled supervisors is not capability but coupling: opencode's binary kept exhibiting the bugs of the Bun it was built with, so every embedded-runtime bug ships until recompile. Mitigate by pinning, asserting at startup and keeping the launcher small enough to requalify fast.

nodes.label: opencode and BM2 prior art
nodes.rationale: opencode's tracker is the best field report on shipping bun-compiled CLIs (frozen runtime, metadata mis-resolution, musl-vs-glibc selection, NAPI panics), and BM2 plus pm2's Bun support show Bun.spawn is adequate for supervision workloads.

nodes.label: Windows regression rate
nodes.rationale: Windows is genuinely first-class in Bun's CI, yet it remains where regressions surface first against a 4.8k+ open-issue backdrop; the Rust rewrite targets exactly the crash/leak class that hits Windows hardest — positive medium-term, destabilizing short-term.

nodes.label: Go as launcher alternative and escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Go wins on pure binary robustness for a ~500-line launcher (reproducible builds, 2-8MB static exe, job objects via x/sys/windows, no FFI, no LGPL linkage); Bun wins on stack coherence. The 1-2 day port cost is itself the argument that betting on Bun now is low-risk.
nodes.norm_label: go as launcher alternative and escape hatch

nodes.label: Bun version policy (pin, assert, soak, never canary)
nodes.rationale: Pin 1.3.14 and never use latest; assert Bun.version at startup; treat the Rust rewrite as a new major and require two consecutive 1.4.x patches, four weeks on stable, no open P0/P1 Windows crashes and a green Windows suite before moving; bump the pin in its own PR, never alongside launcher logic.
nodes.norm_label: bun version policy (pin, assert, soak, never canary)

nodes.label: bun:ffi can drive Windows Job Objects (GO-WITH-CAUTIONS)
nodes.rationale: Empirically verified end-to-end on Bun 1.3.14 / Windows 11 x64; cautions are the experimental API label, one open FFI crash issue in compiled executables, and mandatory CREATE_SUSPENDED to close the grandchild race.
nodes.norm_label: bun:ffi can drive windows job objects (go-with-cautions)

nodes.label: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE crash guarantee
nodes.rationale: Kernel closes all handles on any termination path, so the tree is reaped even when the launcher is hard-killed; chosen over userspace cleanup because it needs no code to run at crash time.

nodes.label: Grandchild race: AssignProcessToJobObject is not retroactive
nodes.rationale: Measured: a grandchild spawned before assignment survived TerminateJobObject. Windows only auto-associates processes created while the parent is already in the job.
nodes.norm_label: grandchild race: assignprocesstojobobject is not retroactive

nodes.label: CREATE_SUSPENDED spawn-then-assign-then-resume pattern
nodes.rationale: Closes the grandchild race entirely inside bun:ffi by assigning the job before the initial thread runs; costs Bun.spawn's stdio piping and exited promise.

nodes.label: PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST (no-race alternative)
nodes.rationale: Windows 10 1607+ assigns the job before the initial thread runs with no race window at all; not tested because CREATE_SUSPENDED already suffices.

nodes.label: Launcher-in-umbrella-job alternative
nodes.rationale: Putting the launcher itself in the job first makes children inherit membership atomically, keeping Bun.spawn's plumbing; trade-off is that a tree kill also kills the launcher.

nodes.label: Bun issue #31941 — FFI trampoline segfault in standalone exes
nodes.rationale: The single NO-GO tripwire: sustained 100ms-interval FFI polling from a bun build --compile binary crashes; mitigation is event-driven, low-frequency FFI calls.
nodes.norm_label: bun issue #31941 — ffi trampoline segfault in standalone exes

nodes.label: bigint handle discipline (u64 returns are bigint, not number)
nodes.rationale: Docs imply number returns but measurement shows bigint; typing all handle plumbing as bigint plus a typeof smoke assert absorbs the doc/behaviour drift.
nodes.norm_label: bigint handle discipline (u64 returns are bigint, not number)

nodes.label: Kilo-Org/kilocode windows-job.ts prior art
nodes.rationale: The only found production bun:ffi Job Object implementation; its existence turns ~120 lines of first-party FFI from a gamble into a tractable port.

nodes.label: taskkill /T /F process-tree enumeration race
nodes.rationale: The npm ecosystem standard (tree-kill and family) kills a snapshot, so a process spawned between snapshot and kill escapes; not crash-safe and no kill-on-close guarantee.

nodes.label: FFI fallback ladder: bun:ffi to N-API addon to Go
nodes.rationale: koffi under Bun is unverified and ffi-napi is effectively dead, so the realistic ladder is bun:ffi, then a ~50-line prebuilt N-API addon, then Go's x/sys/windows.
nodes.norm_label: ffi fallback ladder: bun:ffi to n-api addon to go

nodes.label: Bun.spawn as the child-spawn layer (GO-WITH-CAUTIONS)
nodes.rationale: Acceptable for vendor CLIs because timeout/killSignal/maxBuffer/AbortSignal are built in, but tree kill, graceful stop and race-free job assignment must all come from outside it.

nodes.label: libuv uv_spawn as Bun's Windows process substrate
nodes.rationale: Because Bun delegates to uv_spawn, libuv's Windows process model — not Bun's docs — is the ground truth for kill, detach and exit-code behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: libuv uv_spawn as bun's windows process substrate

nodes.label: Tree-kill gap: .kill() terminates the direct child only
nodes.rationale: Highest-severity risk: vendor CLIs are trees (npm shim to node to ...), so timeouts leak grandchildren holding pipes and ports unless the launcher owns a Job Object.
nodes.norm_label: tree-kill gap: .kill() terminates the direct child only

nodes.label: libuv's implicit job with SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK
nodes.rationale: Easy to miss: libuv already puts non-detached children in a kill-on-job-close job, but silent breakaway means the guarantee is depth-1 only.

nodes.label: CTRL_BREAK graceful-shutdown channel has no Bun built-in
nodes.rationale: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent needs a shared console plus CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, a combination Bun.spawn cannot produce because detached also strips the console; so polite-stop needs FFI CreateProcessW or hard-kill-only.
nodes.norm_label: ctrl_break graceful-shutdown channel has no bun built-in

nodes.label: CREATE_SUSPENDED and raw creation flags absent from SpawnOptions
nodes.rationale: Confirmed by absence across the whole reference interface; libuv exposes no arbitrary dwCreationFlags, so race-free job assignment must leave Bun.spawn entirely.
nodes.norm_label: create_suspended and raw creation flags absent from spawnoptions

nodes.label: Streaming stdout/stderr byte counting for heartbeats
nodes.rationale: Pull-based ReadableStream reads give per-chunk byte counts without whole-output buffering; stderr defaults to inherit so it must be explicitly piped to be counted.
nodes.norm_label: streaming stdout/stderr byte counting for heartbeats

nodes.label: Bun issue #15564 — garbled piped stderr on Windows
nodes.rationale: Corruption appears when stderr is piped but stdout is not; mitigation is to always pipe both together, which the launcher does anyway.
nodes.norm_label: bun issue #15564 — garbled piped stderr on windows

nodes.label: Bun issue #24690 — empty spawn stdout inside bun test
nodes.rationale: Directly threatens spawn-integration unit tests, so mock the spawn layer in bun test and run real-spawn smoke tests as standalone scripts instead.
nodes.norm_label: bun issue #24690 — empty spawn stdout inside bun test

nodes.label: Bun issue #33020 — async-iterable stdin hang on Windows
nodes.rationale: The stream pump promise never settles so the parent never exits; feed stdin via FileSink writes rather than an async iterable.
nodes.norm_label: bun issue #33020 — async-iterable stdin hang on windows

nodes.label: Bun Shell ($) maturity on Windows
nodes.rationale: Its own cross-platform interpreter is fine for short harness scripts, but it has no kill and no job control, so it is unusable for long-running supervised processes.

nodes.label: bun test adequacy: JUnit reporter and fake timers
nodes.rationale: JUnit output, --bail, per-test timeouts and jest-compatible fake timers cover heartbeat/timeout logic; TAP is unsupported and the fake timers are only months old.
nodes.norm_label: bun test adequacy: junit reporter and fake timers

nodes.label: NTSTATUS exit-code fidelity through libuv
nodes.rationale: libuv passes the full 32-bit DWORD so truncation is unlikely, but unverified at the Bun layer; log the raw code and treat values above 255 as abnormal Windows termination.

nodes.label: Four-bucket defect classification (A/B/C/D)
nodes.rationale: Buckets are mutually exclusive and a row earns A only where prevention follows from a verified Unison mechanism and requires more than rewriting the same shell predicate in Unison.

nodes.label: Bucket-A share is 3 of 97 defects (3.09%) as an upper bound
nodes.rationale: All three A rows require rehoming shared state into STM or transactional storage; a transliteration that still coordinates through files, Git and shell prevents 0 of 97 by language choice alone.
nodes.norm_label: bucket-a share is 3 of 97 defects (3.09%) as an upper bound

nodes.label: Unison abilities and handlers as effect isolation
nodes.rationale: Effects appear in function types and can be swapped for deterministic handlers, which reduces mock drift — but no handler makes a shell, filesystem, process or Git action transactional.
nodes.norm_label: unison abilities and handlers as effect isolation

nodes.label: Unison base STM.atomically
nodes.rationale: Covers contenders only when their state is centralized in one Unison runtime; multi-process coordination needs a shared transactional service, which is an infrastructure redesign not a free language property.

nodes.label: Unison Cloud typed transactional storage
nodes.rationale: Could give an atomic shared-state backend for multi-process contenders, but it is not demonstrated as a property of local Unison programs or arbitrary filesystem operations.

nodes.label: Content-addressed deployments protect identity, not evidence
nodes.rationale: Code-derived deployment hashes secure version identity and rollback but authenticate no vendor log, Git snapshot, audit file or caller-supplied inventory row.
nodes.norm_label: content-addressed deployments protect identity, not evidence

nodes.label: Bucket A: check-then-act mkdir mutex admits double winners
nodes.rationale: Moving lock state into an atomic transactional operation eliminates the split check/create interleaving rather than testing for it afterwards.
nodes.norm_label: bucket a: check-then-act mkdir mutex admits double winners

nodes.label: Bucket A: loser overwrites the winner's owner token
nodes.rationale: A transactional compare-and-set of {owner, held} plus owner-checked release makes publication and release one atomic transition; possibly a downstream double-count of the mkdir race.
nodes.norm_label: bucket a: loser overwrites the winner's owner token

nodes.label: Bucket A: compaction read/modify/rename races an append
nodes.rationale: One transactional store serializes or retries the conflicting update instead of hiding it behind separate file operations; content-addressed deployments do not help.
nodes.norm_label: bucket a: compaction read/modify/rename races an append

nodes.label: Cheaper intervention 1: make success artifact-bound
nodes.rationale: Per-attempt ids, freshness, declared deliverable sets, content hashes and nonzero failure aggregation; never accept a vendor exit code or self-report alone.

nodes.label: Cheaper intervention 2: independent negative controls
nodes.rationale: Mutation-test every checker and exercise zero denominators, stale artifacts, wrong paths, missing inputs and real backends rather than only shims.

nodes.label: Cheaper intervention 3: a directly owned supervisor
nodes.rationale: Launch vendors directly, persist findings incrementally, tag and register every process, define completion by artifacts, and supervise trees outside the agent turn.
nodes.norm_label: cheaper intervention 3: a directly owned supervisor

nodes.label: Cheaper intervention 5: harden platform adapters
nodes.rationale: Real files instead of nested heredocs, argv-safe launchers, pinned and preflighted vendor CLIs, explicit Windows/WSL path domains, and real-daemon integration checks.

nodes.label: Extract only the typed decision core
nodes.rationale: A small typed state/evidence module behind the existing shell adapters captures most readability and testability benefit without porting ~8,800 lines of OS-facing orchestration.
nodes.norm_label: extract only the typed decision core

nodes.label: Do-not-port position: the mismatch is structural, not scheduling
nodes.rationale: Foreman's entire purpose is the part of the OS that Unison deliberately abstracts away, so the argument does not improve with time.
nodes.norm_label: do-not-port position: the mismatch is structural, not scheduling

nodes.label: Unison's complete process-control API is five builtins
nodes.rationale: Measured from Builtin.hs rather than marketing pages: one handle, one process, no process groups, no setsid, no namespaces, no Job Objects, no choice of signal.
nodes.norm_label: unison's complete process-control api is five builtins

nodes.label: Unison has no signal API at all
nodes.rationale: Zero builtin matches for signal handling against 47 load-bearing traps, so a Unison Foreman interrupted at the terminal leaves worktrees, locks and the lane registry as they were — disqualifying on its own.
nodes.norm_label: unison has no signal api at all

nodes.label: No setEnv, no per-child env or cwd on process.start
nodes.rationale: Foreman's entire isolation model is environment-scoped across 169 variables, and getEnv exists while setEnv does not, so per-lane vendor isolation cannot be expressed.
nodes.norm_label: no setenv, no per-child env or cwd on process.start

nodes.label: Process-global setCurrentDirectory is a data race under real concurrency
nodes.rationale: N lanes in N worktrees would mutate one global cwd from N threads — a race in the one piece of state that decides which repository a worker edits.
nodes.norm_label: process-global setcurrentdirectory is a data race under real concurrency

nodes.label: Liveness diagnosis needs /proc state and CPU time
nodes.rationale: Unison's exitCode returns None for running, stopped, network-blocked and wedged alike, and 'still running' is the most dangerous status; Windows additionally needs /proc/<pid>/winpid.
nodes.norm_label: liveness diagnosis needs /proc state and cpu time

nodes.label: No chmod, umask, symlink, exec-bit or flock in Unison IO
nodes.rationale: The release's largest workstream exists because mkdir atomicity failed and flock was measured as the replacement, so a Unison port would ship it by shelling out to flock(1).
nodes.norm_label: no chmod, umask, symlink, exec-bit or flock in unison io

nodes.label: Git is not typed by rewriting the caller
nodes.rationale: The porcelain-collapse bug was well-typed text that was semantically wrong about the world; the fix was -uall plus a content hash, identical in bash and in Unison.
nodes.norm_label: git is not typed by rewriting the caller

nodes.label: A port adds shell-quoting seams rather than removing bash
nodes.rationale: The practical escape hatch is process.call bash -lc, so the port layers above bash and moves every argument through the exact boundary that cost four incidents in one session.
nodes.norm_label: a port adds shell-quoting seams rather than removing bash

nodes.label: Score: 0 of 12 checker defects cleanly prevented
nodes.rationale: Eleven are wrong predicates, vacuous truths, stale artifacts or wrong thresholds; the one partial is a Python library-semantics defect the orchestrator port does not touch.
nodes.norm_label: score: 0 of 12 checker defects cleanly prevented

nodes.label: Score: 0 of 8 strandings prevented, two strictly worse
nodes.rationale: The SIGTTIN suspension and the pgrep watchdog cases needed OS visibility Unison does not expose, and every stranding was caught by an out-of-band filesystem or process check.
nodes.norm_label: score: 0 of 8 strandings prevented, two strictly worse

nodes.label: v0.2.5 four-lens pre-implementation plan audit
nodes.rationale: Four read-only lanes ran in parallel under the Fable architect and none ran bats, per the gate-mutex doctrine; amendments were folded into the plan documents themselves.

nodes.label: Environment actions taken during the audit (Bun 1.3.14, pueue 4.0.4)
nodes.rationale: Bun installed via winget which does not self-pin, so tool-check must verify the exact version; pueue binaries were staged by hand because no package-manager route exists.
nodes.norm_label: environment actions taken during the audit (bun 1.3.14, pueue 4.0.4)

nodes.label: Plan-versus-shipped drift audit (v0.2.5 plan vs v0.2.0 main)
nodes.rationale: The plan was frozen one day before the durable-lanes rework landed, so it repeatedly treats already-shipped work as still-to-do; re-implementing audited fixes is pure regression risk.
nodes.norm_label: plan-versus-shipped drift audit (v0.2.5 plan vs v0.2.0 main)

nodes.label: Config loader is a closed allowlist, so new keys silently no-op
nodes.rationale: Every new key must be added to both the parse case and the env-var table, and new thresholds belong in the existing [durable] namespace rather than a parallel [freshness] home.
nodes.norm_label: config loader is a closed allowlist, so new keys silently no-op

nodes.label: checkpoint versus commit field collision in event schema v2
nodes.rationale: resume.sh reads .commit or .payload.checkpoint but never a top-level .checkpoint, so the 'additive' schema would silently drop checkpoint recovery — a real breakage, not an addition.
nodes.norm_label: checkpoint versus commit field collision in event schema v2

nodes.label: Round B lane-run and watch fixes were already shipped
nodes.rationale: All four lane-run and all three watch fixes are on main with citations, so the tasks must be rescoped to the genuinely new work instead of re-running audited code.
nodes.norm_label: round b lane-run and watch fixes were already shipped

nodes.label: foreman-launch insertion is a contract change, not a drop-in
nodes.rationale: cmd_pid would capture the launcher, rc would carry launcher codes 124/125, the taskkill sweep becomes redundant against KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, and /dev/null stdin forwarding is unspecified.
nodes.norm_label: foreman-launch insertion is a contract change, not a drop-in

nodes.label: PIPE_BUF is a non-issue; el_compact atomicity is the real constraint
nodes.rationale: The seq lock serializes the whole read-modify-append so appends cannot tear, but el_read halts at the first malformed line, so compaction lines must be written tmp-plus-rename.
nodes.norm_label: pipe_buf is a non-issue; el_compact atomicity is the real constraint

nodes.label: Integer line-number cursor must survive attempt/checkpoint replay
nodes.rationale: nats-bridge depends on the integer cursor, so any attempt or checkpoint dimension must be layered without changing it.
nodes.norm_label: integer line-number cursor must survive attempt/checkpoint replay

nodes.label: wt-merge aborts when report paths are named in any pathspec
nodes.rationale: The shipped code already uses the exclude-pathspec candidate and still aborts, so the fix must stop naming reports at both sites and the bats case needs a genuinely gitignored tree.
nodes.norm_label: wt-merge aborts when report paths are named in any pathspec

nodes.label: Background-and-stop attractor (12 occurrences)
nodes.rationale: Nine of twelve occurrences land in the finish/verify/report phase, which no planned primitive owns, so prompt discipline demonstrably fails and typed state only names the loss.

nodes.label: Prevention tally: 0 impossible, 5 detected-only, 7 unchanged
nodes.rationale: The plan detects the attractor but prevents lost work only in the implement phase; the single clean win is the Job Object reaping an unreaped vendor subprocess.

nodes.label: Amendment A: lane-run owns the whole round under the pueue daemon
nodes.rationale: Making the supervised tree equal the whole round and its owner the daemon means an agent that backgrounds and stops cannot strand it; --post and a naked foreground round-script were both rejected.
nodes.norm_label: amendment a: lane-run owns the whole round under the pueue daemon

nodes.label: --detach: the one-flag launcher contract delta
nodes.rationale: Re-parents the supervisor off the caller's console and returns before the round completes, so the round survives the caller ending its turn; the degrade path when pueue is absent.

nodes.label: Amendment B: bounded auto-resume supervisor (Task 8)
nodes.rationale: The resume owner must be the one process guaranteed not to be an agent turn; it owns no new state, classifies ABANDONED from existing evidence, and stops at max_attempts.

nodes.label: Amendment C: attempt-fresh terminal predicate
nodes.rationale: 'Report exists' is satisfiable by a stale prior-round report, and CLI exit is not round completion, so round_done requires whole-round-script exit plus an attempt-fresh artifact.

nodes.label: AGENT-ABANDONED as a first-class alertable state
nodes.rationale: Child exit confirmed with no round_done and no attempt-fresh report must never classify SUCCEEDED and never read as a silent false stall during the gate phase.
nodes.norm_label: agent-abandoned as a first-class alertable state

nodes.label: Success criteria SC-A through SC-F make prevention testable
nodes.rationale: The plan's five criteria never exercise an agent stopping in the finish phase; SC-A agent-stop survivability and SC-B whole-round ownership are the load-bearing pair that fails today.
nodes.norm_label: success criteria sc-a through sc-f make prevention testable

nodes.label: Bun 1.3.14 pinned install paths (winget or install.ps1 -Version)
nodes.rationale: winget has the exact version but does not enforce the pin afterwards, so tool-check must assert the exact version at runtime; project-level pinning uses .bun-version plus packageManager.
nodes.norm_label: bun 1.3.14 pinned install paths (winget or install.ps1 -version)

nodes.label: pueue 4.0.4 has no package-manager route on this host
nodes.rationale: GitHub release binaries are the only route, making pueue the repo's first raw-download tool and requiring a new DownloadBinary-style bootstrap helper.
nodes.norm_label: pueue 4.0.4 has no package-manager route on this host

nodes.label: pueued Windows autostart is undocumented upstream
nodes.rationale: The only shipped service unit is Linux-only, so a doctrine decision between Scheduled Task, Startup shortcut or lazy client autospawn is needed plus one empirical check.
nodes.norm_label: pueued windows autostart is undocumented upstream

nodes.label: No exact-version-pin mechanism in the reference manifest
nodes.rationale: Only min_version threshold compares exist and each tool has a hand-written branch in both check scripts, so 'assert exactly 1.3.14' needs a new pin_version field or bespoke logic.
nodes.norm_label: no exact-version-pin mechanism in the reference manifest

nodes.label: CI build/sign/publish pipeline is entirely greenfield
nodes.rationale: Only a reporting maintenance workflow exists; the build must run on windows-latest because cross-compiled bytecode segfaults, and no code-signing certificate plan exists anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: ci build/sign/publish pipeline is entirely greenfield

nodes.label: Nine research caveats omitted from the plan's Global Constraints
nodes.rationale: None blocks Task 1 code, but the compiled-exe env-var stripping, idle RSS drift, autoload determinism flags and last-handle caveat all bite the launcher's actual shape.
nodes.norm_label: nine research caveats omitted from the plan's global constraints

nodes.label: reference-manifest.toml is not parsed generically
nodes.rationale: Each tool id has a hand-written branch in tool-check.ps1 and tool-check.sh, so adding manifest entries is necessary but not sufficient.

nodes.label: T-INFRA gate-speed foundation must run first
nodes.rationale: Without it the gate re-enters the ~40-minute regime that caused the v0.2.0 force-merge; highest leverage and lowest cost of any change in the plan.
nodes.norm_label: t-infra gate-speed foundation must run first

nodes.label: WATCH_VTICK injectable clock must land before typed states
nodes.rationale: Phase-aware thresholds cannot be integration-tested on a wall clock, and retrofitting the clock onto a 10-state machine repeats the documented multi-layer rabbit hole on a larger surface.
nodes.norm_label: watch_vtick injectable clock must land before typed states

nodes.label: slow/fast test tagging plus inline-setup consolidation
nodes.rationale: Wall-clock minutes grow faster than test count because new tests land in timing-sensitive files; tagging keeps the inner loop single-digit minutes and the merge gate 10-15 minutes.
nodes.norm_label: slow/fast test tagging plus inline-setup consolidation

nodes.label: Host-wide gate pueue group (parallel=1) as a structural bats mutex
nodes.rationale: Turns 'serialize the gates' from human discipline into structure and makes the auditors' do-not-run-bats rule fail-safe rather than discipline-dependent.
nodes.norm_label: host-wide gate pueue group (parallel=1) as a structural bats mutex

nodes.label: .gitattributes CRLF fix moved from last to first
nodes.rationale: lane-run.sh is CRLF and .gitattributes is absent, so leaving the fix in the last task means every WSL lane fights pipefail\r for the whole release.
nodes.norm_label: .gitattributes crlf fix moved from last to first

nodes.label: T5 split: plumbing now, real-grok verdict deferred
nodes.rationale: The grok CLI is missing on the host, so queue serialization is provable with a PATH shim while only the real-vendor verdict must wait; do not gate T5 completion on grok.
nodes.norm_label: t5 split: plumbing now, real-grok verdict deferred

nodes.label: FORCE_MISSING shim pattern makes both branches deterministic
nodes.rationale: The docs-check precedent is already live, so present-pueue and absent-pueue paths can both be tested; since pueue was missing at audit time the shim is mandatory to cover enqueue at all.
nodes.norm_label: force_missing shim pattern makes both branches deterministic

nodes.label: Windows kill-shot test must use heartbeat winpid plus taskkill
nodes.rationale: kill -9 is POSIX phrasing; MSYS kill targets the wrapper pid and MSYS ps cannot see native grandchildren, so the criterion must be stated per build.
nodes.norm_label: windows kill-shot test must use heartbeat winpid plus taskkill

nodes.label: POSIX launcher subsumes group_timeout for v0.3.0
nodes.rationale: Same setsid plus kill-by-pgid contract, so it supplies the outer watchdog layer the v0.3.0 review flagged missing — but WSL2 exercises the less-tested POSIX build, so add a POSIX kill-shot test.
nodes.norm_label: posix launcher subsumes group_timeout for v0.3.0

nodes.label: v0.3.0 session-transport series audit: BLOCKED for direct merge
nodes.rationale: No critical security bugs; the blockers are process/acceptance and repo topology, not code quality — the spec's own live demo was never run and main diverged from the architecture the series extends.
nodes.norm_label: v0.3.0 session-transport series audit: blocked for direct merge

nodes.label: Foundational architecture mismatch with main (adapters layer gone)
nodes.rationale: main stubbed hard-mode worker-run.sh and rewrote audit-run.sh to call codex inline with no adapters directory, so a patch-level merge would resurrect a deliberately deprecated path and create two incompatible audit code paths.
nodes.norm_label: foundational architecture mismatch with main (adapters layer gone)

nodes.label: Task 11 live acceptance demo was never executed
nodes.rationale: Because decision D6 made a live demo the sole acceptance mechanism, skipping it means the real codex mcp-server tool and property names are carried from spec assumption; it fails closed, so it is a safe failure but shipped as verified-complete.
nodes.norm_label: task 11 live acceptance demo was never executed

nodes.label: mcp-session.py fail-closed JSON-RPC parsing
nodes.rationale: Non-dict JSON, unexpected ids and server-to-client requests are handled explicitly rather than crashing or silently dropping, and killpg runs unconditionally in the finally block.

nodes.label: enforce_mcp_decorrelation fail-open closure
nodes.rationale: An orchestrator model-family value never equalling any vendor family string silently passed the check; closed with an explicit allow-list, layered on top of the unconditional harness-name check rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: group_timeout process-leak fixes (INT/TERM traps, watchdog sleep reaping)
nodes.rationale: Both fixes are real, narrowly scoped and justified in the commit message; they cover the setsid group and the watchdog's own sleep child.
nodes.norm_label: group_timeout process-leak fixes (int/term traps, watchdog sleep reaping)

nodes.label: Banner-tolerant session-id extraction
nodes.rationale: A lenient jq fromjson filter stops a non-JSON banner line aborting the extraction pipeline and silently disabling resume.

nodes.label: mcp-mode timeout enforcement is single-layered
nodes.rationale: Container mode wraps docker in an outer timeout; mcp mode delegates entirely to the adapter, matching the interface contract but leaving no second layer if group_timeout's own wait ever hangs.

nodes.label: Zero committed automated coverage for ~1900 new lines
nodes.rationale: Spec-authorized under D6 and offset by careful per-task manual verification, but manual non-committed verification leaves no regression guard for the JSON-RPC handling or the adapter contract.
nodes.norm_label: zero committed automated coverage for ~1900 new lines

nodes.label: Content-diff re-port merge strategy (never cherry-pick)
nodes.rationale: The branches share filenames but not structure or intent; the architect must first decide hard-mode revival versus soft-mode port, because that changes the whole porting plan. Docs port cleanly and go first.

nodes.label: Tiered audit: medium-effort screen routing to high-effort deep
nodes.rationale: Biggest lever on median wall-clock so mechanical diffs never pay the 27-minute tax; false-negative risk is bounded by always-deep categories plus shadow sampling that measures recall rather than assuming it.
nodes.norm_label: tiered audit: medium-effort screen routing to high-effort deep

nodes.label: audit-screen.sh hunk risk classifier (recall-biased)
nodes.rationale: A screen tier's job is recall, not precision, so it escalates liberally into mechanical/logic/security_sensitive/cross_cutting classes with an escalate hunk-id list.

nodes.label: Non-overridable always-deep floor in code
nodes.rationale: Config may add paths and categories but never subtract, and the floor includes the audit tooling's own scripts because a bug in the auditor defeats every future audit.

nodes.label: Sharded audit with a mandatory whole-diff structural pass
nodes.rationale: Sharding provably loses cross-file findings, so the cheap signature-only structural pass is non-optional; below the file threshold spawn overhead dominates so sharding no-ops.
nodes.norm_label: sharded audit with a mandatory whole-diff structural pass

nodes.label: Consolidation stays a real model call, not a set union
nodes.rationale: A pure union cannot judge severity interaction across shards — two low-severity findings in different files can compose into a high-severity issue — so consolidation must exercise judgement.
nodes.norm_label: consolidation stays a real model call, not a set union

nodes.label: Hunk-hash cache shared by scoped re-audit and stream tier
nodes.rationale: One staleness mechanism instead of two; the hunk id includes surrounding context to reduce false-identical hits, ttl_days bounds age, and security-sensitive findings are never cached.
nodes.norm_label: hunk-hash cache shared by scoped re-audit and stream tier

nodes.label: Incremental checkpoint-stream audit during implementation
nodes.rationale: Converts latency from serial-after to overlapped-during — the flagship win — but must fail soft to end-of-round audit when the durable-lanes primitives are absent, never blocking a merge.

nodes.label: AUDIT_BUNDLE pre-packaging so the auditor spends no turns on recon
nodes.rationale: Directly attacks the recon-time hypothesis and extends prompt assembly that already exists in miniature; the graphify section is best-effort and never fails the bundle build.
nodes.norm_label: audit_bundle pre-packaging so the auditor spends no turns on recon

nodes.label: lib/audit-call.sh centralizes the cross-vendor check and mutation guard
nodes.rationale: Every tier calls the same code path so no per-entrypoint reimplementation can drift; a screen or shard script with a slightly different check could otherwise allow same-vendor audit on one path only.
nodes.norm_label: lib/audit-call.sh centralizes the cross-vendor check and mutation guard

nodes.label: verdict.schema.v2.json additive and versioned
nodes.rationale: schema_version lets gate-eval branch cleanly while v1 files keep working untouched, so there is no forced migration mid-release.

nodes.label: [audit.routing] risk-class to vendor/model/effort/scope table
nodes.rationale: Config-driven rather than hardcoded, read with the existing nested-table toml_get helper so no new TOML parser is needed; the always-deep floor always wins over routing.

nodes.label: Audit-side session-transport interface (mirror, not reimplementation)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the existing worker session contract so a round-2 re-audit reuses a warm thread; the thread is bound to (task_id, worker_vendor, audit_vendor) and fails closed to a cold start on mismatch.

nodes.label: Per-tier timing telemetry and before/after audit metrics
nodes.rationale: All timings derive from new event-type strings on the existing eventlog primitive, so legacy runs simply report n/a rather than erroring; enables a legacy-vs-tiered comparison on one task lineage.
nodes.norm_label: per-tier timing telemetry and before/after audit metrics

nodes.label: gate-eval fails closed when a mandated deep pass did not run
nodes.rationale: A screen-tier APPROVED can never silently stand in for a mandated deep pass; audit-meta.json records exactly which tiers ran so coverage is checkable.
nodes.norm_label: gate-eval fails closed when a mandated deep pass did not run

nodes.label: Risk: screen-tier false negatives ship a real defect
nodes.rationale: Mitigated by the hardcoded floor plus a recall-biased prompt, and measured rather than assumed via shadow full-deep sampling feeding back into the floor list over time.
nodes.norm_label: risk: screen-tier false negatives ship a real defect

nodes.label: Shadow full-deep sampling as an empirical recall proxy
nodes.rationale: Roughly one in ten screen-only APPROVED diffs get a shadow deep pass purely for measurement, which is the empirical justification required before flipping the default mode.
nodes.norm_label: shadow full-deep sampling as an empirical recall proxy

nodes.label: Reasoning effort is the single biggest latency dial
nodes.rationale: Reasoning tokens are output tokens and output count is roughly linear with latency; xhigh buys about two intelligence-index points over high at ~40s time-to-first-token versus a 2.6s tier median.
nodes.norm_label: reasoning effort is the single biggest latency dial

nodes.label: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna tiers and the effort ladder
nodes.rationale: max and ultra appear in launch coverage but not the Codex config reference, whose ceiling is xhigh, so their CLI availability is treated as unverified.
nodes.norm_label: gpt-5.6 sol/terra/luna tiers and the effort ladder

nodes.label: codex exec versus codex mcp-server thread reuse
nodes.rationale: No published startup-overhead number exists, but codex-reply avoids re-spawning the agent and re-exploring the repo; separate exec runs can still hit the server-side prefix cache.
nodes.norm_label: codex exec versus codex mcp-server thread reuse

nodes.label: GPT-5.6 guaranteed 30-minute prompt-prefix cache
nodes.rationale: Byte-stable audit preambles above 1024 tokens get cheap prefill across separate exec runs, but input-side cuts are only 1-5% of latency so the real win is avoided re-exploration turns.

nodes.label: Shard-and-consolidate is the dominant published review pattern
nodes.rationale: Claude Code PR review, a 9-agent per-dimension setup and commercial reviewers all converge on parallel agents plus one consolidation phase that dedupes, ranks and filters.
nodes.norm_label: shard-and-consolidate is the dominant published review pattern

nodes.label: Parallel breadth raises recall and false positives together
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks show roughly 5x false-positive inflation without a consolidation/verification stage, so consolidation is what protects precision rather than an optional tidy-up.
nodes.norm_label: parallel breadth raises recall and false positives together

nodes.label: Output tokens dominate latency; prompt size barely matters
nodes.rationale: Cutting half the output may halve latency while cutting half the prompt yields 1-5%, which is why effort level and terse schema-forced output outrank context trimming.
nodes.norm_label: output tokens dominate latency; prompt size barely matters

nodes.label: TraceLab: ~19% residual harness overhead over 253k Codex tool calls
nodes.rationale: Average 1.11s per call with an approval-dominated tail to 10s+, so a read-only sandbox with no approvals plus fewer tool calls cuts real seconds; the larger win is avoided model turns.
nodes.norm_label: tracelab: ~19% residual harness overhead over 253k codex tool calls

nodes.label: codex exec --output-schema forces a schema-valid verdict
nodes.rationale: Fits Foreman's verdict schema directly and also works on resume; neither Grok CLI nor Gemini CLI has an equivalent, so third vendors need post-validation.
nodes.norm_label: codex exec --output-schema forces a schema-valid verdict

nodes.label: Grok CLI headless as a third audit vendor
nodes.rationale: Named headless sessions, an --effort flag and per-session cost reporting exist, but the JSON output format is an envelope not a user-schema-forced verdict; adds independence, not speed.
nodes.norm_label: grok cli headless as a third audit vendor

nodes.label: Gemini CLI as auditor: no documented thinking-level flag
nodes.rationale: Headless JSON and stream-json exist and the model must be pinned rather than trusting the auto-router, but thinking level is API-only and schema forcing is absent.
nodes.norm_label: gemini cli as auditor: no documented thinking-level flag

nodes.label: Sanity math: levers 1 and 2 give a credible 4-6x to 5-9 minutes
nodes.rationale: No single lever reaches the sub-10-minute target alone; effort reduction plus parallel shard-and-consolidate are the core, with turn-count and output-token cuts on top.
nodes.norm_label: sanity math: levers 1 and 2 give a credible 4-6x to 5-9 minutes

nodes.label: Executive lever ranking for cutting the audit pass
nodes.rationale: Effort reduction and parallel shard/consolidate rank highest on impact times confidence; --ephemeral and third-vendor lanes rank lowest.
nodes.norm_label: executive lever ranking for cutting the audit pass

nodes.label: Kill agentic exploration: pre-package so the auditor makes ~0 tool calls
nodes.rationale: Each tool call is a full model turn, so converting an N-turn loop into one turn is the unquantified but mechanically sound win; read-only plus never-approve removes the approval residual entirely.
nodes.norm_label: kill agentic exploration: pre-package so the auditor makes ~0 tool calls

nodes.label: Third vendors are viable for independence but weaker on schema
nodes.rationale: Neither Grok Build nor Gemini CLI offers Codex-style schema-forced final output, so use them for independence and racing rather than for speed.
nodes.norm_label: third vendors are viable for independence but weaker on schema

nodes.label: Foreman audit pipeline end-to-end map
nodes.rationale: audit-run.sh for hard mode and the codex-auditor agent for soft mode, with evidence collected upfront and a schema-forced verdict returned inside a 600s bound.

nodes.label: Asymmetric effort: implementer optimized, auditor left at high
nodes.rationale: The codex implementer was pinned to medium in a specific commit while the auditor stayed high across all versions, so the auditor always consumes the full timeout.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric effort: implementer optimized, auditor left at high

nodes.label: Highest latency hypothesis: serial single-shot audit on the full diff
nodes.rationale: Cost is order diff-size plus reasoning depth every round with no incremental scoping; mitigation is tagging changed findings and replaying only what changed.
nodes.norm_label: highest latency hypothesis: serial single-shot audit on the full diff

nodes.label: Session startup overhead per round (fixed on dev-v1)
nodes.rationale: 10-30 seconds per round times N rounds, already addressed by the MCP threadId persistence shipped on the dev branch.
nodes.norm_label: session startup overhead per round (fixed on dev-v1)

nodes.label: Event log and git checkpoints unused by the audit path
nodes.rationale: Both primitives exist but no audit consumer reads them, which is what makes an overlapped checkpoint-consuming audit lane an unclaimed opportunity.
nodes.norm_label: event log and git checkpoints unused by the audit path

nodes.label: Graphify graph is committed but never injected into the audit prompt
nodes.rationale: The auditor re-derives architecture each round; injecting a graph summary is a UX and context win largely orthogonal to raw latency.
nodes.norm_label: graphify graph is committed but never injected into the audit prompt

nodes.label: 600-second audit timeout ceiling
