nodes.rationale: Bounds a single audit invocation and raises the open question of checkpoint recovery when the timeout fires mid-analysis.

nodes.label: v0.2.9 infrastructure OpenSpec audit: BLOCKED
nodes.rationale: The eight packages are structurally valid but several gates use predicates that do not establish their claims, so a competent implementer would have to invent security-critical semantics; strict validation passing addresses none of it.

nodes.label: Audit freshness bound only to diff_sha256, not attempt or tree
nodes.rationale: An interrupted same-diff re-audit leaves a prior APPROVED gate-valid, and a rebase can produce a byte-identical patch over a different tree; the formal model abstracts this away so it cannot falsify the real predicate.
nodes.norm_label: audit freshness bound only to diff_sha256, not attempt or tree

nodes.label: git status --porcelain digest is an unsound write-evidence predicate
nodes.rationale: It does not change when an already-dirty file is edited again, yet a bare report skeleton satisfies it; the package about evidence fidelity uses a predicate that does not entail its claim, and it has two owners.
nodes.norm_label: git status --porcelain digest is an unsound write-evidence predicate

nodes.label: One workspace-change predicate imposed on all four lane types
nodes.rationale: A correct read-only auditor writes outside the reviewed worktree so its digest should not change, while touching one of four planning files ends the loop on an incomplete package.
nodes.norm_label: one workspace-change predicate imposed on all four lane types

nodes.label: round-ownership-default refuses and permits the same state
nodes.rationale: An unconditional refusal plus an unnamed escape hatch lets different implementers produce opposite compliant behaviours; the DURABLE_ENABLED 'exactly two occurrences' premise can also self-stop the first task.
nodes.norm_label: round-ownership-default refuses and permits the same state

nodes.label: Lock fallback never consumes the atomicity evidence it requires
nodes.rationale: The probe lands only in host inventory, so a host can be declared not ready and still run the helper fail-open on the known non-atomic primitive — the exact defect the amendment was ordered to close.
nodes.norm_label: lock fallback never consumes the atomicity evidence it requires

nodes.label: Lock nesting and reclamation contracts are contradictory or unsafe
nodes.rationale: The spec forbids holding one lock while acquiring another and then orders nesting; delegating bridge recovery to global init can delete live locks, and .index.lock has no reclamation task.
nodes.norm_label: lock nesting and reclamation contracts are contradictory or unsafe

nodes.label: Metric M5 has two definitions and two owners
nodes.rationale: Different populations, comparators and denominators under one identifier means the same release can report two incompatible M5 values and no implementer can know which schema is authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: metric m5 has two definitions and two owners

nodes.label: Metrics not computable from their declared dependencies
nodes.rationale: A mutually-exclusive-and-exhaustive phase set with a fifth phase added, an authorship share with no authorship event, and five metrics with no zero-denominator behaviour force the generator to invent semantics.
nodes.norm_label: metrics not computable from their declared dependencies

nodes.label: Regression Tier 0 and Tier 1 acceptance are unfalsifiable
nodes.rationale: 'Materially larger than normal noise' has no statistic, and covering every failure class in the bug log with 10-12 vendor-transcript cases is impossible because most classes are not vendor responses.
nodes.norm_label: regression tier 0 and tier 1 acceptance are unfalsifiable

nodes.label: Tier budgets and statistical gates are not executable
nodes.rationale: A confidence interval over three paid external runs is not a defensible regression threshold and a pinned model name does not pin a changing vendor backend, so Tier 2 should be on-demand research.
nodes.norm_label: tier budgets and statistical gates are not executable

nodes.label: Formal manifest cannot encode its own required rows
nodes.rationale: The outcome vocabulary is VIOLATED/HOLDS while the classifier adds ERROR and witness rows need REACHABLE/NOT REACHABLE, with no mapping or row-kind discriminator defined.
nodes.norm_label: formal manifest cannot encode its own required rows

nodes.label: A positive-control registry callers populate can attest to itself
nodes.rationale: Without a mechanical inventory binding every decision predicate to an independently executed failing control, a checker passes the checker-soundness gate without ever rejecting a planted defect — self-refuting under the workstream's own standard.
nodes.norm_label: a positive-control registry callers populate can attest to itself

nodes.label: Claimed EARS conformance is false; hash-failure branches missing
nodes.rationale: Clauses reverse or combine the required order, multi-SHALL requirements have partial scenarios, no EARS lint task exists, and a hash-command failure can be read as empty input, mismatch or pass.
nodes.norm_label: claimed ears conformance is false; hash-failure branches missing

nodes.label: The workstream does not survive its own standard
nodes.rationale: Its thesis — checker output is evidence only if the predicate discriminates the claimed property — is correct, yet four of its own proposed controls fail exactly that test.
nodes.norm_label: the workstream does not survive its own standard

nodes.label: Proportionality cuts recommended for v0.2.9
nodes.rationale: Cut the mandatory formal drift gate, move Tier 2 to on-demand and drop Tier 3, reduce to five metrics, and cut the per-diff mutation gate — preserving deterministic regressions, three-outcome gates, content-bound evidence, locking and round ownership.

nodes.label: TerminusDB packages, Codex lane: BLOCKED at the seams
nodes.rationale: The decision to ship TerminusDB is not in question and R8 guardrails are preserved; these are concrete package fixes, not reasons to revisit the owner decision.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb packages, codex lane: blocked at the seams

nodes.label: B1: no package defines an end-to-end regenerable materialization
nodes.rationale: Rebuild names an event stream and lane journals no adapter ingests, so a timed rebuild restoring only knowledge facts while silently omitting work facts still passes the current tests.
nodes.norm_label: b1: no package defines an end-to-end regenerable materialization

nodes.label: B2: CAS tokens conflated with diff references
nodes.rationale: Stripping the branch prefix from an opaque version yields neither the demonstrated CAS token nor a documented branch name, and replaying a stale body after backoff recreates the last-writer-wins loss the wrapper exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: b2: cas tokens conflated with diff references

nodes.label: B3: external invariant validator is honest but unowned
nodes.rationale: Identity-resolution cycles corrupt answers transitively, so a schema that knowingly accepts them is unsafe unless the external check is transactional and unavoidable; no package implements it.
nodes.norm_label: b3: external invariant validator is honest but unowned

nodes.label: B4: N2's relation split and per-edge provenance not implemented
nodes.rationale: depends_on carries both sub-tasking and dependency, replacing one merged-concept defect with another, and document-level provenance cannot identify the producer of one member of a set-valued edge.
nodes.norm_label: b4: n2's relation split and per-edge provenance not implemented

nodes.label: B5: graph.json cannot be ingested against the frozen schema
nodes.rationale: TerminusDB is schema-first and rejects unknown fields, and no node-kind-to-class mapping, hyperedge type or version stamp exists, so the first production ingest requires inventing ontology and data-loss policy.
nodes.norm_label: b5: graph.json cannot be ingested against the frozen schema

nodes.label: B6: the 24-query green gate is unachievable as written
nodes.rationale: Two queries are recorded schema gaps and one depends on a package deferred to the next release, so the gate either cannot pass or goes green on stubs while claiming full coverage.
nodes.norm_label: b6: the 24-query green gate is unachievable as written

nodes.label: B7: canaries contradict the normalization contract
nodes.rationale: The normalizer strips and proceeds while the canary rejects the same input before HTTP, and no mutation switch or test seam exists, so a canary asserted only against mocks stays green when the vendor drifts.
nodes.norm_label: b7: canaries contradict the normalization contract

nodes.label: B8: migration covers ChangeParents but not the likely changes
nodes.rationale: ChangeCollection is also unimplemented, and calling later reification 'an insert, not a migration' ignores that existing direct edges still need deterministic backfill, dual-read transition and removal.
nodes.norm_label: b8: migration covers changeparents but not the likely changes

nodes.label: B9: ownership still overlaps graph-store-port
nodes.rationale: The port still owns the same deliverables the three packages claim, and its every-read-and-write boundary risks making the graph consumers store clients, violating the no-store-dependency invariant.

nodes.label: B10: the exact final schema is never live-loaded
nodes.rationale: 'Valid JSON using documented constructs' is not evidence that a frozen schema is accepted or has the claimed cardinality and rejection behaviour; the gate must load it into a pinned server.
nodes.norm_label: b10: the exact final schema is never live-loaded

nodes.label: TerminusDB packages, Opus lane: BLOCKED but bounded
nodes.rationale: Strong packages with real research and no census overclaim; every blocker is one-to-three-line spec edits plus one live-load task and one architect-owned delta. A gating verdict, not a redesign verdict.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb packages, opus lane: blocked but bounded

nodes.label: B1: verification against a superseded draft is not verification
nodes.rationale: The schema is declared frozen and un-amendable, yet the first TerminusDB process in the programme starts after the freeze and after the adapter gate, so a rejected construct becomes a critical-path human revision at the worst moment.
nodes.norm_label: b1: verification against a superseded draft is not verification

nodes.label: B2: SUBTASK_OF absent; depends_on merges two relations
nodes.rationale: The requirement merges two concepts in its own normative text while prohibiting exactly that, and the cycle-detection query then conflates legitimate subtask nesting with dependency ordering.
nodes.norm_label: b2: subtask_of absent; depends_on merges two relations

nodes.label: B3: the GraphUpdate journal is ownerless yet load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation offered two branches and neither was taken, so the non-waivable timed drop-and-rebuild — the thing that makes 'never the system of record' a fact — reads an input no component produces.
nodes.norm_label: b3: the graphupdate journal is ownerless yet load-bearing

nodes.label: B4: the ingest path cannot write a single document
nodes.rationale: Three stoppers on one code path: a required version stamp no class declares, no node-to-class mapping owned by any package, and a fail-closed classifier whose reified target does not exist.
nodes.norm_label: b4: the ingest path cannot write a single document

nodes.label: B5: normalize_data_version silently produces an invalid ref
nodes.rationale: An opaque data-version id and a hand-written branch ref share a prefix; stripping it yields a value that passes the assert and the type gate and reaches HTTP — reintroducing the silent-empty-diff class the wrapper exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: b5: normalize_data_version silently produces an invalid ref

nodes.label: B6: the /api/log ban is asserted three times and enforced nowhere
nodes.rationale: The endpoint appears zero times in the adapter that could enforce it, and its closed error taxonomy has no banned-call error; this is the mitigation for the single most load-bearing fragility finding.
nodes.norm_label: b6: the /api/log ban is asserted three times and enforced nowhere

nodes.label: B7: three capabilities contradict an unamended sibling
nodes.rationale: All three lanes documented the sibling's defects and correctly declined to fix them, so four packages validate while normatively conflicting on at least seven points strict validation cannot see; the architect delta must land first.
nodes.norm_label: b7: three capabilities contradict an unamended sibling

nodes.label: B8: every-CQ-is-a-regression-test collides with declared gaps
nodes.rationale: Two of the 24 are schema gaps by design and one depends on a deferred package, so the scenario must permit 'maps to a named query or a recorded gap' rather than demanding none unmapped.
nodes.norm_label: b8: every-cq-is-a-regression-test collides with declared gaps

nodes.label: N1/N2: no edge carries provenance; RESOLVED_TO loses its own
nodes.rationale: Node-level provenance records the entity's extraction, not the resolution decision, so who merged A into B and at what confidence is unrecoverable; defensible but never stated as a tradeoff.
nodes.norm_label: n1/n2: no edge carries provenance; resolved_to loses its own

nodes.label: N4: five property names carry divergent ranges across classes
nodes.rationale: Independent of whether the server rejects it, one triple pattern then spans the work and knowledge planes, defeating the structural disjointness the schema names as its main guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: n4: five property names carry divergent ranges across classes

nodes.label: N13: release cadence has no tripwire
nodes.rationale: The sharpest dormancy evidence was a 12.5-month release gap, which a commit-count tripwire can miss entirely; add 'no stable release in any rolling 9-month window'.
nodes.norm_label: n13: release cadence has no tripwire

nodes.label: The exit path is specified as rehearsed, not merely documented
nodes.rationale: Running a full round on the files-only implementation with the adapter stopped, before reliance and re-rehearsed within one release of any tripwire firing, is the difference between a documented exit and a real one.
nodes.norm_label: the exit path is specified as rehearsed, not merely documented

nodes.label: Honest declaration plus unassigned ownership
nodes.rationale: The schema is admirably explicit that five invariants are unenforceable, but all five are deferred to a research lane rather than a change package — which is how invariants quietly never get built.

nodes.label: The audit-evidence-root contradiction
nodes.rationale: Two constraints collide: the write-evidence digest needs a git work tree, and the audit contract forbids writing into the reviewed one — so the spec forbids the way the entire effort was conducted.

nodes.label: Reviewed set versus report path (first formulation)
nodes.rationale: Relaxing the rule, writing outside the repo, and exempting a path prefix were all rejected; the constraint is relationship to the reviewed set, not location, and the report must be created rather than modified.
nodes.norm_label: reviewed set versus report path (first formulation)

nodes.label: Work root versus artifact root (the implemented resolution)
nodes.rationale: Better than the reviewed-set formulation because it explains which property required git in the first place — status enumeration catches undeclared writes — and confines that requirement to the root that needs it.
nodes.norm_label: work root versus artifact root (the implemented resolution)

nodes.label: Three independent routes reached the same defect
nodes.rationale: The re-audit applied the rule to the reports, a formal model proved the satisfiability invariant violated pre-fix, and the repairing lane found it while writing the fix — the rule was right, its predicate discriminated the wrong property.
nodes.norm_label: three independent routes reached the same defect

nodes.label: D1: derive the exec-bit inventory by property, not by directory
nodes.rationale: Four successive counts were wrong because the set was derived by directory, and any directory list is an enumeration wearing a sweep's clothing; reading the index blob shebang also lets the regression test run against a synthetic index.
nodes.norm_label: d1: derive the exec-bit inventory by property, not by directory

nodes.label: D2: the four README ambiguities answered from evidence
nodes.rationale: Roles and producers are different sets that nearly collide and the fourth lane breaks the count anyway; the v0.2.5 stamp is stale; GATE is the post-worker gate command; and 'host identity' means the config directory.
nodes.norm_label: d2: the four readme ambiguities answered from evidence

nodes.label: D3: keep bin/lane.sh but land it through evidence-contracts
nodes.rationale: It is an early implementation of the artifact-assertion doctrine, so it must be reconciled with the specified helper rather than living beside it; committing product code that contradicts a same-day spec is how doctrine drift gets created.
nodes.norm_label: d3: keep bin/lane.sh but land it through evidence-contracts

nodes.label: D4: amend the OpenSpec README rather than migrate eight packages
nodes.rationale: A mechanical header transform is churn across files four in-flight packages already claim, and the README asserting a conformance the repo lacks is itself the drift defect; state the actual convention instead.
nodes.norm_label: d4: amend the openspec readme rather than migrate eight packages

nodes.label: D5: the Git-Bash half of the S1 gate is deferred, not satisfied
nodes.rationale: Seeding a plausible digest would ship a trust anchor nobody traced — the exact failure the package exists to prevent — so durable lanes on MSYS2/Git-Bash are unavailable until one real trace is committed; the blocker is host access, not design.
nodes.norm_label: d5: the git-bash half of the s1 gate is deferred, not satisfied

nodes.label: D6: split decision-lineage rather than reorder the stage
nodes.rationale: The dependency is real for verdict lineage but not for token, cost and model emission, so splitting is smaller than reordering and unblocks the half most needed — a whole session of dispatches left no bytes in the event log.
nodes.norm_label: d6: split decision-lineage rather than reorder the stage

nodes.label: D7: every new gate lands in shadow mode first
nodes.rationale: A wrong gate is worse than an absent one because it blocks correct work while looking principled; promotion requires ten real runs with no false positive, generalizing the reaper's two first-run false positives into policy.
nodes.norm_label: d7: every new gate lands in shadow mode first

nodes.label: D8: evidence-contracts owns and creates lib/evidence.sh
nodes.rationale: The file is that package's subject matter rather than an incidental dependency, and under the contention-derived schedule it also lands first in execution order.
nodes.norm_label: d8: evidence-contracts owns and creates lib/evidence.sh

nodes.label: D9: dogfood every enhancement in the session that produces it
nodes.rationale: The strandings, the undetected suspension and the unearned pass are all failures the release's own packages prevent, and they happened because those packages were unbuilt; shadow mode is the bootstrap-risk mitigation.
nodes.norm_label: d9: dogfood every enhancement in the session that produces it

nodes.label: D10: schedule by contention, but round depth is the real limit
nodes.rationale: Three heavily-claimed files serialize most stages regardless of colouring, vendor caps bound width, and parallelism cannot compress a serial audit-rework cycle — only better specification up front can, so the schedule is advisory.
nodes.norm_label: d10: schedule by contention, but round depth is the real limit

nodes.label: D11: the exec-bit exclusion list is by pattern with a stated reason
nodes.rationale: Excluding a pattern means a new file inherits a justified decision while excluding a filename leaves the next file undecided; an exclusion without a reason is indistinguishable from an oversight.
nodes.norm_label: d11: the exec-bit exclusion list is by pattern with a stated reason

nodes.label: D11 correction: an exclusion wildcard fails silent
nodes.rationale: A wildcard is safe for inclusions because it covers files that do not exist yet, but for exclusions it silently covers directories nobody checked — so the pattern's breadth is part of the claim and must be verified match by match.
nodes.norm_label: d11 correction: an exclusion wildcard fails silent

nodes.label: D12: premises cite behaviour and carry their check command
nodes.rationale: Line-pinned premises expire on the next edit and one asserted count was false when written because nobody ran the grep; a number in a specification is a claim, and an unrun claim is a guess.
nodes.norm_label: d12: premises cite behaviour and carry their check command

nodes.label: D12 consequence: re-baseline downstream premises at dispatch
nodes.rationale: Under same-session dogfooding the codebase moves while the plan executes, so a premise written against the planning snapshot describes a repository that no longer exists; this is the standing cost of D9 and must be paid deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: d12 consequence: re-baseline downstream premises at dispatch

nodes.label: D13: do not port the orchestration layer to Unison

nodes.label: README fact-checking edit plan
nodes.rationale: 'Shipped' is defined as present and executable from a fresh clone, not merely specified elsewhere, which is what turns several confident README claims into stale ones.

nodes.label: The single most misleading sentence: hard mode is fail-closed at every stage
nodes.rationale: The gate only checks that an audit file exists with an allowed verdict while five ordinary audit failure paths exit without replacing it, so after a rework round a stale APPROVED satisfies the gate for a different diff.
nodes.norm_label: the single most misleading sentence: hard mode is fail-closed at every stage

nodes.label: worker-run.sh is shipped, not the stub the README describes
nodes.rationale: Both launcher-only and container profiles plus draft-PR creation are implemented; the honest qualifier is that a fresh clone has no built launcher binary, so it must be built or supplied first.
nodes.norm_label: worker-run.sh is shipped, not the stub the readme describes

nodes.label: The cross-vendor invariant check is miswired in hard mode
nodes.rationale: The audit compares a configured worker vendor key while the hard worker reads a different key defaulting to Codex, so a default Codex worker can pass the purported check and be audited by Codex.
nodes.norm_label: the cross-vendor invariant check is miswired in hard mode

nodes.label: install.sh is mode 100644 so ./install.sh exits 126
nodes.rationale: Verified literally on a clean checkout; the script then chmods 33 indexed-100644 scripts, permanently dirtying every installed clone — which poisons the README's own dirty-safety claims.

nodes.label: durable.enabled is inert: parsed and mapped but read by nothing
nodes.rationale: true and false do not switch durable lanes, and the shipped example exposes the key without a warning — a configuration surface that looks like a control and is not.
nodes.norm_label: durable.enabled is inert: parsed and mapped but read by nothing

nodes.label: Claude is a half-wired vendor, not a functional worker
nodes.rationale: Worktrees create its vendor home, lane-run maps its env variable and pueue gives it a group, but the hard worker command builder accepts only Grok and Codex.
nodes.norm_label: claude is a half-wired vendor, not a functional worker

nodes.label: 33 bats files and 382 tests, but no CI runs them on any platform
nodes.rationale: The maintenance workflow only reports and the smoke workflow only exercises the installer, so the suite must be presented as a local result rather than implied CI coverage.
nodes.norm_label: 33 bats files and 382 tests, but no ci runs them on any platform

nodes.label: All ten tracked active change packages fail openspec validate
nodes.rationale: The layout is OpenSpec-like rather than conformant, and the release premise's count of sixteen pre-existing packages cannot be reproduced from the current tree, so the report states the observable count.
nodes.norm_label: all ten tracked active change packages fail openspec validate

nodes.label: Unverifiable-claims class and the evidence that would settle each
nodes.rationale: Model availability, vendor upload behaviour, live concurrency results, NTSTATUS recovery and the 45-77% token saving are all empirical claims about external or time-sensitive systems, not properties of the repository.
nodes.norm_label: unverifiable-claims class and the evidence that would settle each

nodes.label: README line-edit pass (sentence-level only)
nodes.rationale: Scope deliberately held to sentence rewrites with no section moves and no claim verification, so structural and factual work stay with their own lanes.

nodes.label: Tic: the contrastive snap 'X, not Y'
nodes.rationale: The document's signature move and often its strength; keep it when Y is a concrete false comfort the reader might reach for, cut it when Y only renames X.
nodes.norm_label: tic: the contrastive snap 'x, not y'

nodes.label: Tic: 'silent/silently' as a moral intensifier
nodes.rationale: The product story is about making silence visible so the word earns some uses, but applying the same adverb to every failure mode replaces concrete verbs like refuses, drops, masks and skips.

nodes.label: Tic: 'never' as sentence engine
nodes.rationale: Blunt bans are a virtue, not an error, but when every third rule opens with 'never' the reader stops ranking severity; vary the secondary ones so the hard bans still land.

nodes.label: Tic: em-dash cargo packing secondary facts into primary sentences
nodes.rationale: One claim per sentence in the limits section — the honesty already does the work, and density is not the same as rigour.
nodes.norm_label: tic: em-dash cargo packing secondary facts into primary sentences

nodes.label: Best-written passage: the Grok headless write-cancellation bug
nodes.rationale: Short sentences advance one fact each and the killer clause is concrete and visual, then the digests pin the story to the evidence contract without restating the doctrine.
nodes.norm_label: best-written passage: the grok headless write-cancellation bug

nodes.label: Worst-written passage: the vendor-concurrency bullet
nodes.rationale: One bullet tries to be a test log, a capacity decision, a citation and an operational rule; parentheticals swallow the pass criteria and a second topic wears the first topic's bullet.

nodes.label: Diagnosis: three documents interleaved into one README
nodes.rationale: A concept paper, an operator manual and a release ledger each damage the other two; the manual duplicates reference material that is already drifting, and the ledger does the roadmap's job.
nodes.norm_label: diagnosis: three documents interleaved into one readme

nodes.label: Principle: the README states what is, ROADMAP states when it became so
nodes.rationale: Version-stamped provenance in the README is structurally guaranteed to rot every release, so release stamps should move wholesale to the roadmap.
nodes.norm_label: principle: the readme states what is, roadmap states when it became so

nodes.label: Replace hard-numbered cross-references with named anchors
nodes.rationale: At least four numbered references already point at the wrong section — the fossil record of an unpropagated insertion — and after a restructure they would lie fifteen times.
nodes.norm_label: replace hard-numbered cross-references with named anchors

nodes.label: Proposed order: fifteen sections become twelve
nodes.rationale: Highest-value move is defining the five-part spec before the parties that speak it; the lifecycle merges into the quickstart so it is taught at the moment the reader lives it, and hard mode follows the doctrine it mechanizes.
nodes.norm_label: proposed order: fifteen sections become twelve

nodes.label: New section: The record (event log, work-DAG, knowledge plane, store)
nodes.rationale: Placed after 'reports are claims' because it answers where claims, evidence and verdicts live; must be sold as cross-session provenance and deterministic gate checks, never as retrieval accuracy.
nodes.norm_label: new section: the record (event log, work-dag, knowledge plane, store)

nodes.label: Re-key the cross-vendor invariant on model family, not CLI name
nodes.rationale: A gateway CLI serving another vendor's family is that family, so an agy lane on a claude model auditing a Claude-implemented diff is same-family review wearing a different binary.
nodes.norm_label: re-key the cross-vendor invariant on model family, not cli name

nodes.label: Checker soundness as the doctrine's fourth movement
nodes.rationale: A test that never fires is silent, whereas a checker whose predicate does not match its claim passes loudly — and a loud pass is trusted; so the checks themselves are claims too.
nodes.norm_label: checker soundness as the doctrine's fourth movement

nodes.label: The three cuts worth fighting for
nodes.rationale: Exit-code tables, the per-CLI bug forensics and component-level launcher trivia crowd out the doctrine-level limits that decide adoption; a reader who stops at NTSTATUS masking never learns Foreman records no tokens or cost.
nodes.norm_label: the three cuts worth fighting for

nodes.label: F-UUTILS-MKDIR: the portable mkdir mutex is not atomic on Ubuntu 26.04
nodes.rationale: Measured 57 mutual-exclusion violations over 15 rounds of 8 racers against zero with GNU mkdir; a blocker because it invalidates an invariant the durable-lanes design treats as axiomatic.
nodes.norm_label: f-uutils-mkdir: the portable mkdir mutex is not atomic on ubuntu 26.04

nodes.label: Mechanism: uutils does a userspace statx check-then-act
nodes.rationale: strace shows uutils never issuing the syscall on an existing directory while GNU lets the kernel return EEXIST, so any lock on the former has a window between statx and create.
nodes.norm_label: mechanism: uutils does a userspace statx check-then-act

nodes.label: Blast radius: every lock in the system is this primitive
nodes.rationale: Sequence, attempt, compaction and worktree locks all use it, the event log is the documented source of truth for durable lanes, and raised concurrency caps make multi-lane contention the normal operating mode.
nodes.norm_label: blast radius: every lock in the system is this primitive

nodes.label: Remedy: prefer flock, fall back to mkdir only on MSYS2
nodes.rationale: flock is present on WSL and already a required tool, so the mkdir mutex should survive only where flock genuinely does not exist.
nodes.norm_label: remedy: prefer flock, fall back to mkdir only on msys2

nodes.label: Detect the hazard rather than assume it away
nodes.rationale: A preflight probe should assert the resolved mkdir takes EEXIST from the kernel and refuse or loudly warn otherwise, plus a permanent regression test that measures mutual exclusion under release-level contention.
nodes.norm_label: detect the hazard rather than assume it away

nodes.label: Separate finding: the append-failure test is invalid as root
nodes.rationale: It forces a write failure with chmod 000 but root bypasses permission bits so the assertion inverts; a test-validity bug tied to the non-root WSL setup residual, not a product defect.
nodes.norm_label: separate finding: the append-failure test is invalid as root

nodes.label: Codex final audit: DO NOT DISPATCH S1
nodes.rationale: The lock package is no longer the stop; the executable-scope half is, because the landing note contradicts the package's own normative task — never hand a worker that contradiction.
nodes.norm_label: codex final audit: do not dispatch s1

nodes.label: Per-stage dispatchability with intrinsic readiness separated
nodes.rationale: Reporting intrinsic readiness alongside sequence position keeps a dependency from being mistaken for a defect in a later package.
nodes.norm_label: per-stage dispatchability with intrinsic readiness separated

nodes.label: Blocked-before-dispatch versus fixable-in-flight distinction
nodes.rationale: Operational rather than severity-based: blocked means the contract must change before a worker starts, fixable means the worker can start and close the gap as an explicit evidence task.

nodes.label: Finding rate is not falling; defects relocate across fresh seams
nodes.rationale: Release convergence is governed by the structural class — architecture, joint unsatisfiability, orphaned ownership and non-discriminating predicates — and that class is not empty, so a lower count of old defects proves nothing.
nodes.norm_label: finding rate is not falling; defects relocate across fresh seams

nodes.label: Cross-fix contradictions ranked by the work they stop
nodes.rationale: Reversed stage order, a widened landing row whose package never widened, telemetry that guarantees a downstream premise stops, and a directed producer with two consumers still requiring the old flag.
nodes.norm_label: cross-fix contradictions ranked by the work they stop

nodes.label: Verified without running Graphify: --directed is rejected
nodes.rationale: The update parser accepts only two options and exits 2 otherwise, and neither publishing cadence passes a directed keyword, so the old gate could never be satisfied.
nodes.norm_label: verified without running graphify: --directed is rejected

nodes.label: Endpoint-order evidence from the committed graph.json
nodes.rationale: 1,465 of 3,668 links run descending, so the replacement zero-descending gate is non-vacuous on this corpus — but it establishes endpoint-order survival, not parallel-edge survival.
nodes.norm_label: endpoint-order evidence from the committed graph.json

nodes.label: KC-7 cannot distinguish a supporting citation from an unrelated valid id
nodes.rationale: A syntactically valid but semantically unrelated edge id still scores as correct, so the predicate cannot discriminate the property its basis names; rename it as syntactic compliance or add a discriminator.
nodes.norm_label: kc-7 cannot distinguish a supporting citation from an unrelated valid id

nodes.label: RECONCILE decisions were not propagated into the stage table
nodes.rationale: The claim that every stage is independently taggable is false under its own package dependencies, so the S4 order, early instrumentation and gate placement must all be corrected.
nodes.norm_label: reconcile decisions were not propagated into the stage table

nodes.label: release-metrics T1 always reaches its stop branch after S4
nodes.rationale: It requires the S4 event types and emits to remain absent and instructs the worker to stop when they exist, so it must be rewritten as validation of the landed telemetry interface.
nodes.norm_label: release-metrics t1 always reaches its stop branch after s4

nodes.label: Opus final audit: DO NOT DISPATCH S1 (hours, not a round)
nodes.rationale: Both halves of S1 fail a dispatch precondition, but two architect rulings and three mechanical actions clear it; the defect S1 exists to fix was reproduced live, so this is a hold with a short path off it.
nodes.norm_label: opus final audit: do not dispatch s1 (hours, not a round)

nodes.label: L1: flock can never earn a trusted verdict
nodes.rationale: The only trusted evidence class is a create returning EEXIST, which flock never produces, so a faithful implementation refuses every acquisition on the release's own reference host and the flock-path scenario is unreachable.
nodes.norm_label: l1: flock can never earn a trusted verdict

nodes.label: L2: the pinned-mechanism seed is circular
nodes.rationale: The task requires committing a trace from a host the design says ships no tracer — which is the entire reason the pinned class exists — and no Windows tracing method is named anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: l2: the pinned-mechanism seed is circular

nodes.label: C1: three conflicting scope statements for one package
nodes.rationale: Both planning documents absorbed a widening the package never received, so S1's stated rationale that the exec-bit fix unblocks a clean tree is not delivered by S1's contents.
nodes.norm_label: c1: three conflicting scope statements for one package

nodes.label: G1: the entire fix round is uncommitted
nodes.rationale: Worktrees are cut from a committed ref so every worker would receive pre-fix specs, and with no commit boundary the fix round cannot be isolated by any git operation — 'audit the delta only' is not mechanically constructible.
nodes.norm_label: g1: the entire fix round is uncommitted

nodes.label: G2: ten of 33 live packages fail strict validation
nodes.rationale: Six are v0.2.9-authored rather than pre-existing, so the scoping language understates it, and the governing decision is an unchecked box with no decision record.
nodes.norm_label: g2: ten of 33 live packages fail strict validation

nodes.label: B6: a whole-tree control inventory makes its own gate unreachable
nodes.rationale: 382 test blocks each need a registry row with existing control artifacts and no task budgets the work; the fix for a diff-scoped blind spot overshot into an unsatisfiable obligation, in the package that exists to forbid vacuous predicates.
nodes.norm_label: b6: a whole-tree control inventory makes its own gate unreachable

nodes.label: F4g: graph-store-port's central invariant rests on a phantom artifact
nodes.rationale: The sibling package already recorded that GraphUpdate never had an owner, but the port was not updated, so its spec now contradicts its own proposal and tasks and the rebuild proof cannot be discharged.
nodes.norm_label: f4g: graph-store-port's central invariant rests on a phantom artifact

nodes.label: F4: S4's stated order is impossible
nodes.rationale: The package at position 1 states in bold that it must not start before the package at position 2 has merged.
nodes.norm_label: f4: s4's stated order is impossible

nodes.label: F1: doctrine-reality-drift fails the merge gate for every later stage
nodes.rationale: It requires unresolved seeded contradictions to fail a fail-closed gate input while four or more of the seeded claims are owned by packages landing much later; a sibling solves this with a shadow default that this package forbids.
nodes.norm_label: f1: doctrine-reality-drift fails the merge gate for every later stage

nodes.label: F5: an inert rework budget and a nonexistent Abandoned state
nodes.rationale: With no counter anywhere in the codebase, 'shall not be counted against' is satisfied by every possible implementation — the exact inert-flag defect the next package in the same stage exists to eliminate.
nodes.norm_label: f5: an inert rework budget and a nonexistent abandoned state

nodes.label: F6: two packages claim lib/evidence.sh identically
nodes.rationale: Both encode the function the same way, so this needs only a who-writes-it-first ownership ruling rather than a design change.
nodes.norm_label: f6: two packages claim lib/evidence.sh identically

nodes.label: Structural class halves each round but does not empty
nodes.rationale: Counts fell threefold while the structural share rose and finding density tripled on a smaller already-audited scope; three of four S1 structural findings were introduced by the fix rounds themselves.
nodes.norm_label: structural class halves each round but does not empty

nodes.label: The unsatisfiable-gate defect has now moved twice in one requirement
nodes.rationale: Round 1 demanded evidence Git-Bash could not produce, round 3 restored Git-Bash and left flock unsatisfiable — across two consecutive fixes written to remove exactly that defect, now sitting on the primary host.
nodes.norm_label: the unsatisfiable-gate defect has now moved twice in one requirement

nodes.label: Opus per-stage dispatchability table
nodes.rationale: Two stages dispatch as they stand, three go with stated caveats, one needs a five-line deletion, and four each need one architect ruling first.

nodes.label: Consequence: the entire graph plane ships off by default
nodes.rationale: Nearly every kill criterion returns UNCOMPUTABLE this release and the register forbids shipping an uncomputable criterion's component enabled, so this is a deliberate outcome worth saying out loud before the largest implementation block is dispatched.
nodes.norm_label: consequence: the entire graph plane ships off by default

nodes.label: The path off the hold, ranked by what stops work first
nodes.rationale: Commit the fix round first because nothing else is safe or auditable as a delta until it exists, then make the conformance decision, then two architect rulings and one scope sentence.
nodes.norm_label: the path off the hold, ranked by what stops work first

nodes.label: The kill-criteria register is the release's most rigorous artifact
nodes.rationale: Counts agree across three places, the action enum is closed, every criterion names its own denominator, and the omission loophole is closed — rules stated generally rather than as named carve-outs.
nodes.norm_label: the kill-criteria register is the release's most rigorous artifact

nodes.label: Measured exec-bit census contradicts the doctrine package
nodes.rationale: 605 tracked files with 40 at 100755, and 28 of those are markdown including whole spec sets under audit, so the fix rounds themselves shipped executable markdown that the specified test cannot catch.
nodes.norm_label: measured exec-bit census contradicts the doctrine package

nodes.norm_label: directed:true does not establish parallel-edge preservation

nodes.norm_label: td1: the directed:true gate does not entail parallel-edge survival

nodes.norm_label: td2: the collapsed-edge counters pass vacuously

nodes.norm_label: td4: the claimed live terminusdb verification does not exist
