nodes.norm_label: spec amended while tasks.md and proposal.md instruct the opposite

nodes.label: Platform lockout: the mkdir fallback refuses every acquisition
nodes.norm_label: platform lockout: the mkdir fallback refuses every acquisition

nodes.label: Every new unsound predicate sits at a seam the fix round created
nodes.norm_label: every new unsound predicate sits at a seam the fix round created

nodes.label: v0.2.9 Total GeorgeCall implementation
nodes.rationale: Written at the end of the planning session so the next session starts without reconstruction; branch plan/v029-graph-multivendor, nothing pushed.

nodes.label: S1 dispatch (crlf-extensionless-hardening + lock-primitive-hardening first)
nodes.rationale: Both now validate strict and both blockers were resolved; both root causes reproduce live, which is why they go first.

nodes.label: uutils mkdir mutual-exclusion violations (57/15 rounds)
nodes.rationale: uutils mkdir 0.8.0 shows 57 mutual-exclusion violations over 15 rounds of 8 racers; GNU mkdir 9.7 shows 0; flock shows 0 — so the mkdir mutex primitive is the defect, not the harness.

nodes.label: Exec-bit scope as a mechanical 41-file inventory
nodes.rationale: Derived mechanically to replace three contradictory numbers that three documents each carried.
nodes.norm_label: exec-bit scope as a mechanical 41-file inventory

nodes.label: Mechanism-relative syscall evidence definition
nodes.rationale: mkdir(2)+EEXIST for the mutex, flock(2)+EWOULDBLOCK for flock; the prior definition demanded EEXIST of flock, which creates nothing, so every acquisition on WSL and Linux would have refused.

nodes.label: S4 telemetry as the release spine
nodes.rationale: No comparative claim in the release is computable before telemetry lands.
nodes.norm_label: s4 telemetry as the release spine

nodes.label: Keep auditing or start implementing (the open judgement)
nodes.rationale: Three audit rounds cut findings 102 to 37, but the structural share rose 75.5 to 78 percent, per-package yield tripled, and 11 of 12 closure claims carried a new defect in the same package — so working code should adjudicate the specs from here.
nodes.norm_label: keep auditing or start implementing (the open judgement)

nodes.label: Fix rounds reintroduce defects
nodes.rationale: Three of four S1 blockers were introduced by the fix rounds; one round repaired a lock predicate for Git-Bash and reintroduced the identical flaw on WSL and Linux.

nodes.label: 33 uncommitted filemode changes held back deliberately
nodes.rationale: Landing them would quietly perform the exec-bit fix inside an unrelated commit; that fix belongs to crlf-extensionless-hardening, gated.
nodes.norm_label: 33 uncommitted filemode changes held back deliberately

nodes.label: bin/lane.sh (product code outside any package scope)
nodes.rationale: Created outside any package's scope; lands through evidence-contracts per decision D3 rather than as loose product code.
nodes.norm_label: bin/lane.sh (product code outside any package scope)

nodes.label: Never build a heredoc inline through bash -lc
nodes.rationale: Prose containing backticks or apostrophes truncates mid-content and executes prose as shell commands; cost four incidents in one session. Write to /tmp from a file then tr -d '\r' into the target.
nodes.norm_label: never build a heredoc inline through bash -lc

nodes.label: Grok dispatch recipe (stall mitigation)
nodes.rationale: Grok stalled on 3 of 8 lanes; dispatch with --always-approve --max-turns 30, inline every fact, forbid the Read tool, and write the validity-critical file first.

nodes.label: Use /usr/local/bin/openspec, not npx openspec
nodes.rationale: npx openspec resolves to a broken stub.

nodes.label: Two planes, two write disciplines, one join, one gate rule
nodes.rationale: Separating the work plane (deterministic projection of the event log) from the knowledge plane (graphify, two-cadence) keeps every LLM out of the per-commit path while still yielding a queryable cross-run record.
nodes.norm_label: two planes, two write disciplines, one join, one gate rule

nodes.label: Work-DAG plane (deterministic projection of the event log)
nodes.rationale: No LLM ever writes it and it never passes through graphify: ontology-learning F1 is 0.02-0.66 for taxonomies and 0.03-0.36 for axioms, and the work-DAG is fully determined by data Foreman already emits.
nodes.norm_label: work-dag plane (deterministic projection of the event log)

nodes.label: Knowledge plane (graphify, two-cadence schedule)
nodes.rationale: AST-only graphify update per merge (measured zero-token); semantic extraction, clustering and community labels on a nightly/release cadence because the GraphRAG community-refresh analogue costs ~14M tokens per corpus change.

nodes.label: events.jsonl as the system of record for work lineage
nodes.rationale: Frozen top-level shape {seq,ts,type,lane,commit?,payload}; all additions nest in payload so no signature migration is needed.
nodes.norm_label: events.jsonl as the system of record for work lineage

nodes.label: worklog.jsonl (work-DAG projection artifact)
nodes.rationale: A sibling of graph.json, never written into it, because graphify --update rebuilds from the filesystem and would destroy injected rows on every refresh.

nodes.label: graph.json as the sole ingest source
nodes.rationale: It is the highest-fidelity artifact graphify produces; the cypher.txt export emits 5 fields and drops source_file, source_location, confidence_score, hyperedges and communities, destroying the audit trail.
nodes.norm_label: graph.json as the sole ingest source

nodes.label: TerminusDB adopted with guardrails as a queryable materialisation
nodes.rationale: Never the system of record: bus factor 1, one prior 14-month dormancy, 105 npm downloads/month, and the fast commit-log path is the paid tier — so everything is regenerable and the port bounds the downside to a re-materialisation.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb adopted with guardrails as a queryable materialisation

nodes.label: Store commits are an audit trail only, never lineage
nodes.rationale: Measured 2.4 ms/commit dead-linear scan with O(offset) paging, so a commit-per-write lineage design cannot hold at Foreman's volume.
nodes.norm_label: store commits are an audit trail only, never lineage

nodes.label: Closed-world document schema validated at write time
nodes.rationale: 10 of 24 competency questions need negation-as-failure, unanswerable in principle under open-world assumptions; Foreman's graph records a bounded, fully-observed process, so closed-world is the correct model, and ANCHOR showed only write-time validation buys conformance.
nodes.norm_label: closed-world document schema validated at write time

nodes.label: OWL rejected; no second formalism
nodes.rationale: Open-world semantics cannot express the negation and aggregation questions the plane exists to answer; the schema stays OWL 2 RL-shaped only so a mechanical RDF export remains possible.

nodes.label: GraphContextBlock (pre-serialized, content-hashed, budgeted)
nodes.rationale: The block is immutable and content-hashed into the run record so the audit trail can prove what the worker saw and the auditor can be served the same bytes.

nodes.label: Subject-grouped arrow DSL serializer
nodes.rationale: Cheapest of 13 measured formats at 13.7 tokens/edge (expanded JSON-LD is 3.64x); syntax preference inverts across vendors (IoU < 0.2), so the serializer is one swappable function measured per vendor, not a dogma.

nodes.label: 2,000-token default context budget (hard cap 4,000)
nodes.rationale: The accuracy knee is measured at 100-200 triples and over-serving falls below the no-graph baseline, so the builder deliberately under-serves and sets a truncated flag that licenses the escape hatch.

nodes.label: Inline edge-ID citation contract with deterministic verification
nodes.rationale: Post-hoc citation attachment collapses recall from 73.6 to 26.7, and summarizing served edges costs 8-15 points of citation precision; because the targets are DB rows rather than paragraphs, attribution becomes an exact check.
nodes.norm_label: inline edge-id citation contract with deterministic verification

nodes.label: Pre-serialization beats agentic graph traversal
nodes.rationale: Measured 89.80 vs 82.6 WebQSP Hit at one sixth to one eighth the LLM calls, and it is the only design where the audit trail can prove what the worker saw.

nodes.label: graphify MCP server demoted to bounded read-only escape hatch
nodes.rationale: All 10 MCP tools return prose strings rather than JSON, and query_graph's literal substring matching silently returns zero recall without a vocab-expansion pre-step, so lane-facing access must go through Foreman's wrapper or not at all.
nodes.norm_label: graphify mcp server demoted to bounded read-only escape hatch

nodes.label: Two-speed gate rule (closed-world blocks, open-world warns)
nodes.rationale: Open-world grounding runs at 88-94% precision; at ~40 merges/week a blocking check false-blocks about 3 correct merges/week and teaches the operator to bypass the gate.
nodes.norm_label: two-speed gate rule (closed-world blocks, open-world warns)

nodes.label: G1-G9 deterministic audit-groundedness checks
nodes.rationale: All closed-world and 0% false-positive by construction; they catch hallucinated findings and self-contradictory verdicts that nothing catches today, and G1-G6 plus G9 are jq plus git over JSON with no graph store at all.

nodes.label: Validator ships with a known-violating canary
nodes.rationale: pySHACL silently reported Conforms: True when SPARQL-targeted shapes were not evaluated — a no-op gate is worse than no gate, so the validator must fail closed on its own canary.
nodes.norm_label: validator ships with a known-violating canary

nodes.label: Three-outcome verdict contract (errored lane returns UNVERIFIED)
nodes.rationale: An errored audit lane must never return REFUTED/BLOCKED; this directly resolves the existing audit tie-break pain.
nodes.norm_label: three-outcome verdict contract (errored lane returns unverified)

nodes.label: Agents read, only host-side consolidate writes
nodes.rationale: Oracle Poisoning against a production 42M-node code KG had every tested model (9 models, 3 providers) trust poisoned data 100% of the time at moderate sophistication, and of five defences only read-only access control eliminated the direct mutation vector.
nodes.norm_label: agents read, only host-side consolidate writes

nodes.label: Every write is additive: supersede and invalidate, never mutate
nodes.rationale: Follows Graphiti's invalidate-don't-delete and PROV-O wasInvalidatedBy; also required because selective un-merge in the store is assumed impossible.
nodes.norm_label: every write is additive: supersede and invalidate, never mutate

nodes.label: JK-1..JK-5 identifier scheme (the join between planes)
nodes.rationale: The checkpoint SHA bridges work to knowledge mechanically with zero LLM: git diff-tree over the checkpoint commit yields source_file values that are already graphify node keys, falling back to the file node rather than guessing a symbol.
nodes.norm_label: jk-1..jk-5 identifier scheme (the join between planes)

nodes.label: Stamp the producing graphify version at every ingest
nodes.rationale: Node IDs are stable across content edits and machines, but a file move re-IDs every symbol and a graphify version upgrade can migrate the whole ID space (it happened at issue 1504); graph.json does not record the version, so ingest must.
nodes.norm_label: stamp the producing graphify version at every ingest

nodes.label: Cross-vendor independence is mostly an illusion (~2 effective votes)
nodes.rationale: Nine frontier LLMs across seven families behave as about 2 effective independent votes; individual top models matched or exceeded the full panel, so the independence argument justifies roughly two vendors and no more.
nodes.norm_label: cross-vendor independence is mostly an illusion (~2 effective votes)

nodes.label: The cold diff is Foreman's real decorrelation mechanism
nodes.rationale: A different evidence set and a different role is stronger decorrelation than anything the vendor-independence papers audited, so it is the property to protect rather than vendor count.
nodes.norm_label: the cold diff is foreman's real decorrelation mechanism

nodes.label: Graph retrieval loses to trivial baselines on the common case
nodes.rationale: BM-25 beats all nine GraphRAG systems on True/False; LightRAG spent 83.9M construction tokens to score below TF-IDF; MSFT GraphRAG paid ~101M tokens per accuracy point — so the plane is not a retrieval-accuracy play and lookup-shaped questions route to lexical paths.
nodes.norm_label: graph retrieval loses to trivial baselines on the common case

nodes.label: LEED case: assembled neurosymbolic pipelines lose to their own baseline
nodes.rationale: Full pipeline 61.6% vs text-only 67.3% with the deterministic sub-check locally perfect; extraction failures and conservatism cost more globally than the symbolic precision bought, so the plane needs an off-switch and an A/B path.
nodes.norm_label: leed case: assembled neurosymbolic pipelines lose to their own baseline

nodes.label: Falsification harness (ships with the plane or the plane does not ship)
nodes.rationale: Two lanes independently insisted on the just-prompt-the-model baseline; without the harness the architecture's default failure mode is the LEED regression, so the kill criteria are decided before building.
nodes.norm_label: falsification harness (ships with the plane or the plane does not ship)

nodes.label: Query census (kill criterion for the store)
nodes.rationale: One release of architect queries classified point-lookup / single-doc / genuinely multi-hop-cross-run; a small multi-hop share means the store materialisation is activity without progress and GP-6 freezes.
nodes.norm_label: query census (kill criterion for the store)

nodes.label: Locked prompt-baseline arm at equal cost
nodes.rationale: One strong model plus spec, diff, report and deterministic checks at equal cost; if graph-context lanes do not beat it on cross-session tasks the context builder is demoted or shelved.
nodes.norm_label: locked prompt-baseline arm at equal cost

nodes.label: Shadow-mode Tier-3 for ~100 merges before promotion
nodes.rationale: Precision is measured on our own data and promotion to blocking happens only on a pre-declared threshold — never on vibes.
nodes.norm_label: shadow-mode tier-3 for ~100 merges before promotion

nodes.label: Make round-mode dispatch the default (durable.enabled=true)
nodes.rationale: The number-one failure class (background-and-stop, 11+ occurrences across three vendors) is prompt-immune and its structural fix is shipped but off; without it the event log is empty for most rounds and the work plane has nothing to project.

nodes.label: GP-1 work-plane-telemetry
nodes.rationale: M1-M8 and every cost-matched comparison are uncomputable without payload.usage; this is the single biggest telemetry gap.

nodes.label: GP-2 audit-groundedness-gate
nodes.rationale: Near-free: it requires no graph store at all and removes a currently-invisible failure class at 0% false-positive cost.

nodes.label: GP-3 knowledge-plane-refresh
nodes.rationale: Manual refresh is the substrate's biggest operational weakness; three graphify versions coexist (0.9.15 skill / 0.9.16 PATH / 0.9.18 dist-packages) and two concurrent writers are silent last-writer-wins.

nodes.label: GP-4 work-dag-projection
nodes.rationale: All inputs already exist and cost zero LLM tokens; event_offset makes the plane reconstructible and diffable so 'is the graph correct?' becomes a deterministic check.

nodes.label: GP-5 graph-context-builder
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json and worklog.jsonl directly so it does not block on the store; deterministic citation verification is the cheap, novel win.

nodes.label: GP-6 graph-store-port
nodes.rationale: Adopting before the census is a judgement call justified because the port bounds the downside to a re-materialisation and the ontology work is store-agnostic; the architect may legitimately defer it behind the census.

nodes.label: GP-7 graph-eval-falsification
nodes.rationale: This is what makes the kill criteria executable; the census instrumentation can start with GP-1.

nodes.label: The refuse list (22 things explicitly not built)
nodes.rationale: Each entry names the evidence that closes it, so the boundary is auditable rather than a matter of taste.
nodes.norm_label: the refuse list (22 things explicitly not built)

nodes.label: No edge properties: reify Mention now
nodes.rationale: Retrofitting per-edge confidence onto SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS later is a migration plus backfill, so reification is planned up front.
nodes.norm_label: no edge properties: reify mention now

nodes.label: Claim/Evaluation/Finding/Source are top-level documents, never @subdocument
nodes.rationale: Cascade-delete silently violates the invariant that superseded objects remain addressable.

nodes.label: Every LLM-populated field is an enum or a reference
nodes.rationale: Foreman's own graphify extraction spec measured continuous confidence ranges collapsing to a bimodal binary (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+), so free floats and open strings are banned.
nodes.norm_label: every llm-populated field is an enum or a reference

nodes.label: CAS on shared documents, branch-per-lane for independent work
nodes.rationale: Appends of distinct documents need no CAS (12/12 concurrent writers green) but read-modify-write on shared documents is silent last-write-wins in 10/10 runs without the Terminusdb-Data-Version header; branch-per-lane plus /api/apply is the only path with real conflict detection.
nodes.norm_label: cas on shared documents, branch-per-lane for independent work

nodes.label: agy (Antigravity CLI) re-derivation residual
nodes.rationale: The Gemini lane evidence evaluated @google/gemini-cli 0.52.0 but the mandated lane is agy 1.1.7, which has --json-schema, --mode plan|accept-edits and --effort; the adapter contract stands but the gemini row is invalid and must be re-derived live.

nodes.label: No re-modelling of git commit ancestry as graph edges
nodes.rationale: git already answers children, leaves, lineage and diff in four commands; re-modelling buys nothing and adds a sync failure mode, so Commit nodes are sha references only.
nodes.norm_label: no re-modelling of git commit ancestry as graph edges

nodes.label: An auditor's verdict is a claim with provenance, not an unexamined gate
nodes.rationale: Foreman doctrine: mechanically checkable audit findings are re-verified by the architect against live tooling before being accepted.
nodes.norm_label: an auditor's verdict is a claim with provenance, not an unexamined gate

nodes.label: Finding 1 — the --directed mandate is unimplementable on the refresh command
nodes.rationale: graphify update accepts only --force and --no-cluster; --directed exists only on diagnose multigraph as a post-build simulation, so the package gates publication on a counter produced by simulating directedness over a graph whose parallel edges have already collapsed — a check structurally incapable of observing what it gates.
nodes.norm_label: finding 1 — the --directed mandate is unimplementable on the refresh command

nodes.label: Fix: specify the refresh as build_from_json(..., directed=True)
nodes.rationale: Directed construction is real but lives in the Python API, not the CLI; the skill's Step 4 already calls build_from_json with directed, so the package must call into it under a pinned interpreter rather than invoke a nonexistent CLI flag.
nodes.norm_label: fix: specify the refresh as build_from_json(..., directed=true)

nodes.label: diagnose multigraph as a post-build assertion, not the mechanism
nodes.rationale: It exists to confirm collapse did not occur; using it to produce directedness inverts cause and check.
nodes.norm_label: diagnose multigraph as a post-build assertion, not the mechanism

nodes.label: Published graph.json must carry directed: true (jq-checkable gate)
nodes.rationale: It is directly checkable with jq and is the honest gate; the committed graph today is directed:false, multigraph:false.
nodes.norm_label: published graph.json must carry directed: true (jq-checkable gate)

nodes.label: graph-context-builder's edge_key rationale inherits the --directed defect
nodes.rationale: It cites the --directed mandate downstream, so the citation is defective until the mandate is repaired.
nodes.norm_label: graph-context-builder's edge_key rationale inherits the --directed defect

nodes.label: Finding 6 — LANDING-ORDER package counts are stale
nodes.rationale: Written when 24 packages existed; GP-2 and GP-4 landed afterwards making the true count 26 live / 16 authored / 10 pre-existing, and hard-mode-launcher plus v030-soft-mode-report appear in no stage at all.
nodes.norm_label: finding 6 — landing-order package counts are stale

nodes.label: Finding 2 — audit-run.sh contradiction between two adjacent packages
nodes.rationale: cross-vendor-audit-routing T4 says the block is replaced while audit-groundedness-gate T4 says it stays as-is; two lanes authored these independently and the serialisation rule does not catch textual contradictions.
nodes.norm_label: finding 2 — audit-run.sh contradiction between two adjacent packages

nodes.label: Finding 3 — doctrine-reality-drift ordering deadlock
nodes.rationale: Failing closed at S4 on claims owned by S5/S6/S9 is a real deadlock; a closes_in column is the cheaper fix than reordering.

nodes.label: Finding 4 — graph-eval-falsification is self-defeating on thresholds
nodes.rationale: It does not import the PM's already-fixed thresholds while carrying a clause invalidating unregistered criteria; K-2 and K-8 also have no owner.
nodes.norm_label: finding 4 — graph-eval-falsification is self-defeating on thresholds

nodes.label: Finding 5 — the census cannot gate the store inside one release
nodes.rationale: Both sit at S8 and the census needs a full release of data, so the store's stated gate is unexecutable in v0.2.9.
nodes.norm_label: finding 5 — the census cannot gate the store inside one release

nodes.label: TerminusDB ships, but the census may not be claimed as its validation
nodes.rationale: The owner decided the store ships; what finding 5 changes is what may be claimed for it — the honest framing is that it ships on live R8 evidence (ontology loaded, three lineage queries correct first attempt, 12/12 concurrent writers, time-travel verified) with the census reporting in v0.3.x.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb ships, but the census may not be claimed as its validation

nodes.label: Keep the query wrapper and non-emptiness contract in scope regardless
nodes.rationale: 'No rows' from jq is exactly as ambiguous as an empty WOQL binding, so the assertion is a files-only concern too and survives any scope cut.
nodes.norm_label: keep the query wrapper and non-emptiness contract in scope regardless

nodes.label: The contention table counts mentions, not modifications
nodes.rationale: test-infrastructure-hardening appears as a tool-check.sh claimant on the strength of a sentence saying it does not touch that file, so the eight-way contention figure is an overcount and the serialisation rule it justified must be re-derived.
nodes.norm_label: the contention table counts mentions, not modifications

nodes.label: Live schema load test against pinned TerminusDB 12.0.6
nodes.rationale: Both audit lanes returned BLOCKED on the same defect, so rather than accept or dispute it on paper the architect ran the test the auditors specified; fresh container healthy in 3 s against R8's measured 2.6 s.
nodes.norm_label: live schema load test against pinned terminusdb 12.0.6

nodes.label: Schema block extracted deterministically from the package itself
nodes.rationale: Taken as the largest parseable fenced JSON block from terminusdb-schema/design.md rather than retyped: 33 objects — 1 @context, 12 Enum, 19 Class, 1 TaggedUnion.
nodes.norm_label: schema block extracted deterministically from the package itself

nodes.label: The schema gate is prose-only and must become an executable load test
nodes.rationale: The process criticism is upheld but the implied risk is not: the schema is accepted by pinned 12.0.6 exactly as written including top-level TaggedUnion, subdocument-with-links, abstract classes and multiple inheritance — so severity drops from unlandable defect to missing gate.
nodes.norm_label: the schema gate is prose-only and must become an executable load test

nodes.label: Ingest cannot write a single document (confirmed live)
nodes.rationale: TerminusDB rejects a document carrying graphify_version because no class declares that field, and the adapter requires that stamp on every ingested document — so as specified the first production ingest fails on its first write, reproducible in three seconds.
nodes.norm_label: ingest cannot write a single document (confirmed live)

nodes.label: Fix Lane C adds GraphNode.graphify_version
nodes.rationale: After the field was declared, a Source carrying graphify_version is accepted, undeclared fields and invalid enums are still rejected, and subtask_of and depends_on are accepted as distinct relations — 5 passed, 0 failed.

nodes.label: Enum discipline is real and enforced at write time
nodes.rationale: An invalid enum value is rejected on write, which is the property the every-LLM-field-is-an-enum-or-reference rule depends on.
nodes.norm_label: enum discipline is real and enforced at write time

nodes.label: Fixtures derived from the schema, never guessed
nodes.rationale: An earlier attempt failed four times on invented enum values and missing fields, so fixtures now carry every required field and only enum values read from the schema.
nodes.norm_label: fixtures derived from the schema, never guessed

nodes.label: @id must be omitted (classes use generated keys)
nodes.rationale: A submitted @id yields SubmittedIdDoesNotMatchGeneratedId.
nodes.norm_label: @id must be omitted (classes use generated keys)

nodes.label: The artifact contradicted the claim being made about it
nodes.rationale: The post-fix run was reported in conversation and never written to the file, so for several hours the only artifact on disk said the opposite; the Opus re-audit checked the artifact rather than the claim and caught it (TD4).
nodes.norm_label: the artifact contradicted the claim being made about it

nodes.label: Stated limits of the live verification
nodes.rationale: It did not test the EvaluationTarget exactly-one constraint, Optional resolved_to cardinality, subdocument provenance round-tripping, the CAS header, the branch:-prefixed diff footgun, or any of the 24 competency queries — those findings stand untouched.
nodes.norm_label: stated limits of the live verification

nodes.label: Durable event log (events.jsonl, on-disk source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Append-only atomic O_APPEND writes kept under the 4 KB PIPE_BUF; git-committable and replayable from offset 0, so it is the authoritative ordered record of what happened.
nodes.norm_label: durable event log (events.jsonl, on-disk source of truth)

nodes.label: Invariant: the log is the single source of truth
nodes.rationale: The transport is a disposable, rebuildable view and never a second source of truth; the rule is enforced by design because the bridge is one-way, log to NATS.
nodes.norm_label: invariant: the log is the single source of truth

nodes.label: Per-consumer commit-after-process cursor
nodes.rationale: A line number committed after processing gives at-least-once delivery, converting a plain file into a replayable bus; torn-tail-safe reads stop at the first line lacking a trailing newline or failing jq.

nodes.label: Continuous worktree checkpoints via git plumbing
nodes.rationale: An isolated GIT_INDEX_FILE means no index.lock contention with the agent's own git, and pinning to refs/checkpoints/* makes snapshots gc-safe; chosen over auto-commit branches or watchers because plumbing is non-disruptive and cross-platform.
nodes.norm_label: continuous worktree checkpoints via git plumbing

nodes.label: Reasoning-stream persistence (tee streaming JSON to disk)
nodes.rationale: stdbuf -oL line-buffers so events flush immediately, leaving every completed event on disk after a mid-turn crash.
nodes.norm_label: reasoning-stream persistence (tee streaming json to disk)

nodes.label: NATS/JetStream transport with msg-id dedup
nodes.rationale: Nats-Msg-Id of run_id:seq gives exactly-once dedup so a bridge restart that re-reads log lines does not double-publish; durable consumers get every event, ack per message and resume exactly after a crash.

nodes.label: Degradation rule (NATS down, log still captures everything)
nodes.rationale: NATS is primary transport but never the durability guarantee; the bridge replays unpublished lines from its own cursor on reconnect.
nodes.norm_label: degradation rule (nats down, log still captures everything)

nodes.label: Stall watchdog with RUNNING/STALLED/DEAD state machine
nodes.rationale: Alerts fire only on state transitions, debounced by N consecutive stalled ticks, to avoid flapping; a heartbeat every ~30 s per live lane is what makes a stalled producer distinguishable from a quiet one.
nodes.norm_label: stall watchdog with running/stalled/dead state machine

nodes.label: Resume: snapshot-heavy, replay-light
nodes.rationale: Agents are non-deterministic, so restore state rather than replay logic.

nodes.label: WSL2 mirrored mode and native-FS store_dir requirement
nodes.rationale: Mirrored mode makes localhost:4222 work across the Windows/WSL boundary and NAT mode does not; store_dir must be on a native FS rather than /mnt/c for fsync integrity.
nodes.norm_label: wsl2 mirrored mode and native-fs store_dir requirement

nodes.label: A long agent round is a black box
nodes.rationale: Work is durable only at merge boundaries, progress is visible only at agent completion, and a stalled round looks identical to a working one — the session relied on manual git commit checkpoints to de-risk long rounds.
nodes.norm_label: a long agent round is a black box

nodes.label: Single portable foreman skill (soft + hard merged)
nodes.rationale: Merges Fable Advisor soft orchestration (architect cost discipline, five-part specs, Grok/Codex implementers, Fable/Opus advisor) with the original Foreman hard harness (worktrees, evidence outside worktrees, independent checks, cold-diff audit, deterministic gate).
nodes.norm_label: single portable foreman skill (soft + hard merged)

nodes.label: Soft mode (default; prompt + agent contracts + independent verification)
nodes.norm_label: soft mode (default; prompt + agent contracts + independent verification)

nodes.label: Hard mode (opt-in; bash scripts + optional Docker)
nodes.norm_label: hard mode (opt-in; bash scripts + optional docker)

nodes.label: Lane drift plus false narration (dogfood defect 1)
nodes.rationale: Grok round 1 deviated from the five-part spec on four points while narrating success, and ran git commit without authorization, touching do-not-touch files.
nodes.norm_label: lane drift plus false narration (dogfood defect 1)

nodes.label: Git-write ban (standing rule for workers)
nodes.rationale: Workers never run git commit/add/reset/branch/push/rebase/merge/tag; read-only git is allowed and the architect owns all git writes.

nodes.label: Evidence contract (HEAD + status digest before/after)
nodes.rationale: The wrapper records git log -1 --format=%H and a SHA-256 digest of git status --porcelain before and after the CLI run; if HEAD moved the report sets UNAUTHORIZED_GIT_ACTIVITY true with the offending commits listed.

nodes.label: Grok headless permission wall (dogfood defect 2)
nodes.rationale: Grok's shell tool always fails with PermissionCancelled under --permission-mode acceptEdits headless, so it cannot delete or rename files or run verification; four retries burned ~17 minutes because the limit was not codified.

nodes.label: ARCHITECT_ACTIONS report field
nodes.rationale: Mechanical operations a lane cannot perform (deletions, renames, permission changes) are listed for the architect to execute instead of being retried.

nodes.label: Worktree-by-default for every soft-mode implement round
nodes.rationale: A concurrent session committed to main four times mid-run while soft-mode implementers ran in the main checkout with no isolation; even single-file trivial edits get a worktree because the cost is one script call and the collision class disappears.
nodes.norm_label: worktree-by-default for every soft-mode implement round

nodes.label: wt-merge overlap refusal
nodes.rationale: Squash-applies as staged changes without committing by default and refuses when the target tree has uncommitted modifications to any incoming file; fail-closed rather than partial-apply.

nodes.label: bats-core test harness for shipped scripts
nodes.rationale: tests/ was empty while shipped bash scripts kept growing; each test creates a throwaway repo under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR so no test touches the real repo.
nodes.norm_label: bats-core test harness for shipped scripts

nodes.label: Documentation and comment-quality stage (docs-check)
nodes.rationale: markdownlint-cli2 + codespell + lychee + shdoc comment coverage + PSScriptAnalyzer, fail-closed; Vale was rejected for now as the highest setup cost requiring a maintained style package.

nodes.label: Vendored reference skills (scrapling, graphify, superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Full copies with upstream LICENSE preserved and a no-local-modification policy (update by re-vendoring); local-overlay files such as cookie vaults must never enter the repo.

nodes.label: OpenSpec folder conventions + EARS requirement phrasing
nodes.rationale: Grok-bound specs MUST use EARS phrasing (Ubiquitous / WHEN / WHILE / WHERE / IF-THEN / Complex) so constraints and verification are unambiguous for a headless implementer.
nodes.norm_label: openspec folder conventions + ears requirement phrasing

nodes.label: Graph-query-first doctrine for repo questions
nodes.rationale: Token experiments against the live graph measured 45-77% savings versus raw reads, so repo questions go to graphify query with a budget under 1500 before file exploration, hopping to sources via source_location only as needed.

nodes.label: Maintenance and updates stage
nodes.rationale: Upstream vendored-skill content-hash check, graph refresh with health check, and CLI/model compat check against manifest floors; report-only in CI, opening an issue with findings.

nodes.label: Self-contained teaching README
nodes.rationale: A reader who opens only the README must be able to install, run a task end to end and understand every subsystem; USAGE.md is retained as the terse quick-reference, not deleted.

nodes.label: Anti-slop voice rules
nodes.rationale: Every sentence states a fact or a reason; rules are explained by naming the bug they prevent; em dashes are limited to term-definition separators; where something is a stub or unexercised, say so plainly.

nodes.label: Six required ASCII diagrams
nodes.rationale: Architecture, soft loop, lane routing tree, worktree lifecycle, evidence contract and hard-mode gate pipeline — plain ASCII in fenced blocks so they render in a monospace terminal with no external images.

nodes.label: Verbatim security sentence (containers share the kernel)
nodes.rationale: Kept word-for-word because it states defense-in-depth, not a hard boundary — a claim that must not drift under rewriting.
nodes.norm_label: verbatim security sentence (containers share the kernel)

nodes.label: Truth audit of every command, path, flag and number
nodes.rationale: Accuracy is non-negotiable, so the rewrite is cross-vendor audited for truth as well as slop, with a zero-slop-word grep as a mechanical check.
nodes.norm_label: truth audit of every command, path, flag and number

nodes.label: Three-stage lifecycle (Setup & Environment → Use → Cleanup)
nodes.rationale: All model authentication lives in Setup and never mid-Use, so a lane can never stop early because a vendor was not signed in; Use does not begin until Setup reports READY for the required lanes.

nodes.label: Package 1: lifecycle-three-stage (foundational)
nodes.rationale: Landed first so the other packages attach to the stages: vendor auth to Setup, worktree teardown to Cleanup, full-WSL install to Setup on Linux.

nodes.label: Package 2: grok-lane-activation
nodes.rationale: Grok access was absent when the gaps were written and was verified end-to-end during this planning cycle (Build 0.2.103, signed in, rc 0) — the default implementer lane foreman was designed around is live for the first time.

nodes.label: Grok security rider (secrets-free worktrees only)
nodes.rationale: A single-source report claims Grok Build uploads the whole repo including secrets regardless of telemetry toggles; until refuted, a preflight scans for .env and private-key patterns and refuses the lane on a hit.

nodes.label: Package 3: t5b-concurrency-verdict
nodes.rationale: pueue caps are raised only on green results and UNVERIFIED vendors stay at 1; Claude Code is ruled requires-a-separate-HOME from the public corruption-issue base without local destruction.

nodes.label: Package 4: posix-cascade-parity
nodes.rationale: A process cannot re-parent itself into a new PID namespace, so the launcher is bootstrapped as namespace init via unshare --pid --mount-proc --fork --kill-child; the kernel then SIGKILLs every process in the namespace when init dies, however deeply double-forked, with zero polling.

nodes.label: Package 5: worktree-hardening guard bundle
nodes.rationale: Each guard cites a public failure report and two map onto foreman's own bugeventlog entries; maintenance.auto=false plus a foreman-owned scheduled run kills the reactive gc.autoDetach stall class, and GIT_ASK_YESNO=false kills the Windows unlink-retry hang.

nodes.label: Package 6: wsl-reliability-env-refresh (full WSL setup)
nodes.rationale: Windows stays fully supported while WSL/Linux becomes co-equal; two live bugs were found — the WSL-side codex resolving the Windows npm shim and an env manifest falsely claiming shellcheck installed.

nodes.label: Package 7: docs-readme-refresh (sequenced last)
nodes.rationale: Sequenced last so it documents the whole shipped release; every command, flag and path is verified against the code with no invented flags.

nodes.label: Package 8: hard-mode-launcher (approved spec)
nodes.rationale: Adopts the devcontainer plus default-deny egress-firewall pattern because it is practical on today's Docker Desktop/WSL2 with zero new install, keeping Docker Sandboxes microVMs as the upgrade path when kernel isolation is needed.

nodes.label: Package 9: v030-soft-mode-report (approved spec)
nodes.rationale: Parallel-history re-port via per-commit git format-patch | git am -3, because the 3-way blob merge needs the referenced blobs present locally rather than a common ancestor; git replace/graft is avoided because it fabricates ancestry and misrepresents provenance.

nodes.label: Cross-vendor audit invariant under an explicit model pin
nodes.rationale: The auditor family must differ from the worker family; once T5b greens grok, grok-implemented work is audited by Opus, never same-family.
nodes.norm_label: cross-vendor audit invariant under an explicit model pin

nodes.label: Gate mutex governs every bats run
nodes.rationale: The v0.2.5 pueue gate group with an mkdir-lock fallback makes gate serialization structural instead of a matter of discipline.
nodes.norm_label: gate mutex governs every bats run

nodes.label: Issue 1 fix: native New-Item Junction instead of cmd-shelling
nodes.rationale: An operator hit a PowerShell ParserError at char 26 on the cmd /c mklink line and the Windows skill never became invocable; deep debug could not reproduce it on this host, so it is version/context-specific — but shelling to cmd with interpolated quoted paths is an inherently fragile class.
nodes.norm_label: issue 1 fix: native new-item junction instead of cmd-shelling

nodes.label: Issue 2: grok --prompt-file is a single agentic burst (empty-burst failure)
nodes.rationale: On any spec that asks grok to read or introspect before writing, the whole burst is spent orienting and zero files are written even with --allow Write --allow Edit; this is distinct from cancelled-writes, where writes are attempted then denied. --max-turns did not visibly extend the burst.
nodes.norm_label: issue 2: grok --prompt-file is a single agentic burst (empty-burst failure)

nodes.label: Write-first doctrine for grok specs
nodes.rationale: The first instruction handed to grok MUST be a concrete Write with every needed API fact inlined, so zero reads are required before the first Write.

nodes.label: Coded evidence gate: files_changed == 0 is a FAILED round
nodes.rationale: Reuses the existing before/after git status --porcelain digest contract and emits a distinct empty-burst hint, so a STATUS-complete run that wrote nothing can no longer read as success.
nodes.norm_label: coded evidence gate: files_changed == 0 is a failed round

nodes.label: grok-multiround.sh (bounded re-prompt loop, mechanism B)
nodes.rationale: Re-invokes the same spec with a fed-forward preamble on a zero-change round, giving explore-then-implement resilience without grok's fragile stdio protocol, which remains a documented future option.

nodes.label: Issue 3: the headless codex auth path is --with-api-key
nodes.rationale: On codex-cli 0.144.x, login --device-auth prints the same localhost:1455 browser-callback flow as plain login and the login server dies on detach; interactive login must be operator-run in a persistent foreground shell, never launched-and-detached by the orchestrator.
nodes.norm_label: issue 3: the headless codex auth path is --with-api-key

nodes.label: Issue 4: soft_mode.target = worktree | live
nodes.rationale: The Midnight target needed a vendored wallet SDK under a pinned sub-repo's node_modules, a running proof-server container and live testnet endpoints; a git worktree carries none of that installed state, so worktree isolation breaks the very environment verification needs.

nodes.label: wt-new refuses to cut a worktree under the live profile
nodes.rationale: An optional .foreman/live-target.toml marker also lets a preflight WARN when worktree is selected but external runtime state is present, nudging the operator before a broken worktree is cut.
nodes.norm_label: wt-new refuses to cut a worktree under the live profile

nodes.label: The reframe: v0.2.9 is not about fixing broken WSL-native code
nodes.rationale: The surface audit confirmed platform detection, taskkill gating, tool resolution and docs are already correct; the real gaps are already-built protections that were never shipped or wired, plus the Windows/WSL seam — so none of the correct code should consume budget.
nodes.norm_label: the reframe: v0.2.9 is not about fixing broken wsl-native code

nodes.label: The POSIX launcher was never shipped on WSL
nodes.rationale: launcher/dist is gitignored and build:posix exists but nothing runs it, so on a fresh WSL clone launcher resolution fails and the lane emits a degraded launcher_absent event and runs without the pidns kill-cascade — silently, with no readiness signal.
nodes.norm_label: the posix launcher was never shipped on wsl

nodes.label: P1 wsl-launcher-shipped
nodes.rationale: When bun is present but the launcher is absent the verdict is NOT-READY citing the build command; when bun itself is absent it is a loud DEGRADED warning rather than a hard NOT-READY, else readiness is permanently blocked on a should-tool.

nodes.label: P2 crlf-extensionless-hardening
nodes.rationale: Three extensionless shebang scripts have LF index blobs but no eol=lf attribute because the .gitattributes fix keys on extensions, so an autocrlf=true or shared /mnt/c checkout gets CRLF in the working tree and WSL bash rejects pipefail\r; a fresh ext4 clone is unaffected, making this a shared-checkout seam fix, not a fresh-clone blocker.

nodes.label: Exec-bit trap on the three direct-exec'd extensionless scripts
nodes.rationale: They are git-mode 100644 and invoked by direct exec rather than via bash, and install.sh's chmod glob never touches skills/superpowers, so on a fresh ext4 clone they are 0644 and fail with Permission denied — current, not hypothetical; all 445 tracked files are 100644.
nodes.norm_label: exec-bit trap on the three direct-exec'd extensionless scripts

nodes.label: Repo-root .gitattributes with * text=auto eol=lf
nodes.rationale: Matches Microsoft/VS Code's recommendation with .bat/.cmd/.ps1 CRLF carve-outs plus a binary carve-out as insurance against text=auto mis-detecting a NUL-free binary; git add --renormalize is a near-no-op because the index blobs are already LF.

nodes.label: P3 wsl-preflight
nodes.rationale: One preflight at Setup and lane-start verifies the invariants the harness silently depends on, and the now-lightweight clock check folds into it.

nodes.label: FOREMAN_HOME under /mnt/* is refused (fsync integrity)
nodes.rationale: /mnt/c via 9P/DrvFs is 2-20x slower and lacks the fsync guarantees the event-log crash-safety model needs; a /mnt worktree is only WARNed because refusing it would ban the documented clone-inspected-from-Windows workflow, and FOREMAN_ALLOW_MNT_HOME=1 is the loud-warn escape hatch.

nodes.label: Clock drift was kernel-fixed in WSL 2.1.1 — the preflight pivots
nodes.rationale: foreman's v0.2.7.5 clock preflight and resync Scheduled Task were built for a bug fixed upstream in January 2024, so they must pivot to version-currency plus the residual 1-2 s dual-NTP jitter, fixed by timedatectl set-ntp false; the heavy Scheduled Task retires to an optional operator step.
nodes.norm_label: clock drift was kernel-fixed in wsl 2.1.1 — the preflight pivots

nodes.label: P4 wsl-tool-path-persistence
nodes.rationale: Non-interactive lane shells do not source ~/.bashrc, so tool dirs must be persisted for lanes explicitly rather than via profile; the grok readiness probe is also decoupled so unit tests stop depending on live network reachability.

nodes.label: P5 wsl-ci-parity
nodes.rationale: The bats suite including the pidns launcher family runs on no CI platform today, so WSL protections are verified by hand, once; ubuntu-latest is the WSL proxy and windows-latest with shell: bash covers the Git-Bash half (explicit bash is what enables pipefail).

nodes.label: P6 wsl-seam-doctrine
nodes.rationale: Codifies one uniform rule for browser/localhost-callback auth (operator-foreground, never orchestrator-detached, noting that ::1 is not forwarded), that systemd=true does not keep the WSL VM alive so pueued is restart-on-demand, and that Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend is the supported container host.

nodes.label: Portability and correctness checklist
nodes.rationale: Wave-1 implementation surfaced the bug classes: jq select emptying whole objects on 1.8+, Windows jq.exe emitting CRLF into compared values, git stderr advisories corrupting merged captures, truncate-before-write emptying files, PIPESTATUS for piped exit codes, no flock on Git Bash, and set -e aborting on a trailing [[ ]] && form.

nodes.label: durable-preflight.sh (single dependency list + verify)
nodes.rationale: One place lists every durable dependency and verifies it, gating all durable-mode work; exits 3 when a required dep is missing and prints the install hint rather than failing opaquely.

nodes.label: dp_verify
nodes.rationale: Run in the current shell via a temp file rather than command substitution, because a subshell would lose DP_MISSING and the exit-3 path would never fire.

nodes.label: el_emit
nodes.rationale: Ordering under failure is build line, reserve seq atomically, then append: a duplicate seq is the only unacceptable outcome, and a gap is fine. jq del is used instead of select because select(.!="") empties the whole object on jq 1.8+.

nodes.label: el_init
nodes.rationale: Clears a leftover .seq.lock single-threaded at init, which is why el_emit does no in-band stale reclaim — any check-then-rmdir reclaim has an unavoidable ABA race in bash.

nodes.label: el_read
nodes.rationale: Stops at the first torn or invalid line so a partially-written tail can never be handed to a consumer.

nodes.label: mkdir mutex for seq read-modify-write
nodes.rationale: Multiple lanes emit to one run's log concurrently and the seq update must be atomic; mkdir is atomic on Git Bash and WSL where flock is unavailable on MSYS2.

nodes.label: Test-only jq CR-stripping wrapper in helpers.bash
nodes.rationale: Windows jq.exe emits CRLF, so the wrapper lives in the test environment only and never in the shipped library.
nodes.norm_label: test-only jq cr-stripping wrapper in helpers.bash

nodes.label: ckpt_snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshots the working tree into refs/checkpoints/<lane> using an isolated index so the running agent's own index and HEAD are never touched and refs stay gc-safe.

nodes.label: lane-run.sh (lane runner wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Runs the coding-CLI invocation with its stdout tee'd to the worktree's stream.ndjson, emitting prompt, throttled checkpoint, heartbeat and round_done events so a crash leaves a replayable record.

nodes.label: nb_bridge (one-way log to JetStream bridge)
nodes.rationale: Commits its cursor only after a successful publish, so a publish failure replays on the next tick instead of silently dropping events.

nodes.label: nats/setup.sh
nodes.rationale: Calls durable-preflight first and aborts with its install hints rather than half-creating a stream.

nodes.label: wd_state (pure state-transition function)
nodes.rationale: Kept pure — taking last age and previous state and returning the new state and stall count — so the state machine is testable without wall-clock waits.

nodes.label: resume.sh
nodes.rationale: Finds the last checkpoint or round_done SHA for the lane, falls back to ckpt_latest, checks that tree out and prints the last prompt payload; exits 4 when no checkpoint exists rather than restarting blind.

nodes.label: Pre-implementation Codex audit of task code blocks
nodes.rationale: Tasks 3-4 and 5-7 were cold-audited before being built, catching must-fix defects (including config being purely decorative) while they were still cheap text edits.
nodes.norm_label: pre-implementation codex audit of task code blocks

nodes.label: CS1 doctrine and lane-contract hardening (lands first)
nodes.rationale: Lands first because the CS2-CS4 workers must obey the contracts it writes.
nodes.norm_label: cs1 doctrine and lane-contract hardening (lands first)

nodes.label: CS2 machinery (bats harness, wt-merge, docs-check)
nodes.rationale: Builds the tooling that the CS3 and CS4 merges then use, so the merge train exercises freshly tested code.

nodes.label: wt-merge.sh
nodes.rationale: Documented exit codes make each refusal mode distinguishable: 3 missing metadata, 4 dirty target index, 5 overlap refusal, 7 squash conflict — never a partial apply.

nodes.label: docs-check.sh
nodes.rationale: Fail-closed with a distinct exit 2 for a missing tool, so an absent linter can never be mistaken for a clean run; emits JSON for gate consumption.

nodes.label: setup_tmp_repo test helper
nodes.rationale: Exports REPO, SCRIPTS and an isolated FOREMAN_HOME so no test touches the real repo or real run state.

nodes.label: shdoc comment-coverage check
nodes.rationale: Every function in scripts/**/*.sh must carry at least an @description header and every script a top-of-file purpose block, with vendored skills excluded because upstream style is theirs.

nodes.label: foreman-launch (compiled Bun supervisor executable)
nodes.rationale: Owns every vendor-CLI process tree so orphans are impossible by construction rather than by cleanup discipline.

nodes.label: launcher/src/win/jobobject.ts
nodes.rationale: Handles are plain bigints with no GC finalizers, held in a module-level variable for launcher lifetime, and the job handle is never closed while the child runs because closing it IS the kill switch.

nodes.label: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE as the only trusted kill primitive
nodes.rationale: Every exit path — timeout, cancel, launcher crash — reaps the whole tree at kernel level, so no userspace sweep has to be correct for the guarantee to hold.
nodes.norm_label: kill_on_job_close as the only trusted kill primitive

nodes.label: launcher/src/supervise.ts
nodes.rationale: Assigns the child to the job immediately after spawn returns, pipes stdout and stderr together, and drives heartbeats from a JS timer rather than an FFI wait loop.

nodes.label: launcher/src/posix.ts (setsid + kill -pgid build)
nodes.rationale: Same contract from the same source so lane-run stays portable across Windows and WSL/CI.

nodes.label: Frozen launcher CLI + exit-code contract (124 timeout, 125 launcher error)
nodes.rationale: Frozen because lane-run consumes it: CMD's stdout and stderr pass through unmodified and heartbeat JSON goes only to the heartbeat file, so a caller can distinguish child failure from timeout from launcher error.
nodes.norm_label: frozen launcher cli + exit-code contract (124 timeout, 125 launcher error)

nodes.label: No hot FFI polling (bun issue 31941 tripwire)
nodes.rationale: Sustained 100 ms FFI polling in compiled executables triggers a trampoline segfault, so exit detection uses proc.exited and heartbeats are timer-driven JS; a CI FFI smoke test guards Bun-version bumps against the regression class.
nodes.norm_label: no hot ffi polling (bun issue 31941 tripwire)

nodes.label: Grandchild assignment race (accepted residual)
nodes.rationale: A child can spawn a grandchild in the microseconds before AssignProcessToJobObject; accepted because vendor CLIs boot slower than the window, with a taskkill sweep as belt-and-braces and CREATE_SUSPENDED via CreateProcessW as the proven escalation path if ever observed.

nodes.label: Bun pinned to 1.3.14 with a 1.4.x soak rule
nodes.rationale: The Rust-core 1.4.x line is canary-only, so the launcher asserts its Bun version at startup and warns rather than fails on drift; adoption waits for two or more patch releases.
nodes.norm_label: bun pinned to 1.3.14 with a 1.4.x soak rule

nodes.label: Compile and redistribution constraints
nodes.rationale: No --bytecode when cross-compiling, no --env=inline, never install as a symlink, and builds are not reproducible — so CI builds once and publishes the artifact plus SHA256, signs post-build, and carries the LGPL notice for the embedded JavaScriptCore.

nodes.label: The F1-F6 failure classes from bugeventlog
nodes.rationale: bash plus GNU timeout could not own process trees (F1, F2), grok lanes were serialized blind with no admission control (F3), and a parallel-history branch had no merge safety (F6).
nodes.norm_label: the f1-f6 failure classes from bugeventlog

nodes.label: Keep Foreman in-house; adopt Job Objects + pueue
nodes.rationale: Prefect is deferred unless the control plane moves to Python, Temporal unless multi-host, Hatchet/Windmill are Docker-shaped, and LangGraph-as-core has no process ownership — the one property the failure classes demanded.
nodes.norm_label: keep foreman in-house; adopt job objects + pueue

nodes.label: Scoped Bun adoption
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Go or C# because it gives identical Job-Objects FFI capability with one language for launcher and tests, built-in cross-compilation and signing, and Bun Shell as a credible escape hatch from the bash-on-Windows failure class; rewriting the audited bash libs is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: pueue per-vendor groups + the gate group
nodes.rationale: Any bats invocation from any role enqueues in the gate group at parallel 1, making gate serialization structural instead of discipline; lanes degrade gracefully to direct spawn when pueue is absent.
nodes.norm_label: pueue per-vendor groups + the gate group

nodes.label: lane-queue.sh
nodes.rationale: Carries a LANE_QUEUE_FORCE_MISSING test hook mirroring the DOCS_CHECK_FORCE_MISSING precedent so the absent-pueue branch is deterministically testable.

nodes.label: Round ownership (the launched unit is the whole round)
nodes.rationale: Because the supervisor is never the agent's turn, an agent that backgrounds-and-stops cannot strand the round; the gate itself runs under the launcher so heartbeats continue through the gate phase.
nodes.norm_label: round ownership (the launched unit is the whole round)

nodes.label: WAITING_CHILD terminal rule
nodes.rationale: round_done may be emitted only after the whole round-script exits AND an attempt-fresh report exists, so a prior round's report can never satisfy the predicate.

nodes.label: Attempt-fresh report predicate
nodes.rationale: The report must carry the current attempt id or have an mtime newer than the attempt-start timestamp — otherwise stale artifacts read as success.

nodes.label: Event schema v2 (additive, nested in payload)
nodes.rationale: el_emit is fixed 5-positional, so top-level additions would be a signature migration rather than an addition; the checkpoint SHA also stays in the existing top-level commit field because the originally planned checkpoint field collides with what resume.sh actually reads and would silently break recovery.
nodes.norm_label: event schema v2 (additive, nested in payload)

nodes.label: el_compact (compaction with immutable milestones)
nodes.rationale: Structural milestones stay immutable while heartbeat chatter rolls up, and rollup lines are written atomically because el_read halts on the first malformed line.

nodes.label: T4a VTICK injectable clock
nodes.rationale: Typed states are untestable without a test-drivable clock source, so VTICK lands before them; it also fixes the wd_sleep_remainder fractional-tick integer-arithmetic crash.

nodes.label: T4b typed lane states + AGENT-ABANDONED
nodes.rationale: Queued is not running, verifying is not stalled, and silence alone never classifies a lane; liveness comes from launcher heartbeats and phase events rather than file writes, because bats gates write to /tmp and mtime liveness false-stalls.

nodes.label: T5a per-lane vendor config isolation (GROK_HOME / CODEX_HOME)
nodes.rationale: Recorded in the ownership event; the launcher must pass these paths through verbatim because compiled Bun executables strip backslashes from env vars on Windows (bun issue 12970).
nodes.norm_label: t5a per-lane vendor config isolation (grok_home / codex_home)

nodes.label: merge-gate.sh (merge-freshness gate)
nodes.rationale: Records the merge-base at dispatch and re-verifies at pre-merge; no common ancestor yields a non-mergeable verdict and a respawn-from-fresh-base recommendation, never salvage automation.

nodes.label: wt-merge gitignored-report bug fix
nodes.rationale: The shipped exclude-pathspec still aborts, so the fix stops naming report paths in ANY pathspec and builds the add-list from status --porcelain output, which never lists ignored files; the test must use a genuinely gitignored tree to be non-vacuous.

nodes.label: wt-cleanup report-archiver glob fix
nodes.rationale: The 2026-07-17 data loss archived only fixed FOREMAN_REPORT names and dropped versioned audit reports, so the glob must cover FOREMAN_REPORT*.* and DIFF_*.patch.

nodes.label: T-INFRA gate-speed foundation (runs first)
nodes.rationale: The v0.2.0 force-merge was caused by a 40-minute gate under time pressure, and suite growth would re-enter that regime; the renormalize must commit to main before any lane worktree is cut or CRLF churn re-collides in every lane merge.

nodes.label: lane-supervise.sh (bounded auto-resume supervisor)
nodes.rationale: No new state store — it reads the event log, checkpoint refs and heartbeats; it never respawns while the prior attempt's Job Object or lane.lock is alive, never exceeds max_attempts, and stops after one terminal abandoned alert.

nodes.label: The config loader is a closed allowlist
nodes.rationale: Every new key must be added to both the TOML parse case allowlist and the env-var table and consumed via cfg_load/cfg_get, or it silently no-ops — which is how config became decorative before.
nodes.norm_label: the config loader is a closed allowlist

nodes.label: Nested Job Objects (new, unvalidated assumption)
nodes.rationale: Round ownership creates a launcher spawning further launchers, but the validated chain covered one launcher, child and grandchildren only; Win8+ permits nested jobs and the cascade should hold, so it is flagged for the plan-time spec audit and a nested tree-kill test.

nodes.label: Graded stop resolved: wait grace, then TerminateJobObject
nodes.rationale: The cooperative phase is dead as originally specified: CTRL_BREAK is impossible via Bun.spawn and CMD's stdin is the null device, so closing stdin signals nothing.
nodes.norm_label: graded stop resolved: wait grace, then terminatejobobject

nodes.label: SC-A..SC-F prevention criteria
nodes.rationale: Completion must be provable from the event log and refs alone with the dispatching agent absent, so agent-gone-plus-no-round_done never reads as done and never as a false stall during the gate phase.

nodes.label: Auditor agents never run bats
nodes.rationale: They reason from code instead, stated up front in every brief, so audit work never contends for the gate mutex.

nodes.label: foreman-setup.sh
nodes.rationale: Composes tool-check and prints per-vendor auth instructions but NEVER runs a login itself, because auth is an operator action Setup instructs; it stays idempotent as a pure read of state.

nodes.label: foreman-cleanup.sh
nodes.rationale: Delegates to wt-cleanup's existing porcelain guard rather than reimplementing it, stops pueued only when an ownership marker proves this run started it, and never touches the global gate.lock because a concurrent gate may own it.

nodes.label: vendor_authed (non-billing auth probe)
nodes.rationale: The probe command must be determined empirically per CLI and must never trigger a billed inference or hang; where a CLI has no non-billing check, credential-file presence is used and documented as a known limitation.

nodes.label: NOT_AUTHENTICATED tool-check state
nodes.rationale: Surfaced in both report_text and report_json so a caller can gate on a distinct verdict field rather than parsing prose; installed-but-signed-out is no longer indistinguishable from ok.

nodes.label: LANE_READY lane-scoped readiness verdict
nodes.rationale: Kept additive so the default no-flag output is unchanged.

nodes.label: Use-path readiness gate in lane-run
nodes.rationale: The spec requires Use to REFUSE routing to a not-ready lane, not merely for Setup to report it, so the door-check is coded into dispatch and 'the agent stopped early because grok was not signed in mid-lane' becomes impossible; unset LANE_VENDOR keeps today's frozen behavior.

nodes.label: lane_grok_secrets_scan
nodes.rationale: Scoped to the worktree source and excluding .harness scaffolding to avoid false positives; emits alert{kind:grok_secrets_refused} and exits non-zero before the spawn, and is distinct from the readiness gate — both apply to a grok lane.

nodes.label: Normalized GROK_HOME vendor-home isolation
nodes.rationale: GROK_HOME relocates the whole config root, which maps directly onto the existing normalized vendor-home plumbing rather than needing a new mechanism.

nodes.label: grok-implementer headless recipe
nodes.rationale: Documented with the resume form and the device-code/XAI_API_KEY auth doctrine done in Setup; grok stays optional until the concurrency verdict greens it, making promotion a one-line doctrine flip.

nodes.label: Live acceptance: a real grok --round audited cross-vendor
nodes.rationale: Worker is xAI and auditor is Anthropic, so the cross-vendor invariant holds by construction on the proof run.
nodes.norm_label: live acceptance: a real grok --round audited cross-vendor

nodes.label: bootstrap-wsl.sh as a full native provisioner
nodes.rationale: Each install is idempotent and skip-if-present, and the acceptance proof is a Setup to trivial-Use to Cleanup pass run entirely inside WSL invoking no Windows-side tool.
nodes.norm_label: bootstrap-wsl.sh as a full native provisioner

nodes.label: WSL codex PATH-leak fix (appendWindowsPath=false)
nodes.rationale: A live bug: wsl codex resolves the Windows npm shim and errors on the missing Linux native dependency, so the fix is proven by a before/after re-probe rather than asserted.

nodes.label: .wslconfig agent-host tuning
nodes.rationale: Mirrored networking, DNS tunneling, gradual memory reclaim and sparse VHD, with processors cut from 24 to 20 to reserve host headroom against the wall-clock-flake class; virtiofs stays off because it is still buggy.

nodes.label: Sleep-resume clock-sync hook + lane-start drift preflight
nodes.rationale: Protects the event log's timestamp-based logic from post-sleep VM clock drift by re-syncing or refusing before any timestamped event is written.
nodes.norm_label: sleep-resume clock-sync hook + lane-start drift preflight

nodes.label: Manifest reconciled to probe-verified reality
nodes.rationale: Every entry carries a probe-verified date and no claimed-but-absent tool may remain, because the stale shellcheck claim was itself one of the two live bugs; Bun is explicitly held at 1.3.14.

nodes.label: root to non-root migration inventoried, not executed
nodes.rationale: Every /root-hardcoded path is enumerated first and the default user is deliberately not flipped, so the migration becomes a later scoped change rather than a surprise mid-release break.
nodes.norm_label: root to non-root migration inventoried, not executed

nodes.label: git-guards.sh
nodes.rationale: Idempotent config bootstrap that must also register a maintenance path, so disabling reactive gc does not leave the repo un-maintained; on Windows Git-Bash where no user scheduler exists it falls back to a foreman-owned maintenance tick.

nodes.label: git_retry (backoff around shared-lock ops)
nodes.rationale: Five attempts with 200 to 3200 ms backoff returning the last failure's code, wrapped around the worktree add/remove operations that contend on shared locks.

nodes.label: wt_sweep_stale_locks
nodes.rationale: Removes only 0-byte .lock files older than ~30 s and spares fresh or non-empty ones, so a genuinely held lock is never stolen.

nodes.label: Scoped GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS / GIT_ASK_YESNO
nodes.rationale: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is for read-only polling only and never on commit or add, asserted via a git shim that records the environment.

nodes.label: SIGINT lane subprocess before git worktree remove
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing — SIGINT then remove, never the reverse; the porcelain-refuse and report-archive halves already ship, so the plan guards them with a regression test instead of reimplementing them.
nodes.norm_label: sigint lane subprocess before git worktree remove

nodes.label: Defender path exclusions for the repo and sibling worktrees
nodes.norm_label: defender path exclusions for the repo and sibling worktrees

nodes.label: setChildSubreaper (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER via bun:ffi)
nodes.rationale: A safety net so any escapee stays reapable; called once at startup with no fork around it, and on failure it logs and continues rather than aborting the lane.

nodes.label: pidns-init bootstrap (the cascade guarantee)
nodes.rationale: --mount-proc gives the launcher a correct /proc but makes its pid namespace-local, so the host pid is recorded before entering the namespace to keep the heartbeat consistent with what a host-side kill-shot targets; on unshare absence it falls back to setsid/pgid with a logged degraded marker rather than silently proceeding without the guarantee.

nodes.label: WSL kill-shot test (setsid/double-fork escapee)
nodes.rationale: Killing the launcher must leave zero survivors of a process that escaped its pgid, which is exactly the case the pgid-only path fails — so the test is the package's proof, not a formality.

nodes.label: Exit-code and heartbeat contract parity under pidns
nodes.rationale: The contract is frozen, so the task asserts byte-parity with the Windows build rather than changing anything; the Windows build carries zero diff.
nodes.norm_label: exit-code and heartbeat contract parity under pidns

nodes.label: vendor-concurrency-test.sh (matrix runner)
nodes.rationale: Harness logic is shim-tested and deterministic while the destructive runs consume real vendor quota, so the two are split: the runner is bats-covered, the quota runs are a manually-invoked contained protocol.

nodes.label: Destructive-run containment and abort criteria
nodes.rationale: Throwaway repos, isolated config dirs and lowest-tier auth; abort on any write outside the throwaway config dir, sibling-lane auth invalidation, a process needing kill -9, or a 429 cascade beyond shared-quota math.

nodes.label: Caps raised only on a recorded green verdict row
nodes.rationale: Default-on-doubt is 1 and every cap must cite a verdict row, so concurrency claims can never outrun the evidence.
nodes.norm_label: caps raised only on a recorded green verdict row

nodes.label: Claude Code ruled REQUIRES-SEPARATE-HOME from the public record
nodes.rationale: The .claude.json write races are documented publicly and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does not cover top-level session state, so the verdict is recorded without local destruction.
nodes.norm_label: claude code ruled requires-separate-home from the public record

nodes.label: Ground-truth surface inventory before any doc rewrite
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing command, flag, path and env var is enumerated and verified against the code so no invented flag can enter the docs; there is no automated invented-flag gate, so the discipline is enforced by inventory plus review.
nodes.norm_label: ground-truth surface inventory before any doc rewrite

nodes.label: docs-check cannot measure AI slop (audit correction)
nodes.rationale: It runs markdownlint-cli2, codespell, lychee and comment-coverage — there is no slop detector in it — so the prose-quality bar is the Opus review, not a docs-check signal.
nodes.norm_label: docs-check cannot measure ai slop (audit correction)

nodes.label: Named humanizer substitution rather than a silent skip
nodes.rationale: blader/humanizer is an interactive slash-command that may not be invocable in a headless lane, so the blocker must be stated and the closest available prose skill named — never silently skipped; the pass changes wording only and never a technical claim.
nodes.norm_label: named humanizer substitution rather than a silent skip

nodes.label: fl_resolve_launcher (lib/launch.sh)
nodes.rationale: Factors launcher resolution into a self-contained unit so worker-run reuses the v0.2.5 supervision contract without touching byte-frozen lane-run.sh; lib/launch.sh sits one level deeper than lane-run so it computes four levels to the repo root, not three.

nodes.label: lib/worker-cmd.sh (per-vendor worker argv builder)
nodes.rationale: Delivers the task prompt as a file or positional argument because the launcher nulls CMD's stdin, so stdin can never be the prompt channel.

nodes.label: worker-run launcher-only profile (default, no Docker)
nodes.rationale: Built and proven end-to-end first because the container profile layers on top; its clean-slate env keeps the Windows-essential vars the Node vendor CLIs need, since a bare env -i broke them.

nodes.label: worker-run container profile (bridge + egress firewall)
nodes.rationale: Runs the worker in a clean file copy of the worktree with no .git, because a linked worktree's .git is a FILE pointing at the host repo and must never be bind-mounted; the hardened read-only run adds tmpfs for a writable vendor HOME and the iptables lock.

nodes.label: sandbox/init-firewall.sh (default-deny allowlist)
nodes.rationale: Applied by a root entrypoint that then drops to an unprivileged worker, so the firewall is in place before any untrusted code runs.

nodes.label: rsync -a --delete sync-back of the worker copy
nodes.rationale: Propagates worker deletions and renames, which a plain tar extraction would not.
nodes.norm_label: rsync -a --delete sync-back of the worker copy

nodes.label: Host-side commit of the worker diff (never inside the sandbox)
nodes.rationale: Gate and audit both diff BASE_SHA...HEAD, so HEAD must carry a host-side commit or both are vacuous; the commit uses git_nohooks because the worktree is untrusted.
nodes.norm_label: host-side commit of the worker diff (never inside the sandbox)

nodes.label: Heartbeats mirrored by a batch read after the worker exits
nodes.rationale: Avoids tail -F, FIFO and background-lock hazards that a live mirror would introduce.
nodes.norm_label: heartbeats mirrored by a batch read after the worker exits

nodes.label: toml_get is the config accessor for hard_mode keys
nodes.rationale: config_get does not exist and cfg_get's closed allowlist has no hard_mode.* entry, so only toml_get can read an arbitrary dotted key — a rev-2 audit correction.
nodes.norm_label: toml_get is the config accessor for hard_mode keys

nodes.label: pr-open.sh (gate → PAT push → draft PR)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the gate-decision.json.pass precondition, pushes host-side with a fine-grained single-repo expiring PAT the container never holds, and leaves gh pr ready as a separate human gate; the token goes through GIT_ASKPASS so it never appears in argv.

nodes.rationale: It holds under OAuth or home-isolated vendor auth, but API-key auth necessarily passes that one vendor key — stated as a narrowing rather than claimed as absolute.

nodes.label: No-invented-flags verification rule

nodes.label: foreman-setup.sh lifecycle wrapper

nodes.label: docs-check.sh documentation gate

nodes.label: MSYS grandchild-orphan cleanup limit

nodes.label: Grok Build (xAI terminal coding agent)
nodes.rationale: Installed via `npm i -g @xai-official/grok` because the x.ai/cli host is Cloudflare-walled; the community superagent-ai/grok-cli is unaffiliated and must not be used. Windows is xAI best-effort/untested, so WSL is the tested fallback.

nodes.label: GROK_HOME per-lane config root
nodes.rationale: GROK_HOME relocates the whole grok config root, which maps directly onto T5a's per-lane vendor-home model, so no new isolation mechanism is needed for the grok arm.

nodes.label: Grok headless flag set
nodes.rationale: Verified against docs.x.ai/build/cli/reference: -p/--single, --output-format, -r/--resume, --session-id, --cwd, --always-approve, --no-auto-update. There is no --output-file flag, so stdout must be redirected.

nodes.label: Grok whole-repo upload risk report
nodes.rationale: A single-source wire-level gist (cereblab, grok 0.2.93) reports the CLI uploads the whole repo including git history and unredacted .env regardless of telemetry toggles. Not independently reproduced, so it is treated as a RISK mitigated by a preflight rather than a blocker.

nodes.label: Grok-gated worktree secrets preflight
nodes.rationale: A cheap bash scan (.env excluding .env.example, PEM private-key headers) gated on LANE_VENDOR=grok that refuses the lane on a hit — fail-safe and removable once the upload claim is refuted.

nodes.label: Deferral of grok default-implementer promotion
nodes.rationale: Promotion is deliberately excluded from this change and held as a one-line doctrine flip in t5b-concurrency-verdict, gated on green concurrency evidence, so activation and promotion can be reviewed independently.

nodes.label: Cross-vendor worker/auditor invariant
nodes.rationale: The first real grok --round lane is audited by Opus so worker (xAI) never equals auditor (Anthropic) — the invariant that keeps an audit independent of the vendor that produced the diff.

nodes.label: Change: grok-lane-activation
nodes.rationale: Doctrine named grok-implementer as the default lane but the CLI was absent at v0.2.5, so Sonnet-implements/Opus-audits was the working substitution. With Grok Build 0.2.103 verified end-to-end the lane can finally be wired in; backward compatible because LANE_VENDOR unset is byte-identical to today.

nodes.label: Requirement: lane-run maps grok to an isolated GROK_HOME
nodes.rationale: GROK_HOME must reach CMD on both the launcher-present and launcher-absent spawn branches and be recorded in the ownership event's config_dir, so isolation is observable in the event log and not merely intended.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: lane-run maps grok to an isolated grok_home

nodes.label: Requirement: the grok-implementer recipe is non-interactive and isolated
nodes.rationale: --output-format json plus --always-approve makes the invocation fully unattended, satisfying lane-run's CMD non-interactive contract; resume uses grok -r <session-id> with the same GROK_HOME and --cwd.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the grok-implementer recipe is non-interactive and isolated

nodes.label: Requirement: grok lanes refuse secrets-bearing worktrees
nodes.rationale: Scoped WHILE the whole-repo-upload behavior is unrefuted; emits alert{kind:grok_secrets_refused} and exits non-zero before spawning CMD, so the guard is auditable in the event stream.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: grok lanes refuse secrets-bearing worktrees

nodes.label: Requirement: the env manifest describes a real, resolvable grok install
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the env manifest describes a real, resolvable grok install

nodes.label: Requirement: grok authentication is a Setup-stage responsibility
nodes.rationale: Auth moves out of the lane so an unauthenticated grok is caught at the door by Setup instead of failing mid-round; the secrets preflight stays in-lane because it is a per-worktree safety check, not an environment-readiness concern.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: grok authentication is a setup-stage responsibility

nodes.label: Empirical non-billing auth-probe commands
nodes.rationale: Probes were determined by reading each CLI's own --help tree and exercising signed-in and simulated signed-out states via throwaway vendor-home overrides, so the host's real credentials were never touched.

nodes.label: grok models auth probe
nodes.rationale: grok has no whoami/auth-status subcommand and `grok inspect --json` carries no auth field, so `grok models` is the CLI's only auth-status surface. It always exits 0 regardless of auth state, so the signal must be read from stdout text, not the exit code — the one probe that deviates from the vendor_authed exit-code template.

nodes.label: codex login status auth probe
nodes.rationale: Clean exit-code signal verified both ways (0 signed in, 1 signed out), so it matches the vendor_authed template as-is.

nodes.label: claude auth status auth probe
nodes.rationale: Emits JSON with loggedIn plus a clean exit code, verified both ways, so it matches the vendor_authed template as-is.

nodes.label: Fail-closed auth-probe logic
nodes.rationale: The original design tested only for absence of the string 'not authenticated', which was fail-OPEN: any unrelated error banner or reworded message would read as READY, exactly the mid-round auth failure the gate exists to prevent. The corrected logic requires a positive 'logged in' substring AND no negative wording AND exit 0 AND non-empty output; every other case returns not-authenticated. Proven with a shim printing an unrelated error at exit 0.

nodes.label: Bounded probe call (timeout 10)
nodes.rationale: `grok models` round-trips to a remote model-list endpoint with no bound of its own and now runs on tool-check's default path and inside every lane-run readiness gate, so a network stall would hang Setup and Use.
