Wrapped in timeout 10 (gtimeout fallback); if neither is resolvable the probe refuses the unbounded call and reports not-authenticated. Verified against a sleep-60 shim.

nodes.label: Non-billing probe constraint
nodes.rationale: No probe may invoke -p/exec/agent or any model turn, so readiness checks never consume vendor quota; grok -p and grok agent were never invoked during probe determination.

nodes.label: Three-stage foreman lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The stages COMPOSE existing machinery rather than replacing it — an organizing frame, not a rewrite — and the same lifecycle runs on Windows and WSL. It is foundational for v0.2.7.5: other packages attach their content to a stage.

nodes.label: Setup & Environment stage
nodes.rationale: tool-check with auth probes, then bootstrap, then vendor auth, then WSL provisioning, ending in READY/NOT-READY; idempotent so a re-run on a provisioned host changes nothing.

nodes.label: Use stage (orchestration loop)
nodes.rationale: The existing soft-mode loop preceded by a readiness assertion keyed on the lanes the task will use; Use never authenticates, so lapsed auth surfaces at the door rather than deep inside a round.

nodes.label: Cleanup stage (ordered teardown)
nodes.rationale: Ordered and idempotent: SIGINT lane subprocs, wt-cleanup with porcelain check and archive, gate-lock/owned-pueued release, stale-lock sweep — so an interrupted teardown can be completed by a re-run.

nodes.label: Machine-readable readiness verdict
nodes.rationale: Extends tool-check's MISSING/OUTDATED vocabulary with NOT-AUTHENTICATED plus a lane-scoped READY, so a caller can ask 'is the grok lane ready?' and gate on the answer. The probe must verify auth works, not merely that a token file or env var exists.

nodes.label: Make failure structural, not discipline-dependent
nodes.rationale: Generalizes the v0.2.5 process-ownership lesson to the whole run: rather than each lane discovering missing tools or lapsed auth mid-round, a Setup gate proves readiness once, Use assumes it, and Cleanup guarantees teardown.

nodes.label: Change: lifecycle-three-stage
nodes.rationale: Foreman interleaved setup, auth, the loop and teardown ad hoc; auth in particular was discovered mid-run. Same class of problem the v0.2.5 prevention work attacked for process ownership, and the fix is a defined lifecycle with a gate between stages.

nodes.label: Requirement: foreman operates in three ordered stages
nodes.rationale: Stages must be independently invocable and must compose the existing tool-check/bootstrap/wt-cleanup/lane-supervise scripts rather than replacing them, so adoption is additive.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: foreman operates in three ordered stages

nodes.label: Requirement: Setup owns all model authentication
nodes.rationale: Where a key is accepted, Setup must verify the key actually authenticates via a minimal probe rather than checking that the variable is set — otherwise a stale key reads as READY.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: setup owns all model authentication

nodes.label: Requirement: Setup emits a machine-readable readiness verdict
nodes.norm_label: requirement: setup emits a machine-readable readiness verdict

nodes.label: Requirement: Cleanup runs a deterministic teardown set
nodes.rationale: Ordering is mandated and idempotence is required so an interrupted Cleanup can be re-run; a worktree with uncommitted work is never deleted unless forced, and reports are archived first.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: cleanup runs a deterministic teardown set

nodes.label: Requirement: SKILL.md documents the lifecycle as the operating frame
nodes.norm_label: requirement: skill.md documents the lifecycle as the operating frame

nodes.label: PID-namespace init cascade
nodes.rationale: Chosen as primary because the kernel SIGKILLs every process in a namespace when its init dies — zero polling, kernel-guaranteed, and probed to work unprivileged on WSL2 (unshare --user --pid --fork --kill-child ran without CAP_SYS_ADMIN). A process cannot self-enter a new pidns, so the launcher must be bootstrapped under an outer unshare wrapper.

nodes.label: --kill-child reverse edge (PDEATHSIG)
nodes.rationale: Ties the forked child's death to unshare's own death, closing the reverse edge so a dying wrapper cannot leave an orphaned launcher; reproduced live by killing unshare and observing its sleep child die.

nodes.label: PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER safety net
nodes.rationale: Additive only — it reparents but never kills — so it keeps escapees reapable/discoverable without being load-bearing. Rests on Bun's documented libc-dlopen pattern rather than a direct test, which is why it is not the primary guarantee.

nodes.label: cgroup.kill fallback (cgroup v2)
nodes.rationale: Atomic whole-cgroup SIGKILL confirmed on this WSL, but it needs an external writer on launcher death, so it is a documented fallback rather than the primary mechanism; delegation to a non-root user was not probed.

nodes.label: systemd-run --scope --collect fallback
nodes.rationale: Scopes tear down on explicit kill or command exit but NOT on unrelated-parent death, so it buys graceful per-session kill and observability, not a crash guarantee.

nodes.label: setsid + kill(-pgid) graceful fast path
nodes.rationale: Retained as the graceful fast path and the degraded fallback when unshare is unavailable, but it cannot catch a double-fork/setsid escapee, which is the gap pidns closes.

nodes.label: Change: posix-cascade-parity
nodes.rationale: v0.3.0 will run vendor-CLI sessions on WSL through the POSIX build, so the previously-documented POSIX/Windows asymmetry becomes load-bearing and must be closed. Adds a runtime dependency on unshare (util-linux, present in Ubuntu), degrading gracefully where absent.

nodes.label: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE parity goal
nodes.rationale: The Windows build gets kernel-guaranteed whole-tree kill from Job Objects by construction, including on launcher crash; the POSIX target is the true Linux analog of that guarantee, not a polling imitation.

nodes.label: WSL kill-shot escapee test
nodes.rationale: The package's SC-style proof: CMD spawns a setsid double-fork escapee, the launcher is killed, and the test asserts zero survivors plus a correctly downgrade-logged fallback when unshare is forced absent.

nodes.label: Requirement: the POSIX launcher runs as PID-namespace init
nodes.rationale: When unshare is unavailable or fails, the launcher must fall back to setsid+pgid AND log an operator-visible degraded marker — never silently proceed without the guarantee, because a silent downgrade is indistinguishable from safety.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the posix launcher runs as pid-namespace init

nodes.label: Requirement: a subreaper safety net keeps escapees reapable
nodes.rationale: One-shot prctl on the launcher's own thread with no fork around it; on failure the launcher continues and logs, because the pidns bootstrap is the primary guarantee and the subreaper is additive.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a subreaper safety net keeps escapees reapable

nodes.label: Requirement: exit-code and heartbeat contract is unchanged
nodes.rationale: Freezes exit code = child's / 124 timeout / 125 launcher error and the heartbeat schema {ts,launcher_pid,pid,job_id,alive,stdout_bytes,stderr_bytes,elapsed_s}, so the pidns bootstrap is invisible to every existing consumer.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: exit-code and heartbeat contract is unchanged

nodes.label: Requirement: launcher README documents the closed asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Must carry the honest note that the guarantee requires unshare and that the fallback ladder needs systemd/cgroup-v2 availability, so 'closed' is never read as unconditional.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: launcher readme documents the closed asymmetry

nodes.label: CODEX_HOME isolation and codex concurrency limits
nodes.rationale: CODEX_HOME isolates config/auth/logs/sessions/skills, but codex is designed single-user-per-instance: concurrent instances collide on ports 3000/8000/8080 with kill/restart loops, Computer Use degrades above ~4 parallel, and quota is a shared per-account pool. Confidence med-high.
nodes.norm_label: codex_home isolation and codex concurrency limits

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does not isolate ~/.claude.json
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates ~/.claude but not the top-level ~/.claude.json holding OAuth/session/MCP state, so a separate $HOME per instance is the real fix. Documented write-race corruption plus a per-version-dir lock that freezes a second instance; confidence high enough to settle the verdict without local destruction.

nodes.label: Grok isolation scope undocumented
nodes.rationale: GROK_HOME is documented but whether it isolates sessions or only settings is not; the CLI is closed-source with a changelog mentioning leader-election and past concurrent-writer bugs. Confidence low, which is precisely why grok needs a real destructive run.

nodes.label: Destructive concurrency matrix harness
nodes.rationale: Spins N throwaway lanes with isolated config dirs and throwaway repos, collects the signals and writes verdict rows. Runs under the gate mutex like any lane, but the destructive runs sit outside the normal suite as a manually-invoked protocol because they consume real vendor quota.

nodes.label: Change: t5b-concurrency-verdict
nodes.rationale: T5a shipped vendor-config isolation plumbing but left the destructive N>1 verdict unverified because the grok CLI was absent; caps stayed at 1 as a result. With grok installed the matrix can finally run.

nodes.label: Evidence-gated pueue cap raising
nodes.rationale: Safety-first: no cap is raised without a recorded green verdict row, and the default posture on any doubt is to keep the cap at 1.

nodes.label: Requirement: the destructive matrix runs under strict containment
nodes.rationale: Throwaway repos, per-instance isolated config dirs and lowest-tier auth, with production auth never reused across simultaneous lanes; explicit abort triggers (kill -9 needed, a write outside the throwaway dir, sibling auth invalidation, 429 cascade beyond shared-quota math) leave the cap at 1.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the destructive matrix runs under strict containment

nodes.label: Requirement: a green verdict requires all assertions to hold at N
nodes.rationale: A cap may never exceed a proven-green N; any failed assertion makes that N RED and the cap stays at the last green value (default 1).
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a green verdict requires all assertions to hold at n

nodes.label: Requirement: Claude Code ruled REQUIRES-SEPARATE-HOME from public evidence
nodes.rationale: The public corruption record (.claude.json write races; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR not covering top-level session state) is strong enough that a local destructive run would add risk without adding information.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: claude code ruled requires-separate-home from public evidence

nodes.label: Requirement: results are recorded and gate cap changes
nodes.rationale: Every cap change in lane-queue.sh/config must cite its corresponding green verdict row, so a cap can always be traced back to the evidence that justified it.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: results are recorded and gate cap changes

nodes.label: Requirement: grok promotion is gated on a green grok verdict
nodes.rationale: The doctrine flip is a single reviewable edit citing the verdict; if grok's run is RED or aborted, grok stays an optional lane and doctrine stays unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: grok promotion is gated on a green grok verdict

nodes.label: index.lock contention under parallel lanes
nodes.rationale: Root cause is that worktrees share one object DB and index-lock domain (62% failure at 13 agents per claude-code#55724); guards are git_retry backoff plus never auto-deleting a dirty tree. Confidence high.

nodes.label: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 on read-only polls
nodes.rationale: Killed background `git status` pollers took the optional lock and left a stale 0-byte lock blocking all later commands, so polls must not take the lock at all — but write ops must still take it, hence the strict scoping.

nodes.label: maintenance.auto=false plus scheduled git maintenance
nodes.rationale: gc.autoDetach silently forks a background gc that competes for the lock and causes random multi-second mid-commit stalls; replacing reactive gc with a foreman-owned scheduled maintenance run removes the stall without leaving the repo un-maintained.

nodes.label: GIT_ASK_YESNO=false unlink-prompt guard
nodes.rationale: Windows open handles from Defender/MCP/indexer during rename or unlink produce an endless 'Unlink failed. Try again?(y/n)' hang; auto-declining plus Defender exclusions and killing subprocs before removal turns a hang into a clean failure.

nodes.label: Windows path and filesystem guards
nodes.rationale: core.longpaths=true plus short worktree names address Windows MAX_PATH 'Filename too long'; core.fsmonitor and core.untrackedCache address slow status/checkout where no FS watcher exists. Confidence medium on MSYS path-rewrite and fsmonitor sizing.

nodes.label: wt_with_lock worktree serialization
nodes.rationale: lib/worktree.sh already serializes add/remove via flock with an operator-visible 'flock missing' WARN fallback, so this change deliberately adds the missing config/env guards rather than a second lock.

nodes.label: Guards derived from foreman's own bugeventlog
nodes.rationale: Two guards trace to foreman's own incident log rather than external research: the porcelain-check-before-delete (2026-07-17 report-loss) and kill-subprocess-before-remove (2026-07-16 orphan/shutdown-ordering failure).
nodes.norm_label: guards derived from foreman's own bugeventlog

nodes.label: Change: worktree-hardening
nodes.rationale: Targets the operator's reported active pain (stalls and git failures under heavy concurrent worktree use on Windows/Git Bash); guards are additive and scoped so the change is backward compatible.

nodes.label: git-guards.sh idempotent config bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Applies repo config inherited by all worktrees and registers the scheduled maintenance path, reporting which settings it applied so the guard state is observable.

nodes.label: git_retry bounded-backoff wrapper
nodes.rationale: Transient index.lock contention is expected under parallel lanes, so a bounded exponential backoff around shared-lock ops turns a first-attempt failure into a completed op instead of an aborted lane; retry counts are heuristic (low confidence).

nodes.label: Stale-lock sweep at lane start
nodes.rationale: Only 0-byte locks older than ~30s are removed, so a lock a live git process may hold (non-zero size or recent mtime) is never swept; each removal is logged.

nodes.label: wt-cleanup porcelain check and shutdown ordering
nodes.rationale: Porcelain status must be checked before any delete so uncommitted work is never destroyed, and lane subprocesses must be SIGINTed before `git worktree remove`, never after — the exact 2026-07-16 ordering failure.
nodes.norm_label: wt-cleanup porcelain check and shutdown ordering

nodes.label: Windows Defender path-exclusion doctrine
nodes.rationale: Real-time scanning of .git/VHDX is a measured cause of stalls and unlink failures, so the repo and all sibling *-wt-* worktree dirs are excluded.

nodes.label: Concurrent-lane soak proof
nodes.rationale: Spinning N concurrent worktree lanes and asserting zero stale-lock stalls and no dirty-delete is the package's SC-style proof, because the failure class only appears under real concurrency.

nodes.label: Requirement: the repo carries the concurrency-safe git config
nodes.rationale: Disabling reactive gc must not leave the repo un-maintained: while maintenance.auto is false a maintenance path (scheduled task or foreman tick) must exist so pack/ref hygiene still occurs.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the repo carries the concurrency-safe git config

nodes.label: Requirement: lanes scope optional-lock and yes/no env vars
nodes.rationale: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is forbidden on commit/add/write paths; a write that fails on a lock is the retry wrapper's job, not the env var's.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: lanes scope optional-lock and yes/no env vars

nodes.label: Requirement: shared-lock operations retry with bounded backoff
nodes.rationale: Bounded at 5 attempts with 200 to 3200 ms exponential backoff and failure returned only after the last attempt, so a lane never aborts on a first transient index.lock failure yet also cannot retry forever.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: shared-lock operations retry with bounded backoff

nodes.label: Requirement: stale locks are swept before a lane starts
nodes.norm_label: requirement: stale locks are swept before a lane starts

nodes.label: Requirement: wt-cleanup never destroys uncommitted work and orders shutdown
nodes.rationale: Untracked report files must be archived by the existing FOREMAN_REPORT*.* archiver and the tree must not be deleted without a passing porcelain check or --force; a dirty target exits non-zero with a clear message rather than proceeding.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: wt-cleanup never destroys uncommitted work and orders shutdown

nodes.label: Requirement: Defender exclusion doctrine is documented
nodes.norm_label: requirement: defender exclusion doctrine is documented

nodes.label: WSL /mnt/c PATH leak
nodes.rationale: 62 /mnt/c PATH entries make WSL-side `codex` resolve the Windows npm shim, which then crashes on the missing @openai/codex-linux-x64 native dep; appendWindowsPath=false is preferred over PATH reordering because reordering leaves the shim reachable.

nodes.label: .wslconfig agent-host tuning
nodes.rationale: processors=24 on a 24-logical-CPU host reserves zero host headroom, which is the wall-clock-flake class; mirrored networking + dnsTunneling buy localhost/VPN interop; autoMemoryReclaim=gradual beats dropcache; virtiofs is not GA so it stays a throwaway-distro trial.

nodes.label: Post-sleep WSL clock-sync hook
nodes.rationale: WSL's clock freezes across S0 sleep (GH #10006), which directly threatens foreman's timestamp-ordered event log; a resume-triggered `hwclock -s` plus a lane-start preflight is cheaper than making the event log clock-independent.

nodes.label: Dependency hold/upgrade reconciliation table
nodes.rationale: Bun is held at 1.3.14 because 1.4 is canary-only and the 2-patch soak rule is unmet; gh is upgraded for security fixes; WSL npm 9.2.0 against node 22 is an anomaly to reprovision via fnm.

nodes.label: Root-to-non-root user migration (inventory only)
nodes.rationale: Flipping the WSL default user breaks every hardcoded /root/... path and every root-owned install, so the change is inventoried here and executed in its own audited pass.

nodes.label: Probe-evidence acceptance for config work
nodes.rationale: Host/WSL config is hard to unit-test, so each requirement's scenario is re-probed and the output pasted, and the manifest is diffed against live --version output rather than trusted.

nodes.label: WSL as a co-equal foreman environment
nodes.rationale: Making WSL first-class (not just the POSIX helper) makes the pidns launcher and the v0.3.0 session-transport lanes native and gives Linux users a supported install path; Windows stays fully supported.
nodes.norm_label: wsl as a co-equal foreman environment

nodes.label: Live bug: WSL codex resolves the Windows shim
nodes.norm_label: live bug: wsl codex resolves the windows shim

nodes.label: Live bug: reference-manifest.toml claims an absent shellcheck
nodes.rationale: The manifest asserted an install date for a tool present on neither side — a declared-state-versus-measured-reality divergence that only a live probe catches.
nodes.norm_label: live bug: reference-manifest.toml claims an absent shellcheck

nodes.label: Requirement: WSL is a fully-provisioned co-equal environment
nodes.norm_label: requirement: wsl is a fully-provisioned co-equal environment

nodes.label: Requirement: WSL codex resolves to a native install
nodes.norm_label: requirement: wsl codex resolves to a native install

nodes.label: Requirement: .wslconfig is tuned for an agent host
nodes.norm_label: requirement: .wslconfig is tuned for an agent host

nodes.label: Requirement: the event log survives post-sleep clock drift
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the event log survives post-sleep clock drift

nodes.label: Requirement: shellcheck and WSL bats-core are actually present
nodes.norm_label: requirement: shellcheck and wsl bats-core are actually present

nodes.label: Requirement: dependency versions reconciled to verified currency
nodes.norm_label: requirement: dependency versions reconciled to verified currency

nodes.label: Requirement: the root-to-non-root migration is inventoried, not executed
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the root-to-non-root migration is inventoried, not executed

nodes.label: Devcontainer + egress-firewall sandbox pattern
nodes.rationale: Adopted rather than invented: it is the lightest 2026 SOTA pattern practical on today's Docker Desktop/WSL2, with Docker Sandboxes microVMs as the kernel-isolation upgrade path.

nodes.label: Worktree file copy, not a read-only bind mount
nodes.rationale: A linked worktree's .git is a file pointing back at the host repo, so binding it exposes the host repo; a clean `git archive` copy synced back with rsync -a --delete keeps the container off the canonical tree.
nodes.norm_label: worktree file copy, not a read-only bind mount

nodes.label: Egress-capable bridge narrowed by default-deny allowlist
nodes.rationale: `--network none` would block the vendor API and git-remote traffic the worker legitimately needs, so the network stays capable and is narrowed by init-firewall.sh instead of disabled.
nodes.norm_label: egress-capable bridge narrowed by default-deny allowlist

nodes.label: gh pr create with --body-file, not -b
nodes.rationale: -F/--body-file (accepting -) is the researched correct form; passing a body string with -b is named the #1 gh automation anti-pattern. A fine-grained expiring single-repo PAT replaces classic PAT/GITHUB_TOKEN.

nodes.label: Post-ship spec reconciliation of the network wording
nodes.rationale: The folder's original 'network default none' wording predated implementation; once the shipped code settled on the researched pattern the EARS text was corrected rather than left to contradict the code.
nodes.norm_label: post-ship spec reconciliation of the network wording

nodes.label: Launcher-only hard-mode profile (default)
nodes.rationale: Made the default so hard mode works with zero new install on top of the v0.2.5 launcher; the launcher + worktree + vendor-home isolation is the sandbox, and Docker is not required.

nodes.label: Requirement: worker-run supervises the worker through foreman-launch
nodes.norm_label: requirement: worker-run supervises the worker through foreman-launch

nodes.label: Requirement: pr-open pushes only after the gate and only host-side
nodes.norm_label: requirement: pr-open pushes only after the gate and only host-side

nodes.label: Requirement: secrets and mounts follow least privilege
nodes.norm_label: requirement: secrets and mounts follow least privilege

nodes.label: Closed-world check
nodes.rationale: A set-membership, range-containment or structural-implication test over artifacts Foreman itself produced; its answer is determined by its inputs, so it carries no probability and can be made structurally incapable of a false positive.

nodes.label: Open-world check
nodes.rationale: Asks whether evidence supports a claim; accuracy is a measured percentage (88-94% precision at best), so at ~40 merges/week a 93%-precision blocker false-blocks roughly three correct merges weekly and teaches the operator to route around the gate.

nodes.label: Structural-zero-false-positive rule
nodes.rationale: A blocking check must be structurally incapable of a false positive, not merely measured at zero; if the spec cannot state the sentence that makes a false positive impossible the check is advisory, and no configuration value overrides this.

nodes.label: SHACL Core engine (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected on dependency weight plus measured engine disagreement: one engine called 41.1% of valid results invalid, pySHACL is 8500x slower than Jena, and the reference implementation fail-opened (Conforms: True, exit 0) on data violating every invariant. Only the addressed-record output shape is adopted.

nodes.label: Stratified Datalog with reified violations (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Technically strongest (P-complete, proof trees, derived predicates) but every engine is a C++/Rust/commercial dependency and no check here needs recursion; the recorded re-open condition is a constraint genuinely needing unbounded recursion.

nodes.label: Learned classifier over audit output (refused)
nodes.rationale: A refuse-list item: 95% accuracy is the same reliability band as the thing being disciplined, so a checker as unreliable as its subject adds cost and confidence without adding safety.

nodes.label: Shadow mode with measured promotion
nodes.rationale: Closed-world checks are 0% FP against the contract they are written to but not against the contract as the auditor actually uses it; the gap is measurable, so every check ships evaluated-but-non-blocking and is promoted only against a threshold declared before the measurement.

nodes.label: Validator canary
nodes.rationale: Proves the checks are able to fail, not that they are correct — the cheap claim. It runs per invocation rather than at build time because every observed fail-open was a runtime condition, and asserts expected count and focus because a checker reporting 'some violations' can report the wrong ones.

nodes.label: A validator that fails open is worse than no validator
nodes.rationale: Because the agents trust its verdict. Five tools showed the class and none of the instances was a bug — each was documented intended behaviour, which makes it a design constraint rather than a caution.
nodes.norm_label: a validator that fails open is worse than no validator

nodes.label: Conditional obligations split into one check per branch
nodes.rationale: A logical combinator reports at its own level and swallows the inner messages — the very strings that are the required_evidence — so each branch gets its own id, message and evidence sentence and combinators are never used.
nodes.norm_label: conditional obligations split into one check per branch

nodes.label: Provenance and citation gate, not a correctness gate
nodes.rationale: The predictable failure is a run producing beautifully-provenanced, fully-cited claims about a diff that does not work; every measured result says the symbolic layer passes that diff, so the gate output and PR body must state the scope in words.
nodes.norm_label: provenance and citation gate, not a correctness gate

nodes.label: What cannot be made symbolic
nodes.rationale: Published beside the checks so the gate's silence is not read as coverage: the oracle problem, evidence sufficiency, unwritten domain conventions, the Category D architectural residual, Category C runtime properties, and Category E spec defects.

nodes.label: G1 refinement: path resolves nowhere blocks, outside-diff warns
nodes.rationale: N4's 'every cited file resolves to a changed file' is 0% FP for the check but not for the contract: Foreman's auditor is deliberately given repo context and asked about regressions, so a finding about an impacted caller outside the diff is legitimate and blocking it would be a false positive.
nodes.norm_label: g1 refinement: path resolves nowhere blocks, outside-diff warns

nodes.label: G2 refinement: impossible line blocks, out-of-hunk warns
nodes.rationale: A line beyond the file's length cannot exist and is closed-world; a line inside the file but outside every changed hunk is the 'reviewed the file, not the diff' signal and stays advisory. line: 0 is a file-level finding and never a violation.
nodes.norm_label: g2 refinement: impossible line blocks, out-of-hunk warns

nodes.label: gate-ground.sh Tier-2 groundedness checker
nodes.rationale: Implemented as jq + git over JSON so the merge path of a bash+jq+git project gains no RDF, SHACL, Datalog or graph-store runtime dependency; it validates the audit artifact, never the code.

nodes.label: Hallucinated and self-contradictory audit output
nodes.rationale: The failure class gate-eval.sh cannot see today: nonexistent cited paths, lines past end-of-file, APPROVED alongside a critical finding, BLOCKED with an empty findings array. Each is closed-world — answerable from artifacts Foreman already produced.

nodes.label: Cross-vendor invariant checked at the wrong time
nodes.rationale: audit-run.sh:31-33 compares configured vendors at audit start, which says nothing about which auditor actually ran; a recorded device-auth failure caused an entire auditor substitution to Opus-in-session that no artifact recorded, so the invariant must be re-asserted at the gate against the record.
nodes.norm_label: cross-vendor invariant checked at the wrong time

nodes.label: Wave 1/2/3 check sequencing
nodes.rationale: Wave 1 needs nothing new, wave 2 adds two harness-written provenance fields, wave 3 needs a five-part-spec format change whose blast radius is outside the gate — so it is a separate wave rather than a wave-1 task.

nodes.label: Reified violation output artifact
nodes.rationale: One addressed record per violation carrying check, focus, path, message, required_evidence[], world and blocking; the output shape is borrowed from SHACL's report vocabulary while the engine that produced it is not, making the transform a projection rather than a translation.

nodes.label: Check registry and the two refusals
nodes.rationale: Ordered first because it is the doctrine; its twin refusals are that an open-world check cannot be configured enforcing and that a check with no promotion record runs in shadow regardless of configuration.
nodes.norm_label: check registry and the two refusals

nodes.label: Shadow measurement and promotion protocol
nodes.rationale: Names an owner and a release deadline for the wave-1 promotion decision, because a check parked in shadow forever is theatre.

nodes.label: Requirement: only closed-world checks may block a merge
nodes.norm_label: requirement: only closed-world checks may block a merge

nodes.label: Requirement: audit output is checked for internal coherence
nodes.norm_label: requirement: audit output is checked for internal coherence

nodes.label: Requirement: findings that cite nothing real are rejected
nodes.norm_label: requirement: findings that cite nothing real are rejected

nodes.label: Requirement: findings that cite impossible lines are rejected
nodes.norm_label: requirement: findings that cite impossible lines are rejected

nodes.label: Requirement: cross-vendor separation asserted against what actually ran
nodes.norm_label: requirement: cross-vendor separation asserted against what actually ran

nodes.label: Requirement: the rubric an audit claims is identified and resolvable
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the rubric an audit claims is identified and resolvable

nodes.label: Requirement: scope and criterion checks wait for the spec format
nodes.norm_label: requirement: scope and criterion checks wait for the spec format

nodes.label: Requirement: the checker proves it can fail before it is trusted
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the checker proves it can fail before it is trusted

nodes.label: Requirement: every check ships non-blocking and is promoted by measurement
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every check ships non-blocking and is promoted by measurement

nodes.label: Requirement: a check with a missing input is silent and counted
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a check with a missing input is silent and counted

nodes.label: Requirement: violations are addressed records naming their required evidence
nodes.norm_label: requirement: violations are addressed records naming their required evidence

nodes.label: Requirement: evidence sufficiency is advisory in this release
nodes.norm_label: requirement: evidence sufficiency is advisory in this release

nodes.label: Requirement: the gate states what the groundedness layer checks
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the gate states what the groundedness layer checks

nodes.label: Requirement: gate tiers escalate in order and short-circuit
nodes.norm_label: requirement: gate tiers escalate in order and short-circuit

nodes.label: Repo-root text=auto eol=lf catch-all
nodes.rationale: The correct SOTA fix rather than enumerating extensionless scripts by hand, because new extensionless shebang scripts will keep appearing and an extension-keyed allowlist cannot anticipate them; per-path rules for the three known files are kept as documentation matching the hooks/session-start precedent.

nodes.label: tests/line-endings.bats regression test
nodes.rationale: The executable proof the policy holds: it closes the declared-policy-versus-verified-reality gap so the .gitattributes rule and the actual working-tree bytes can no longer silently diverge.

nodes.label: Shared-checkout / autocrlf seam
nodes.rationale: The index blobs were never the bug — they are already i/lf. The defect only materializes where core.autocrlf=true (Git-Bash default, or a /mnt/c checkout read from WSL), so this is seam hardening rather than a fresh-clone blocker.

nodes.label: Exec-bit trap on directly executed scripts
nodes.rationale: The same three files are mode 100644 and invoked by direct exec, and install.sh's chmod glob never touches skills/superpowers/**, so on a fresh ext4 clone (where the CRLF bug does not reproduce) they fail with Permission denied instead.
nodes.norm_label: exec-bit trap on directly executed scripts

nodes.label: Requirement: bash-executed files are index-LF everywhere, working-tree LF on autocrlf checkouts
nodes.norm_label: requirement: bash-executed files are index-lf everywhere, working-tree lf on autocrlf checkouts

nodes.label: Requirement: binary files are protected from text=auto mis-detection
nodes.norm_label: requirement: binary files are protected from text=auto mis-detection

nodes.label: Requirement: every directly executed script is executable in the git index
nodes.rationale: The scope is an inventory, not a count: three documents gave three different numbers (34, 33, 3) and all were wrong; the set must be derived by a mechanical index sweep at the commit under test because a hardcoded count is what produced the contradictions.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every directly executed script is executable in the git index

nodes.label: Requirement: genuine Windows scripts remain CRLF
nodes.norm_label: requirement: genuine windows scripts remain crlf

nodes.label: Cross-vendor invariant expressed over model family
nodes.rationale: CLI identity was only ever a proxy for uncorrelated blind spots, adequate while every CLI mapped to one model family. Comparing families is the same amount of code as a gateway special case and does not need maintaining as vendors change shape.
nodes.norm_label: cross-vendor invariant expressed over model family

nodes.label: Gateway CLI (agy) serving multiple model families
nodes.rationale: agy's live model list spans Gemini, Anthropic and OpenAI-lineage models, so a name-based check passes worker=claude/auditor=agy while the auditor may literally be an Anthropic model reviewing an Anthropic model's work — the check satisfied and the property absent.
nodes.norm_label: gateway cli (agy) serving multiple model families

nodes.label: Fail closed on an unclassifiable model
nodes.rationale: The invariant now depends on a mapping Foreman maintains, so a model Foreman cannot classify is refused as an auditor with a named reason rather than assumed distinct; the cost is refusals when a vendor renames models, mitigated by keeping the mapping with the adapter.
nodes.norm_label: fail closed on an unclassifiable model

nodes.label: Enforcement at every tier from one shared point
nodes.rationale: Soft mode is the default and enforces nothing in code, so today's single enforcement point covers the minority of rounds. Soft mode has no spawn chokepoint, so enforcement moves to where the choice is recorded — an after-the-fact gate failure, an asymmetry the design accepts rather than pretending away.
nodes.norm_label: enforcement at every tier from one shared point

nodes.label: Ordered auditor preference list over architect judgement
nodes.rationale: A fresh architect decision is not reproducible, not reportable and not testable; a list with the worker vendor filtered out is deterministic and its output is a recordable fact. With four vendors and a race, substitution becomes routine, which is exactly when silent substitution turns dangerous.
nodes.norm_label: ordered auditor preference list over architect judgement

nodes.label: Dual audit specified but not defaulted
nodes.rationale: A nine-model seven-family panel delivers about two effective independent votes, individual top models matched the panel, aggregation closed at most 11% of the gap, and the cost side is a measured 15x tokens — a real cost for a small unmeasured benefit.
nodes.norm_label: dual audit specified but not defaulted

nodes.label: Escalate on auditor disagreement, never take the strictest verdict
nodes.rationale: Defaulting to strictest makes the system's verdict equal to its most pessimistic member, converting any auditor's false positive into a block and training the architect to override audits; escalation keeps the decision with a component that can read both verdicts and the diff.
nodes.norm_label: escalate on auditor disagreement, never take the strictest verdict

nodes.label: lib/audit-call.sh shared enforcement and selection point
nodes.norm_label: lib/audit-call.sh shared enforcement and selection point

nodes.label: Enforcement asymmetry: six prose statements, one code check
nodes.rationale: Six restatements of a rule are evidence the rule is not enforced, not evidence it is well documented; the routing matrix grows from 3x2 to 4x3 in this release while the number of places that check it stays at one.
nodes.norm_label: enforcement asymmetry: six prose statements, one code check

nodes.label: Removal of audit-run.sh's codex-only refusal
nodes.rationale: A vendor with no audit adapter should be rejected by the router at selection time with a named reason, not by a die() in the middle of an invocation builder.

nodes.label: Generalized post-audit worktree tamper assertion
nodes.rationale: Not waived for a vendor whose read-only mode is documented, because a documented mode is a control and not a proof — one vendor's plan mode is enforced by an in-process policy that still permits some writes.

nodes.label: Requirement: the auditor is selected from an ordered preference list
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the auditor is selected from an ordered preference list

nodes.label: Requirement: the cross-vendor invariant is expressed over model family
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the cross-vendor invariant is expressed over model family

nodes.label: Requirement: the invariant is enforced at every tier from one shared point
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the invariant is enforced at every tier from one shared point

nodes.label: Requirement: auditor selection and substitution are always reported
nodes.norm_label: requirement: auditor selection and substitution are always reported

nodes.label: Requirement: dual audit is available, opt-in, and escalates on disagreement
nodes.norm_label: requirement: dual audit is available, opt-in, and escalates on disagreement

nodes.label: Requirement: any configured auditor vendor may be invoked
nodes.norm_label: requirement: any configured auditor vendor may be invoked

nodes.label: Requirement: every audit asserts the auditor did not mutate the worktree
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every audit asserts the auditor did not mutate the worktree

nodes.label: Requirement: prose statements of the invariant cite the enforcing component
nodes.norm_label: requirement: prose statements of the invariant cite the enforcing component

nodes.label: Additive event-schema premise
nodes.rationale: el_emit treats type opaquely, payload is validated only as parseable JSON, is_collapsible matches only heartbeat, and the cursor is line-number based — so four new types and a payload key touch no library code. The premise is checked as task T1, not assumed; if false the change is a signature migration.

nodes.label: Frozen top-level event record shape
nodes.rationale: A top-level decision or usage field reads better but would touch every emit site plus el_read, el_read_after, el_compact, the NATS bridge, resume.sh's fallback and watch.sh's state machine; payload nesting buys the same expressiveness for none of that.

nodes.label: usage.source: vendor_reported / estimated / unavailable
nodes.rationale: The metric's companion number: for cost the misreading is 'cost fell' when what happened is 'fewer lanes reported usage'. A zero-cost round is indistinguishable from an unmeasured round in any aggregate, so an absent figure is recorded as absent and never as zero.

nodes.label: Metrics rollup derived by replay, never accumulated
nodes.rationale: A crashed run still replays correctly where an in-memory accumulator loses exactly the window Foreman most needs; replay makes the rollup reproducible evidence rather than an assertion; and it forces the events to be sufficient — a metric that cannot be derived from the log is a missing event, not a reason for a side channel.
nodes.norm_label: metrics rollup derived by replay, never accumulated

nodes.label: Guarded emission with a gate_decision asymmetry
nodes.rationale: A telemetry failure degrades the record and must never change a merge outcome — except that a failed gate_decision emit means the record of the decision is missing, so gate-decision.json records the emission failure and the record's incompleteness is itself in the record.
nodes.norm_label: guarded emission with a gate_decision asymmetry

nodes.label: Payloads carry references, never contents
nodes.rationale: The prompt event already stores the full joined command and a vendor CLI can be handed secrets; the event log not being mounted into worker sandboxes is not a reason to put prompt text, diff text or file contents in a payload.

nodes.label: Every metric ships with its companion number
nodes.rationale: A metric without a companion is a metric that will be gamed; any metric that gates anything gets gamed, so the companion that detects the common misreading is written into the spec rather than left to reporting discipline.
nodes.norm_label: every metric ships with its companion number

nodes.label: Sidecar decisions file (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A second lineage store would have no sequence allocation, no torn-tail contract, no cursor, no compaction and no tests, and would break the graph plane's join — rebuilding on purpose the join-by-string-convention defect the research names.

nodes.label: Foreman's deciding scripts never write to its lineage store
nodes.rationale: audit-run.sh and gate-eval.sh contain zero el_emit calls and never source lib/eventlog.sh, so the event vocabulary records in detail how lanes ran and nothing about what was decided; the model that reviewed a merged change appears only in a console line.
nodes.norm_label: foreman's deciding scripts never write to its lineage store

nodes.label: finding event type
nodes.rationale: One event per finding rather than an array inside the verdict, because that is what makes findings addressable, countable and joinable to their later upheld outcome; upheld is written null at audit time and recorded later as a new event so the append-only log is never rewritten.

nodes.label: usage event type for out-of-band figures
nodes.rationale: Some vendors report usage only after the process exits or on a separate channel, and attaching a figure late must not require holding a round open.
nodes.norm_label: usage event type for out-of-band figures

nodes.label: Structured model identity per round
nodes.rationale: Frontier behaviour drifts silently under a fixed alias with no version bump, and Foreman's routing and gate thresholds are calibrated to model behaviour — so identity is recorded as fields at round start rather than scraped from the joined command string, as the requested alias plus whatever version the CLI reports.

nodes.label: Requirement: audit decisions enter the event log
nodes.norm_label: requirement: audit decisions enter the event log

nodes.label: Requirement: findings are individually recorded and their outcome recorded later
nodes.norm_label: requirement: findings are individually recorded and their outcome recorded later

nodes.label: Requirement: gate decisions enter the event log
nodes.norm_label: requirement: gate decisions enter the event log

nodes.label: Requirement: decision events extend the vocabulary additively
nodes.norm_label: requirement: decision events extend the vocabulary additively

nodes.label: Requirement: recorded payloads carry references, never contents
nodes.norm_label: requirement: recorded payloads carry references, never contents

nodes.label: Requirement: token counts, cost and model identity are recorded per round
nodes.norm_label: requirement: token counts, cost and model identity are recorded per round

nodes.label: Requirement: an unmeasured cost is recorded as unmeasured, never as zero
nodes.norm_label: requirement: an unmeasured cost is recorded as unmeasured, never as zero

nodes.label: Requirement: phase timing is recorded per round
nodes.norm_label: requirement: phase timing is recorded per round

nodes.label: Requirement: a per-run metrics rollup is derived from the event log
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a per-run metrics rollup is derived from the event log

nodes.label: Requirement: every recorded metric ships with its companion number
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every recorded metric ships with its companion number

nodes.label: Requirement: telemetry failure never changes an outcome
nodes.norm_label: requirement: telemetry failure never changes an outcome

nodes.label: Pinned fact (checkable claim class)
nodes.rationale: A checker cannot verify prose, so the registry's unit is restricted to a number, path, default, supported value or capability existence that is independently observable in code.

nodes.label: Claim registry row schema
nodes.rationale: claim_id | doc_ref | claim_text | probe | expected | observed_at_registration | owner; owner exists so a failure routes to someone rather than everyone.

nodes.label: observed_at_registration column
nodes.rationale: Lets the checker distinguish 'the probe disagrees' from 'the probe found nothing', so a moved target is diagnosable instead of being 'fixed' by loosening the row.

nodes.label: Empty-result rule
nodes.rationale: An empty probe result is a failure, never a pass: the commonest death of this check class is a probe that silently stops matching and goes permanently green.

nodes.label: Stale change folders check
nodes.rationale: Same probe shape as a doc-vs-code contradiction, but between two documents: 0/N tasks while ROADMAP records the work shipped.

nodes.label: Unstamped workaround check
nodes.rationale: Frontier behaviour drifts under a fixed alias with no version bump, so a workaround with no model and no date cannot be re-evaluated; counted first, thresholded later, because failing a gate on an unmeasured number is how a gate gets disabled.

nodes.label: Coverage theatre risk
nodes.rationale: A green doctrine check will be read as 'the docs are true'; mitigated by reporting registered-claim counts and never a percentage, since the denominator is unknowable.

nodes.label: LLM contradiction auditor (rejected as gate)
nodes.rationale: An LLM is not a sound verifier and its output is a claim, not a gate; permitted only as a one-off seeding tool whose output is untrusted until converted to a deterministic probe.

nodes.label: Generate documentation from code (rejected for scope)
nodes.rationale: Works for reference tables but not for the narrative claims that actually mislead; a table-only generator would create the impression that documentation is derived while leaving narrative claims unchecked.
nodes.norm_label: generate documentation from code (rejected for scope)

nodes.label: doctrine-check.sh deterministic checker
nodes.rationale: Shell, jq and git only, no model call, cheap enough to run on every commit.

nodes.label: The eleven documented claims the code contradicts
nodes.rationale: Found by one careful human reading (R5 section 8.2); the argument is that this defect class is found one pair at a time and eleven is not assumed to be the total.
nodes.norm_label: the eleven documented claims the code contradicts

nodes.label: Concurrency caps mismatch (ROADMAP grok=1 vs lane-queue grok:3)
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a live correction that misled a reader today, which is why it is the seeded claim called out specifically.
nodes.norm_label: concurrency caps mismatch (roadmap grok=1 vs lane-queue grok:3)

nodes.label: docs-check.sh documentation gate
nodes.rationale: markdownlint-cli2, codespell, lychee and comment coverage would all pass a document that is beautifully formatted, correctly spelled, fully linked, and false.

nodes.label: Claim ownership routing to owning packages
nodes.rationale: This package fixes the checker, not most of the claims: each false claim is owned by the package that owns the code it describes, and it SHALL NOT re-implement their fixes.
nodes.norm_label: claim ownership routing to owning packages

nodes.label: T3 seed the registry from known contradictions
nodes.norm_label: t3 seed the registry from known contradictions

nodes.label: T4 coordinate the fixes, do not perform them
nodes.norm_label: t4 coordinate the fixes, do not perform them

nodes.label: T7 tests and gate (mutation per probe class)
nodes.rationale: A checker that passes on a repo with eleven known contradictions is broken, so the checker must be run against the repo as it stands and confirmed to fail.
nodes.norm_label: t7 tests and gate (mutation per probe class)

nodes.label: Requirement: load-bearing claims registered against a deterministic probe
nodes.norm_label: requirement: load-bearing claims registered against a deterministic probe

nodes.label: Requirement: deterministic checker fails on any contradicted claim
nodes.norm_label: requirement: deterministic checker fails on any contradicted claim

nodes.label: Requirement: a probe that matches nothing is a failure
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a probe that matches nothing is a failure

nodes.label: Requirement: the checker's own probes are proven able to fail
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the checker's own probes are proven able to fail

nodes.label: Requirement: the doctrine check runs in the documentation gate
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the doctrine check runs in the documentation gate

nodes.label: Requirement: every change registers the claims its documentation makes
nodes.rationale: The registry grows by construction with every change rather than by periodic archaeology.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every change registers the claims its documentation makes

nodes.label: Requirement: a package's stated progress may not contradict the roadmap
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a package's stated progress may not contradict the roadmap

nodes.label: Requirement: workarounds carry the model and date they were added for
nodes.norm_label: requirement: workarounds carry the model and date they were added for

nodes.label: git status --porcelain digest is unsound in both directions
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-07-28: porcelain collapses an untracked directory to one line so files 2..N are invisible, and it is blind to content rewrites; separately the write-first skeleton doctrine manufactures a false positive.
nodes.norm_label: git status --porcelain digest is unsound in both directions

nodes.label: Evidence loop (declare, baseline, invoke, capture, assert, decide, re-prompt)
nodes.rationale: One outer contract for every lane round under every vendor adapter; a round whose success cannot be evaluated is not dispatched.
nodes.norm_label: evidence loop (declare, baseline, invoke, capture, assert, decide, re-prompt)

nodes.label: Lane-type evidence contract
nodes.rationale: One predicate cannot serve four lane types: the single workspace-change predicate rejected a conforming audit that must not mutate, and accepted a partial package.

nodes.label: Two evidence roots: work root and artifact root
nodes.rationale: The defect was the singular: requiring one root to be both outside the reviewed worktree and a git work tree had no satisfying assignment, because the run directory is orchestrator-owned storage outside every repository.
nodes.norm_label: two evidence roots: work root and artifact root

nodes.label: Canonical per-path record with absence as a value
nodes.rationale: Deletion had no encoding, so a correct removal was byte-identical to a do-nothing round; unreadable is kept distinct from absent so a permissions failure cannot impersonate a deletion, and a symlink hashes its target string.
nodes.norm_label: canonical per-path record with absence as a value

nodes.label: INCONCLUSIVE is a property of the mechanism
nodes.rationale: The 2026-07-28 verdict was wrong because the instrument was blind, not because unchanged evidence needs an exemption; scoping INCONCLUSIVE to an untrusted mechanism makes the contradiction with the implement-lane rule structurally impossible.
nodes.norm_label: inconclusive is a property of the mechanism

nodes.label: Attempt-fresh production
nodes.rationale: The assertion asks whether this attempt produced something, not whether the artifact exists, so a resumed lane cannot inherit its predecessor's credit; it closes the empty round, not the lazy one.

nodes.label: Declared deliverable set (orchestrator-resolved, unforgeable)
nodes.rationale: A lane that can name its own deliverables can satisfy its own contract, which is the write-evidence instance of a checker grading its own homework; an unresolvable set refuses dispatch rather than falling back to a whole-tree scan.

nodes.label: Scoped mutation probe on diff-touched lines
nodes.rationale: Agent-written tests do not reliably improve defect catch rate while external adversarial checks do; merge-gate is the justified primary cadence because per-changed-line mutation is too slow per commit.
nodes.norm_label: scoped mutation probe on diff-touched lines

nodes.label: Planted-write positive control
nodes.rationale: The control corpus must be shown to fail the old predicate: a positive control that both the old and new predicate pass demonstrates nothing about the fix.

nodes.label: In-tree audit report contradiction (architect-owned)
nodes.rationale: Every audit and review report in this workstream is written inside the tree under review, which the audit-lane rule defines as tampering; scoping the tamper predicate to undeclared paths makes an explicit contract able to express one without legalising it by default.

nodes.label: Ownership split for lib/evidence.sh and vendor-multiround.sh
nodes.rationale: A helper whose semantics live in one package and whose implementation lives in another is how the two incompatible definitions arose in the first place.
nodes.norm_label: ownership split for lib/evidence.sh and vendor-multiround.sh

nodes.label: Stricter agent self-report (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Prompting cannot fix permission-gate cancellations the agent may not surface, and observed agents checked for missing files and still stopped; self-report is not evidence.

nodes.label: Substring-matching agent output for success (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A checker grepping for 'violation' matched the success string '[ok] No violation found'; matching prose for done/success is account-based, not artifact-based.

nodes.label: evidence-contracts change package
nodes.rationale: Four times in one day across three vendors, lanes exited 0 while producing no real work; exit code, self-report and substring matches are never sufficient.

nodes.label: Vendor termination-reason capture
nodes.rationale: Empty burst and cancelled writes present identically from the outside (unchanged evidence, exit 0), so the stored stop reason is the only after-the-fact differentiator.

nodes.label: T2 declared deliverable sets and lane-type contracts
nodes.norm_label: t2 declared deliverable sets and lane-type contracts

nodes.label: T3 inconclusive semantics and the bounded loop
nodes.norm_label: t3 inconclusive semantics and the bounded loop

nodes.label: Status enumeration invocation (--porcelain=v1 -z -uall --no-renames)
nodes.rationale: -uall for the untracked-directory collapse, -z because porcelain v1 shell-quotes awkward paths, --no-renames so a rename decomposes into an absent plus a present record.

nodes.label: Requirement: every round declares its deliverable set before dispatch
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every round declares its deliverable set before dispatch

nodes.label: Requirement: the declared deliverable set is orchestrator-resolved and unforgeable
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the declared deliverable set is orchestrator-resolved and unforgeable

nodes.label: Requirement: a round is never dispatched into an already-satisfied contract
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a round is never dispatched into an already-satisfied contract

nodes.label: Requirement: each lane declares a work root and an artifact root
nodes.norm_label: requirement: each lane declares a work root and an artifact root

nodes.label: Requirement: write evidence is a content digest over the declared deliverable set
nodes.norm_label: requirement: write evidence is a content digest over the declared deliverable set

nodes.label: Requirement: one canonical per-path encoding covering absence, deletion and type
nodes.norm_label: requirement: one canonical per-path encoding covering absence, deletion and type

nodes.label: Requirement: a path-level status digest is a corroborating signal with two declared blind spots
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a path-level status digest is a corroborating signal with two declared blind spots

nodes.label: Requirement: INCONCLUSIVE is a property of the evidence mechanism
nodes.norm_label: requirement: inconclusive is a property of the evidence mechanism

nodes.label: Requirement: every lane-type artifact assertion requires attempt-fresh production
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every lane-type artifact assertion requires attempt-fresh production

nodes.label: Requirement: lane-type evidence contracts are declared, not inferred
nodes.norm_label: requirement: lane-type evidence contracts are declared, not inferred

nodes.label: Requirement: audit-lane evidence contract
nodes.rationale: The in-progress verdict is published before spawn and before the baseline, so a pre-existing APPROVED cannot be inherited by a no-op audit and a legitimate re-audit is not refused as stale.

nodes.label: Requirement: planning and research lane contracts reject partial packages
nodes.norm_label: requirement: planning and research lane contracts reject partial packages

nodes.label: Requirement: a planted-write positive control gates every evidence verdict
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a planted-write positive control gates every evidence verdict

nodes.label: Requirement: write evidence fails closed when it cannot be computed
nodes.norm_label: requirement: write evidence fails closed when it cannot be computed

nodes.label: Requirement: vendor- and lane-agnostic bounded evidence loop
nodes.norm_label: requirement: vendor- and lane-agnostic bounded evidence loop

nodes.label: Requirement: termination-reason capture for empty-burst vs cancelled-writes
nodes.norm_label: requirement: termination-reason capture for empty-burst vs cancelled-writes

nodes.label: Requirement: scoped mutation probe on diff-touched lines
nodes.norm_label: requirement: scoped mutation probe on diff-touched lines

nodes.label: Vacuous-check problem class
nodes.rationale: Lane claims about their own state pass loudly if trusted alone; the narrow evidence-contract instance is corroboration by digest plus artifact assertion.

nodes.label: The violation is the asset, not the model
nodes.rationale: Only the pair carries information: a post-fix-only arm holds its invariants by construction, which is exactly what the architect's first M1 run produced when the default entrypoint aliased the post-fix configuration.
nodes.norm_label: the violation is the asset, not the model

nodes.label: Expectation manifest as a diffable TSV
nodes.rationale: Quint has no notion of 'this invariant is expected to fail', and a manifest row is diffable while a deleted row is visible; the same edit buried in a shell script is not.
nodes.norm_label: expectation manifest as a diffable tsv

nodes.label: Anchored outcome classifier
nodes.rationale: The harness that parses checker output is itself a check, so it gets a positive control; unknowns must not be green.

nodes.label: Vacuous-predicate registry
nodes.rationale: The wrong predicate was chosen once, produced a confident inverted conclusion, and was caught only by another lane's result; the registry makes the second attempt fail loudly.

nodes.label: Coarse file-level model drift gate
nodes.rationale: A precise dependency analysis of a shell codebase against a Quint abstraction is not tractable, and a gate that is precise but wrong is worse than one that is blunt and forces a sentence of justification.

nodes.label: Method and bound printed with every verdict
nodes.rationale: Formal results carry disproportionate rhetorical weight, and the gap between 'no counterexample within 8 steps' and 'correct' is where an unjustified release decision would live.
nodes.norm_label: method and bound printed with every verdict

nodes.label: Assert on counterexample content (rejected as the gate)
nodes.rationale: Quint's search order is not stable across versions, and a manifest failing on a different valid counterexample trains readers to ignore it.
nodes.norm_label: assert on counterexample content (rejected as the gate)

nodes.label: Generate the manifest from a passing run (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A baseline derived from whatever the code did today is a rubber stamp; every seeded row traces to a result a human ran and recorded.
nodes.norm_label: generate the manifest from a passing run (rejected)

nodes.label: Three vacuous checks in one session
nodes.rationale: grep -q violation, rework_rounds_bounded on a loop where round never advances, and --step=event_step against actions in index_step; none was caught by the check itself, only by cross-checking an independent result.
nodes.norm_label: three vacuous checks in one session

nodes.label: Pinned Quint 0.32.0 / Apalache 0.56.1 toolchain
nodes.rationale: quint resolves through an fnm multishell path that does not survive a new shell, so within one release nobody could reproduce the recorded numbers.

nodes.label: pkill -f ban in lanes and formal/
nodes.rationale: pkill -f "quint verify" matched the issuing lane's own command line and would also have killed a sibling lane sharing the Apalache server on port 8822.
nodes.norm_label: pkill -f ban in lanes and formal/

nodes.label: A drifted model is worse than no model
nodes.rationale: A stale claim now carries a checker's authority, so it becomes actively misleading rather than merely useless.
nodes.norm_label: a drifted model is worse than no model

nodes.label: T1 the outcome classifier and its positive control
nodes.norm_label: t1 the outcome classifier and its positive control

nodes.label: T5 coverage records and the drift gate
nodes.norm_label: t5 coverage records and the drift gate

nodes.label: T8 gate (deliberately weaken a pre-fix arm and confirm failure)
nodes.rationale: A suite never observed failing is not evidence.
nodes.norm_label: t8 gate (deliberately weaken a pre-fix arm and confirm failure)

nodes.label: Requirement: models typecheck in CI against a pinned toolchain
nodes.norm_label: requirement: models typecheck in ci against a pinned toolchain

nodes.label: Requirement: every modelled defect violates before the fix and holds after
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every modelled defect violates before the fix and holds after

nodes.label: Requirement: the manifest carries the architect-reproduced inventory
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the manifest carries the architect-reproduced inventory

nodes.label: Requirement: a verdict is read from an anchored outcome line, never a substring
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a verdict is read from an anchored outcome line, never a substring

nodes.label: Requirement: a model that has drifted from its subsystem is a defect
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a model that has drifted from its subsystem is a defect

nodes.label: Requirement: results state their method and bound and are never called proofs
nodes.norm_label: requirement: results state their method and bound and are never called proofs

nodes.label: Requirement: a predicate observed to be vacuous is registered and cannot be reused
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a predicate observed to be vacuous is registered and cannot be reused

nodes.label: Requirement: lanes terminate processes by handle, never by pattern
nodes.norm_label: requirement: lanes terminate processes by handle, never by pattern

nodes.label: Host-side eleven-step context pipeline
nodes.rationale: Steps 1-10 run before the lane starts and step 11 after it finishes; the worker never traverses.

nodes.label: edge_key durable edge identity
nodes.rationale: graph.json edges carry no id, yet citation, verification and replay all key on edge identity; including source_file and source_location is deliberate because two edges extracted from different places are different evidence.

nodes.label: In-block edge alias and alias table
nodes.rationale: Short opaque IDs are what the citation literature uses, and putting the alias table inside the content hash is what makes OUT_OF_CONTEXT_CITATION decidable by two exact lookups with no model.
nodes.norm_label: in-block edge alias and alias table

nodes.label: Layout is specified normatively, surface syntax is not
nodes.rationale: Information layout is worth 4.8-88.0 accuracy points and widens with scale, while surface syntax is worth ~1.5-10 points, shrinks with scale, and inverts by vendor (IoU of best-format sets often below 0.2).
nodes.norm_label: layout is specified normatively, surface syntax is not

nodes.label: Bounded escape hatch: tools return facts, not context
nodes.rationale: The moment a tool returns 500 edges we have rebuilt context dumping with extra steps; mid-generation retrieval is measured to hurt both citation and correctness.
nodes.norm_label: bounded escape hatch: tools return facts, not context

nodes.label: Over-serving is the asymmetric failure
nodes.rationale: Under-serving costs a follow-up question; over-serving is measured to go below the no-graph baseline, so every default errs low and a hard cap bounds the error.

nodes.label: Worker graph traversal (rejected as primary path)
nodes.rationale: Pre-serialization measures 89.80 WebQSP Hit in one call against agentic traversal's 82.6 in 6-8, and decisively a traversal is unhashable so the audit trail cannot state what the worker saw.
nodes.norm_label: worker graph traversal (rejected as primary path)

nodes.label: PPR and GNN ranking (rejected)
nodes.rationale: PPR fails to reliably yield improvements across a full K sweep, and GNN variants degrade against MLP counterparts through semantic diffusion; directional distance features beat both and cost nothing.

nodes.label: Post-hoc graph provenance attachment (rejected)
nodes.rationale: The single largest measured effect in the evidence base: 73.6 to 26.7 citation recall while correctness moves -2.1, so post-hoc citations are ~2.7x less faithful while looking equally correct.

nodes.label: graphify MCP server as machine interface (rejected as primary)
nodes.rationale: All ten tools return prose strings and query_graph has no stemming, synonyms or cross-language match, so without the mandated vocabulary expansion the answer collapses to noise.
nodes.norm_label: graphify mcp server as machine interface (rejected as primary)

nodes.label: Files-only boundary (no graph store dependency)
nodes.rationale: If GP-6 is deferred or the store proves fragile, the context builder and the gate keep working and lose only cross-run query ergonomics.

nodes.label: graph-context-builder change package (GP-5)
nodes.rationale: Serving the graph badly is worse than not serving it: 20- and 30-document contexts score below closed-book, and effective context is measured at 8K tokens or less for every model tested.

nodes.label: In-band citation contract
nodes.rationale: ALCE measures inline citation at 73.6/72.5 against post-hoc attachment at 26.7/26.7, and summarising the served evidence costs 8-15 points of citation precision.

nodes.label: Deterministic citation verification codes
nodes.rationale: Foreman's citation targets are database rows rather than paragraphs, so verifying a citation is an O(1) exact lookup instead of an NLI judgement - the near-free win of the package.

nodes.label: NO GRAPH CONTEXT marker on zero seeds
nodes.rationale: Irrelevant context is measured to score below no context at all, so there is no fallback subgraph.
nodes.norm_label: no graph context marker on zero seeds

nodes.label: 2,000-token provisional graph budget
nodes.rationale: Inherited from a knee measured on short Freebase triples; Foreman edges carry longer free text so the knee lands earlier, and shipping the number is acceptable while shipping it as measured here is not.

nodes.label: Absence is a query, not a model question
nodes.rationale: Disconnected-node accuracy is 0.5% zero-shot and about 0.0% under every other prompting method: LLMs lack a global model of a graph.
nodes.norm_label: absence is a query, not a model question

nodes.label: Claim discipline: citation precision and multi-hop only
nodes.rationale: No reduced-hallucination claim is made, because that number does not exist anywhere in the KG-RAG literature.
nodes.norm_label: claim discipline: citation precision and multi-hop only

nodes.label: T2 seed resolution and role scoping
nodes.norm_label: t2 seed resolution and role scoping

nodes.label: T6 deterministic verification
nodes.rationale: The verifier is kept out of any selection or reranking loop, because a checker used to optimise output is no longer usable to evaluate it.

nodes.label: Requirement: worker graph access is a pre-serialized block, not traversal
nodes.norm_label: requirement: worker graph access is a pre-serialized block, not traversal

nodes.label: Requirement: every served edge carries a stable verifiable identifier
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every served edge carries a stable verifiable identifier

nodes.label: Requirement: candidates within two hops over a role-scoped allowlist, then ranked
nodes.norm_label: requirement: candidates within two hops over a role-scoped allowlist, then ranked

nodes.label: Requirement: the block is token-budgeted and under-serves by default
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the block is token-budgeted and under-serves by default

nodes.label: Requirement: fixed block layout with labelled, separated conflicts
nodes.norm_label: requirement: fixed block layout with labelled, separated conflicts

nodes.label: Requirement: the citation contract is issued in-context at generation time
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the citation contract is issued in-context at generation time

nodes.label: Requirement: served edges are never summarised or compressed
nodes.norm_label: requirement: served edges are never summarised or compressed

nodes.label: Requirement: every citation is verified deterministically after generation
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every citation is verified deterministically after generation

nodes.label: Requirement: absence and contradiction are found by query, never by model reading
nodes.norm_label: requirement: absence and contradiction are found by query, never by model reading

nodes.label: Requirement: the block is content-hashed, recorded and replayable
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the block is content-hashed, recorded and replayable

nodes.label: Requirement: the MCP path is a bounded, read-only, wrapped escape hatch
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the mcp path is a bounded, read-only, wrapped escape hatch

nodes.label: Requirement: direction is reconstructed at load, not read from the directed field
nodes.rationale: The published artifact is directed:false on every merge-cadence refresh and no graphify CLI cadence publishes otherwise, so branching on the field would reject every valid artifact.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: direction is reconstructed at load, not read from the directed field

nodes.label: Requirement: the builder runs off files and requires no graph store
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the builder runs off files and requires no graph store

nodes.label: Immutable run evidence ledger
nodes.rationale: Every claim must be reproducible from machine-readable evidence rather than from log prose; report.md is derived from those files and is not an independent source of truth.

nodes.label: Arithmetic conservation equations
nodes.rationale: Aggregate equality alone can conceal one missing input and one duplicated input, so conservation is both cardinality arithmetic and exact set partitioning.

nodes.label: Accounting identity input = stored + named-drop + rejected + unreached
nodes.rationale: It must balance even for a failed or partial run, while a conservation pass additionally requires rejected = 0 and unreached = 0.
nodes.norm_label: accounting identity input = stored + named-drop + rejected + unreached

nodes.label: Non-vacuous ordered-endpoint direction check
nodes.rationale: directed:false is observational; direction is the ordered tuple, and the audit refuses to call the test discriminating if the descending-endpoint count is zero.

nodes.label: Named real provenance witnesses across three audit levels
nodes.rationale: TerminusDB has no edge properties, so retaining file, location, score and audit level requires a schema-declared representation; the INFERRED 0.95 witness detects a manifest rule that would rebucket a high score as extracted.
nodes.norm_label: named real provenance witnesses across three audit levels

nodes.label: Competency outcome model (answered / empty-but-valid / unanswerable)
nodes.rationale: Partial execution cannot lose a question or force it into a false answer category, so failed and not-run rows are counted separately and every report must total 24.

nodes.label: Ontology findings, never local workarounds
nodes.rationale: The frozen schema is the thing under test; a local workaround erases the ontology finding and makes the exercise non-reproducible.

nodes.label: Owner-package composition boundaries
nodes.rationale: A second mapper, ingest client, query suite, refresh path or rebuild procedure could pass while production code remains broken, so the runner composes published owner interfaces only.

nodes.label: Declare success from stage exit codes (rejected)
nodes.rationale: An exit code proves only that a process returned, not that the report, counts or round-trip evidence exists.
nodes.norm_label: declare success from stage exit codes (rejected)

nodes.label: Fixture counts as end-to-end proof (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Fixtures have already passed and lack the real relation vocabulary, provenance-bearing links, communities and hyperedges the exercise exists to test.

nodes.label: graph-dogfood release exercise
nodes.rationale: A failed run with a counted ledger and a named blocking seam is valid dogfood evidence; a claimed success without the counts is not.

nodes.label: Committed baseline corpus counts (3,579 nodes / 3,668 links / 6 hyperedges)
nodes.rationale: These values describe one named snapshot built at d4af3a92 and are not silently reused after the repository evolves.
nodes.norm_label: committed baseline corpus counts (3,579 nodes / 3,668 links / 6 hyperedges)

nodes.label: graph.json as the sole ingest source
nodes.rationale: Neo4j, FalkorDB, Cypher, GraphML and visualization exports lose provenance, confidence, communities and hyperedges before TerminusDB sees them, so conservation after such a transform would certify a lossy input.
nodes.norm_label: graph.json as the sole ingest source

nodes.label: Manifest v1 fail-closed on unknown relations
nodes.rationale: The real relation vocabulary is not declared in manifest v1, so the current real graph is not assumed to ingest successfully and the adapter must fail closed rather than guess.
nodes.norm_label: manifest v1 fail-closed on unknown relations

nodes.label: Run contract and evidence layout tasks
nodes.norm_label: run contract and evidence layout tasks

nodes.label: Input disposition ledger tasks
nodes.rationale: Mutation tests remove, duplicate, invent and swap dispositions so each mutation trips a different named predicate.

nodes.label: Two-pass ingest and conservation tasks
nodes.rationale: Adapter log totals may not be used as the database recount; deleting one accepted document after ingest must fail the gate even though the adapter report is unchanged.

nodes.label: Honest report rendering tasks
nodes.rationale: Absent measurements render as missing, unstarted stages as not-run, and successful zero-row queries as empty-but-valid; those states are never collapsed.

nodes.label: graph-dogfood-gate.sh deterministic evidence gate
nodes.rationale: If the pipeline cannot complete the gate must return nonzero and the report must name the first blocker; the gate is not waived to obtain a green result.

nodes.label: Requirement: measured performance and rebuild baseline
nodes.rationale: Previously measured 2.6 s startup, 38 MB idle RSS, 9.7 MB for 5,500 documents and ~1,070 docs/s are labelled historical and never substituted for missing current-run evidence.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: measured performance and rebuild baseline

nodes.label: Requirement: honest terminal report (PASSED / FAILED / INCOMPLETE)
nodes.rationale: An observed failure takes precedence as FAILED; absent evidence without an observed failure is INCOMPLETE, so absence of numbers can never be represented as zero or success.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: honest terminal report (passed / failed / incomplete)

nodes.label: Pre-registration kill-criteria register
nodes.rationale: A threshold chosen after seeing the data is not a threshold, so the register is committed and hashed before the measuring run and an unregistered criterion may not justify keeping the plane.

nodes.label: Locked prompt-only baseline arm
nodes.rationale: Otherwise the baseline drifts upward in exactly the way that makes it lose; cost matching matters as much as the lock because token usage alone explains 80% of performance variance.

nodes.label: Run-to-run sigma as the noise floor
nodes.rationale: Published agent-benchmark sigma is 1.5-2.7 pp with three-run half-widths of 2.7-4.9 pp and Foreman's own has never been measured, so a 3-point improvement and a 3-point regression are currently the same observation.
nodes.norm_label: run-to-run sigma as the noise floor

nodes.label: Query census (instrumented, not recalled)
nodes.rationale: Architects reliably remember the interesting query and forget the forty lookups; the census is the cheapest kill criterion and can freeze the store before a line of adapter code is written.

nodes.label: Shadow-mode Tier-3 open-world checks
