nodes.rationale: At 88-94% precision and Foreman's merge volume a blocking check false-blocks about three correct merges a week, which teaches the operator to bypass the gate - after which the gate protects nothing.

nodes.label: Per-vendor serializer and K sweep
nodes.rationale: Format preference inverts across model generations and the IoU of best-format sets across series is often below 0.2, so a hard-coded serializer is a bet placed on one vendor with the other lanes' money.

nodes.label: M5 cross-vendor unique-catch rate
nodes.rationale: It is the only measurement that can justify a fourth vendor on quality grounds, because nine judges across seven families behave as ~2 effective votes; the replay corpus makes it computable at zero marginal spend.

nodes.label: The UNCOMPUTABLE outcome state
nodes.rationale: Left alone the arithmetic answers for you and usually in the component's favour - precision over zero predicted blocks reads as flawless; a measured zero is not an absent measurement.

nodes.label: Fireability check on every threshold
nodes.rationale: A criterion whose threshold no achievable measurement could cross is the same defect class as a checker that cannot fail; KC-13's 15-minute bound was 176x the achievable rebuild and was re-baselined to 60 s.

nodes.label: Derived-predicate rule
nodes.rationale: Naming exceptions one at a time is how the atomicity rule erodes, so the KC-8/KC-9 carve-out is generalised into a test that KC-13 and KC-15 also pass and a genuinely bad proposal fails.

nodes.label: Locked-measurement threshold rule
nodes.rationale: A bar set against a prior locked hashed measurement is the resolution of the instrument rather than a preference, while a run that sets its own bar cannot fail it.

nodes.label: Architect override rule
nodes.rationale: A criterion that can be overridden into success is not a criterion; the original text recorded the fact of the override but left the component's fate unspecified, which in practice means it stays on.

nodes.label: keep-off action enum extension
nodes.rationale: Eight imported criteria need 'stays in the tree, disabled by default, carries no claim', which neither revert nor descope states, and the counterfactual A/B arm requires the code present and off.

nodes.label: LEED neurosymbolic reference failure
nodes.rationale: 61.6% against a text-only 67.3% with a locally perfect symbolic sub-check: local correctness plus global loss is the shape to watch, and only an untouchable baseline detects it.

nodes.label: K-1 contradiction resolved: KC-1 governs GP-5 only
nodes.rationale: The store already landed on different evidence, the census verdict cannot exist inside v0.2.9, and one measurement with two subjects and two actions violates atomicity.
nodes.norm_label: k-1 contradiction resolved: kc-1 governs gp-5 only

nodes.label: graph-eval-falsification change package (GP-7)
nodes.rationale: The package that decides whether the graph plane was worth building, written so that the answer can be no; a falsification harness that cannot return a negative verdict is the same failure mode as a test that cannot fail.

nodes.label: Negative evidence base against GraphRAG
nodes.rationale: BM-25 beat all nine GraphRAG systems on True/False, LightRAG spent 83.9M construction tokens to score below TF-IDF, and 'graphs reduce hallucination' is unmeasured anywhere in the survey drawn on.

nodes.label: Graph-plane off-switch and A/B path
nodes.rationale: A negative verdict must be executable rather than merely regrettable, and once the plane is on by default the counterfactual is gone.

nodes.label: External benchmark as the gate (rejected)
nodes.rationale: The gate measures Foreman by holding models fixed and varying Foreman, which is the inverse of what SWE-bench and relatives do.

nodes.norm_label: requirement: the round-mode occurrence reduction is registered and measured

nodes.norm_label: requirement: a negative verdict has an executable landing path

nodes.label: Files-only implementation as the default, not the fallback
nodes.rationale: A fallback that nobody runs is a fallback that does not work; a default that everyone runs is tested by definition, so the TerminusDB adapter is opt-in per host.
nodes.norm_label: files-only implementation as the default, not the fallback

nodes.label: Regenerability of the store
nodes.rationale: Everything is derivable from events.jsonl, graph.json and the per-lane GraphUpdate journals, so losing the store costs a re-materialisation rather than a rewrite; the CI drop-and-rebuild test is what keeps that true.

nodes.label: Work-DAG as documents, not commits
nodes.rationale: Commit-log scan measured ~2.4 ms per commit on a clean linear fit (~24 s at 10,000 commits) with O(offset) paging, and fast history is the paid tier; documents answer the same lineage questions at ~230 ms independent of commit count.

nodes.label: Silent-empty query footguns
nodes.rationale: For an audit trail a silently empty result says 'nothing changed' when something did; a gate reading empty as 'no violations found' is the pySHACL canary failure again, and a no-op check is worse than no check because it is trusted.

nodes.label: Silent-empty canary fixtures
nodes.rationale: A wrapper that stops asserting looks exactly like a wrapper that asserts and passes, so the canaries assert on mechanism, not on luck.

nodes.label: Reification of edge attributes
nodes.rationale: Adding a reified class before data exists is a schema addition; adding it afterwards is MoveClassProperty plus a backfill, so writing the target shape down now converts a future migration into a future insert.

nodes.label: Three concurrency rules from three measurements
nodes.rationale: Distinct-document fan-in needs no CAS; same-document contention is silent last-write-wins; CAS via TerminusDB-Data-Version works but is branch-scoped, so blanket CAS produces a retry storm.
nodes.norm_label: three concurrency rules from three measurements

nodes.label: TerminusDB project-health risk
nodes.rationale: Alive but fragile: one human wrote ~93% of last year's commits, the founder left, 27 commits in 2024, 105 npm downloads a month, no fork above one star and no successor project.

nodes.label: TerminusDB commits as the lineage representation (rejected)
nodes.rationale: The single most load-bearing rejection in the package, because it is the design the product's own documentation leads you to.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb commits as the lineage representation (rejected)

nodes.label: graphify export neo4j/falkordb as the ingest path (rejected absolutely)
nodes.rationale: It emits 5 fields and drops source_file, source_location, confidence_score, hyperedges and communities - precisely the provenance the store exists for.
nodes.norm_label: graphify export neo4j/falkordb as the ingest path (rejected absolutely)

nodes.label: Closed-world model over OWL
nodes.rationale: 10 of 24 competency questions require negation-as-failure, unanswerable in principle under the open-world assumption; Foreman's graph records a bounded fully-observed process so closed-world is the correct model, not a convenience.

nodes.label: Ontology changes are code, not a trust signal
nodes.rationale: Single-axiom ontology edits achieved 93.3% attack success with 100% consistency-checker stealth and detection at chance, so schema acceptance proves nothing.
nodes.norm_label: ontology changes are code, not a trust signal

nodes.label: Risk: the store becomes load-bearing by accident
nodes.rationale: Mitigated by a conformance suite running identical assertions against both implementations and by CI running the files-only path by default.
nodes.norm_label: risk: the store becomes load-bearing by accident

nodes.label: graph-store-port change package
nodes.rationale: Funds a store only for the three cross-run questions SYNTHESIS 3 is willing to pay for; everything else in the graph plane runs off files.

nodes.label: GraphStore port
nodes.rationale: One protocol for every graph read and write so Foreman core never imports a TerminusDB client, builds a URL, or sees a WOQL AST; the port is what makes deferral cheap.

nodes.label: files-only implementation (default)
nodes.rationale: Answers the port over graph.json + worklog.jsonl + run-dir JSON with no database, container or network, so a dead or unwanted store costs only time-travel, branch/merge and query ergonomics.

nodes.label: TerminusDB adapter over raw HTTP
nodes.rationale: Targets the HTTP API directly because both thin clients are in dependabot-only maintenance and everything R8 verified was done over raw HTTP.

nodes.label: work-DAG modelled as documents, not commits
nodes.rationale: /api/log is dead linear at ~2.4 ms per commit with O(offset) paging and the fast version is the Enterprise paywall; the same lineage answers cost ~230 ms over 5,000 documents.
nodes.norm_label: work-dag modelled as documents, not commits

nodes.label: reification of edge attributes
nodes.rationale: TerminusDB is a document graph with no edge properties, so an edge attribute silently disappears; SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS reification is designed now because retrofitting it after data exists is a MoveClassProperty plus a backfill.

nodes.label: silent-empty HTTP 200 failure mode
nodes.rationale: Two silent-empty paths in one product means the dominant failure mode is a wrong answer that looks like a true answer, and that lands directly on an audit trail.

nodes.label: ban on graphify neo4j/falkordb export as ingest source
nodes.rationale: The export emits five fields and drops source_file, source_location, confidence_score, hyperedges and communities, destroying exactly the audit trail the store exists to hold.
nodes.norm_label: ban on graphify neo4j/falkordb export as ingest source

nodes.label: store as regenerable materialisation
nodes.rationale: Retreat to files-only within one release is survivable only because everything in the store is regenerable from events.jsonl, graph.json and lane journals.

nodes.label: port conformance suite
nodes.rationale: Written first, against the port alone, so both implementations are graded by the same assertions.

nodes.label: Requirement: the store is a regenerable materialisation, never the system of record
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the store is a regenerable materialisation, never the system of record

nodes.label: Requirement: every graph read and write goes through the GraphStore port
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every graph read and write goes through the graphstore port

nodes.norm_label: requirement: a files-only implementation satisfies the port with no database

nodes.label: Requirement: the work-DAG is stored as documents and never queried through the commit log
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the work-dag is stored as documents and never queried through the commit log

nodes.label: Requirement: the frozen N2 schema is enforced at write time
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the frozen n2 schema is enforced at write time

nodes.label: Requirement: edge attributes are reified because the store has no edge properties
nodes.norm_label: requirement: edge attributes are reified because the store has no edge properties

nodes.norm_label: requirement: concurrent writes follow the measured three-way concurrency rule

nodes.norm_label: requirement: an empty result is never silently accepted

nodes.norm_label: requirement: the adapter is pinned and has a rehearsed exit path

nodes.norm_label: requirement: ingest reads graph.json through a schema-first, two-pass, idempotent path

nodes.label: silent-empty canary fixtures
nodes.rationale: One canary per known silent-empty path, each required to fail when the assertion machinery is disabled, so the assertion layer itself is proven live.

nodes.label: graph-refresh.sh single entry point
nodes.rationale: Everything that writes graphify-out/ goes through one script; the rest of the design is the discipline that script enforces.

nodes.label: slow cadence (LLM-priced, advisory)
nodes.rationale: Community labels and semantic nodes are produced by a model whose self-explanations are measured unstable, so they may never be evidence for a gate decision.

nodes.label: direction as a load-time property
nodes.rationale: No CLI cadence can emit directed:true, so gating on the field made the requirements jointly unsatisfiable; direction is in the data via _src/_tgt regardless of the field.

nodes.label: endpoint-order count gate
nodes.rationale: A canonicalising writer produces exactly zero descending-order links where both measured corpora sit near forty per cent, so zero-with-links is the shape of failure the old directed gate was reaching for.

nodes.label: version stamp in a sidecar, not graph.json
nodes.rationale: graphify --update rebuilds graph.json from the filesystem, so anything Foreman injects is unspecified under the next refresh; a graphify upgrade can migrate the whole path-derived ID space.
nodes.norm_label: version stamp in a sidecar, not graph.json

nodes.label: shrink guard is not a mutual-exclusion primitive
nodes.rationale: Two lanes each adding disjoint nodes both produce larger graphs, both pass the guard, and the second silently replaces the first.
nodes.norm_label: shrink guard is not a mutual-exclusion primitive

nodes.label: graphify watch._rebuild_lock covers only three call sites
nodes.rationale: extract, the skill pipeline, cluster-only, label and every export ignore it, and on Windows fcntl is absent so it degrades to an unconditional yield True.
nodes.norm_label: graphify watch._rebuild_lock covers only three call sites

nodes.label: health counters gated at the stage where they can fail
nodes.rationale: Collapse counters are 0 by construction on a post-build graph.json, so they must be computed over the pre-build AST-cache union; a check that cannot fail must not be written as a gate.
nodes.norm_label: health counters gated at the stage where they can fail

nodes.label: file moves as rename-with-lineage
nodes.rationale: A move re-IDs the file node and every symbol in it; emitting that as deletions and creations destroys the lineage that makes which-findings-recur answerable.

nodes.label: rejected alternative: graphify export as downstream seam
nodes.rationale: to_cypher is twelve lines emitting five values; direct-push variants drop hyperedges and _-prefixed keys, reintroducing the direction inversion the JSON path fixes.
nodes.norm_label: rejected alternative: graphify export as downstream seam

nodes.label: asserted zero-token merge cadence
nodes.rationale: Regenerating community structure on a corpus change is measured at ~14M tokens and Foreman's corpus changes hourly, so the merge cadence asserts zero tokens rather than merely intending them.

nodes.label: the host refreshes, CI enforces the contract
nodes.rationale: CI lacks graphify and installing it would put an LLM-capable extractor one config error away from the per-commit path; the freshness check is pure git and jq.
nodes.norm_label: the host refreshes, ci enforces the contract

nodes.label: knowledge-plane-refresh change package
nodes.rationale: The knowledge plane is today a deterministic zero-token artifact refreshed by hand and invisibly stale; the package exists to protect that property and automate it.

nodes.label: maintenance.sh run_graph four defects
nodes.rationale: It picks whichever graphify it finds, cannot check that direction survived, takes no lock, and runs in CI only as a no-op.

nodes.label: pinned interpreter and graphify version
nodes.rationale: Three graphify versions coexist on the reference box (0.9.16 PATH / 0.9.18 python3 / 0.9.15 skill); a nondeterministic producer cannot support the ID-stability claim GP-4's join keys rest on.

nodes.label: cohesion scores escape every path
nodes.rationale: They exist only in .graphify_analysis.json, which the skill's Step 9 deletes at the end of every run.

nodes.label: T1 reproduce the concurrency claim before building on it
nodes.rationale: The package's central claim is code-derived, not observed; a package whose central claim is unmeasured should measure it before it ships.
nodes.norm_label: t1 reproduce the concurrency claim before building on it

nodes.norm_label: t5 health gate and the metadata sidecar

nodes.norm_label: requirement: the knowledge graph refreshes automatically, ast-only, per merge

nodes.label: Requirement: direction survives as endpoint order and is reconstructed at load
nodes.norm_label: requirement: direction survives as endpoint order and is reconstructed at load

nodes.label: Requirement: a refresh that fails blocks, a refresh that cannot run does not
nodes.rationale: A failed refresh is evidence about the graph; an absent refresh is evidence only about the host, and blocking on it converts an advisory quality signal into an availability requirement nobody agreed to.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a refresh that fails blocks, a refresh that cannot run does not

nodes.label: Requirement: one pinned interpreter and one pinned graphify version, stamped into the output
nodes.norm_label: requirement: one pinned interpreter and one pinned graphify version, stamped into the output

nodes.norm_label: requirement: every graphify write is serialised by a foreman-owned lock

nodes.norm_label: requirement: each health counter is gated at the only stage where it can fail

nodes.norm_label: requirement: cohesion and community labels are captured before cleanup destroys them

nodes.label: Requirement: graph freshness is measured, reported, and checkable without graphify
nodes.norm_label: requirement: graph freshness is measured, reported, and checkable without graphify

nodes.norm_label: requirement: file moves are refreshed as rename-with-lineage

nodes.norm_label: requirement: llm extraction runs only on the slow cadence and is never evidential

nodes.norm_label: requirement: the cypher and graph-database export paths are banned

nodes.label: Requirement: maintenance runs the graph stage through the pinned refresh
nodes.norm_label: requirement: maintenance runs the graph stage through the pinned refresh

nodes.label: lane-ownership-and-reaping change package
nodes.rationale: Eight lanes were stranded in one session across three vendors and not one was detected by the mechanism responsible for detecting it.

nodes.label: existence treated as liveness (pgrep defect)
nodes.rationale: pgrep matches a stopped process identically to a running one, so a lane suspended by SIGTTIN reads as alive for its whole time budget.

nodes.label: FM_LANE_OWNER / FM_LANE_LABEL ownership tagging
nodes.rationale: The safe action for an unattributable wedged process is to leave it running, so without ownership untagged lanes accumulate on a box running concurrent sessions.

nodes.label: never-launched lane as a first-class stall signal
nodes.norm_label: never-launched lane as a first-class stall signal

nodes.label: stall taxonomy SUSPENDED / NEVER_LAUNCHED / NO_OUTPUT / WEDGED
nodes.norm_label: stall taxonomy suspended / never_launched / no_output / wedged

nodes.label: subtree adoption of a running lane
nodes.rationale: A lane is a timeout wrapper plus a vendor child, so claiming only the named pid leaves the child foreign.
nodes.norm_label: subtree adoption of a running lane

nodes.label: headless rounds launch with stdin from /dev/null
nodes.rationale: An interactive prompt then fails fast instead of suspending the process on SIGTTIN after a mid-round vendor CLI self-update.
nodes.norm_label: headless rounds launch with stdin from /dev/null

nodes.label: rejected CPU-delta hang predicate
nodes.rationale: Two successive attempts false-positived on every run, once against a live interactive session and once against a lane blocked on a model response, so the sound predicate set is narrower than it first appears.

nodes.label: pkill -f forbidden, kill by recorded pid
nodes.rationale: It has previously matched its own command line and killed the shell issuing it.
nodes.norm_label: pkill -f forbidden, kill by recorded pid

nodes.label: T5 tests and gate, red-first
nodes.rationale: Every test SHALL be observed failing against a deliberately wrong implementation before it is trusted.

nodes.label: Requirement: lane liveness is judged on process state and CPU, never on existence
nodes.norm_label: requirement: lane liveness is judged on process state and cpu, never on existence

nodes.label: Requirement: every lane and watchdog carries an owner tag
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every lane and watchdog carries an owner tag

nodes.label: Requirement: a lane that never launched its vendor is a stall, not a silence
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a lane that never launched its vendor is a stall, not a silence

nodes.label: Requirement: headless vendor rounds detach stdin
nodes.norm_label: requirement: headless vendor rounds detach stdin

nodes.label: Requirement: a liveness predicate is demonstrated against both a wedged and a healthy lane
nodes.rationale: A lane blocked on a model response and an idle interactive session both consume no CPU while being perfectly healthy, so a predicate that cannot separate network-blocked from wedged must not be used.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: a liveness predicate is demonstrated against both a wedged and a healthy lane

nodes.label: uutils mkdir check-then-act defect
nodes.rationale: POSIX guarantees atomicity of the syscall, not of a check-then-act around it; uutils issues statx then create, leaving a window a second process can enter. Invisible to a naive test because both implementations report File exists.

nodes.label: flock chosen over pinning GNU coreutils
nodes.rationale: Pinning GNU makes correctness depend on a distro-specific binary name and does nothing for the next uutils migration; flock is kernel-arbitrated with no check-then-act and is already used by lib/worktree.sh and task-new.sh.
nodes.norm_label: flock chosen over pinning gnu coreutils

nodes.label: stale-lock semantics differ between flock and mkdir
nodes.rationale: flock releases on process death and a mkdir lock does not, so el_init's reclamation must be preserved for the fallback but not assumed necessary on the flock path; this is the one place the change is not purely mechanical.
nodes.norm_label: stale-lock semantics differ between flock and mkdir

nodes.label: deterministic atomicity probe asserting on mechanism
nodes.rationale: A contention-sampling probe is itself flaky: a correct implementation can pass by luck and a loaded box can fail a good one, so the probe asserts that create issues mkdir(2) and surfaces EEXIST.
nodes.norm_label: deterministic atomicity probe asserting on mechanism

nodes.label: asymmetry of contention evidence
nodes.rationale: One observed double-entry falsifies atomicity outright; a clean sample of any finite size is bounded satisfaction and demonstrates nothing, because a check-then-act mkdir that did not lose the race produces an identical observation.

nodes.label: pinned-mechanism evidence class
nodes.rationale: Atomicity cannot be established on Git-Bash by anything Git-Bash can run, so the syscall observation moves off-host and the host's obligation reduces to a SHA-256 digest plus a filesystem class.

nodes.label: filesystem-class scoping of a lock verdict
nodes.rationale: The round-1 record said nothing about where the lock lives, so a verdict earned wherever tool-check.sh ran was trusted for a lock taken on drvfs, 9p, NFS or a UNC share; the class is computed for the directory that will hold the lock and never inherited.
nodes.norm_label: filesystem-class scoping of a lock verdict

nodes.label: fail-open is a policy defect, not a primitive defect
nodes.rationale: No lock primitive can defend a critical section a caller chose to enter without acquiring it; with a per-PID tmp name each racer writes a well-formed index.json and a lane disappears from the index with no error anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: fail-open is a policy defect, not a primitive defect

nodes.label: el_compact read-modify-write compaction race
nodes.rationale: A unique compaction temporary file name does not fix it: the hazard is the read-modify-write spanning a concurrent append, so snapshot and write-back must be one serialized section or compaction must abandon its write.

nodes.label: NATS bridge lock has no reclamation path
nodes.rationale: el_init reclaims .seq.lock and .attempt.lock but not .nats-bridge.lock, so a crash wedges it permanently.
nodes.norm_label: nats bridge lock has no reclamation path

nodes.label: owner-token inversion under check-then-act
nodes.rationale: Both racers acquire and both write the owner token, so the loser's token lands on disk: the true holder can no longer release and the non-holder can.

nodes.label: flat locking chosen over ordered nesting
nodes.rationale: A stated ordering is a standing permission to nest; a future change needing two locks amends the requirement and brings its own deadlock argument, which is a low bar to clear deliberately and a high bar to clear accidentally.
nodes.norm_label: flat locking chosen over ordered nesting

nodes.label: per-lock, owner-aware reclamation that refuses when unsure
nodes.rationale: A wedged lock is a visible outage; a reclaimed live lock is a silent double-holder. The token records PID and process start time because a reused PID is exactly the case a naive liveness check gets wrong.
nodes.norm_label: per-lock, owner-aware reclamation that refuses when unsure

nodes.label: six ordered, disjoint refusal causes
nodes.rationale: The round-1 enum was not total, not disjoint and not uniform; the invariant is now scoped to the refused acquisition rather than the process so one shape holds for all six causes.

nodes.label: formal/specs/eventlog_concurrency.qnt Quint model
nodes.rationale: Apalache 0.56.1 reproduces the measured defect independently and shows the primitive swap is sound but insufficient: index_fail_open_atomic violates mutual_exclusion at 8 steps with an atomic test-and-set.

nodes.label: bounded satisfaction is not proof
nodes.rationale: atomic/mutual_exclusion clean at 8 steps is bounded satisfaction and Apalache itself says to increase max-steps; a first run also returned a vacuous safe because the step function did not match the module under test.

nodes.label: the mkdir-is-atomic comment as root cause
nodes.rationale: eventlog.sh:70 justifies every durable-core lock on a premise that is false on Ubuntu 26.04's hybrid coreutils; 57 violations in 15 rounds of 8 racers versus 0 for GNU mkdir.
nodes.norm_label: the mkdir-is-atomic comment as root cause

nodes.label: migration of lib/eventlog.sh spin-loops onto the helper
nodes.norm_label: migration of lib/eventlog.sh spin-loops onto the helper

nodes.label: mutual-exclusion-by-occupancy regression test
nodes.rationale: The existing test detects the symptom, and only sometimes; occupancy measurement under release-contention detects the defect itself.

nodes.label: chmod 000 test inverted under root
nodes.rationale: The append-failure test forces a write failure root bypasses, so the assertion inverts under this repo's root WSL default user.

nodes.label: ordering constraint: lands before any graph-plane package
nodes.rationale: The graph plane is specified around many lanes publishing concurrently and will inherit whatever locking discipline exists when it is written; building it on a broken primitive bakes the defect in one layer deeper.
nodes.norm_label: ordering constraint: lands before any graph-plane package

nodes.label: T4 atomicity probe in the host inventory
nodes.norm_label: t4 atomicity probe in the host inventory

nodes.label: T8 OpenSpec conformance debt
nodes.rationale: All sixteen existing change packages fail openspec validate because they use ADDED Requirement: <title> where the CLI parses ADDED Requirements then Requirement then Scenario.

nodes.label: T13 lanes shall not pkill -f by pattern
nodes.rationale: pkill -f quint verify matched its own command line, killed its shell, and would have killed a sibling lane sharing the same Apalache server.
nodes.norm_label: t13 lanes shall not pkill -f by pattern

nodes.label: T14 wire the mechanism to the verdict
nodes.rationale: A probe whose verdict nothing consumes is documentation, not a control; round 1 then required evidence the fallback's only host cannot produce, making its own scenario unreachable.
nodes.norm_label: t14 wire the mechanism to the verdict

nodes.norm_label: t15 one refusal shape, six ordered causes

nodes.rationale: No Foreman-controlled MSYS2 host is available to trace, and a fabricated pin is worse than an unreachable fallback, so the register ships empty with a recorded reason.

nodes.norm_label: requirement: mutual exclusion is regression-tested by occupancy

nodes.norm_label: requirement: compaction never discards a concurrently appended event

nodes.label: Eight Vendor Contract Points
nodes.rationale: The complete set of per-vendor differences a caller must never guess: prompt delivery, write authorization, read-only enforcement, structured verdict, result capture, write evidence, config-home isolation, non-billing auth probe. Anything outside that set is not vendor-specific and does not belong in an adapter.

nodes.label: Rejected alternative: declarative vendor table
nodes.rationale: Rejected on evidence: live argv shapes are not renderings of one template (grok takes a path, codex the contents as positional, agy the contents as the value of a must-be-last flag). A data table cannot express positional-order sensitivity whose misplacement hangs rather than errors without a shell escape hatch on day one.

nodes.label: ADAPTER_ARGV array output convention
nodes.rationale: Array output exists so no argv element is ever re-interpreted by a shell; a rendered string cannot preserve that guarantee, which is why adapters stay sourced shell functions rather than subprocess executables.

nodes.label: Never-stdin invariant needs an owner
nodes.rationale: Today the rule is satisfied by luck of vendor design and stated only in a comment; it must become a property the adapters are tested for, not a rule a future author is expected to have read.

nodes.label: Argument-order hazard: agy --print hang
nodes.rationale: Worse than the stdin hazard because its failure mode is a hang, not an error: prompt as positional with a bare trailing --print produced no output for 180s and had to be killed; prompt as the value of a trailing --print answered immediately rc 0. Every layer above the adapter misreads the first case as a slow model.

nodes.label: git status --porcelain digest false negative
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-07-28: porcelain collapses an untracked directory to one '?? pkg/' line, so files 2..N inside produce a byte-identical digest, and it is blind to content changes inside untracked files. -uall fixes the first and not the second. A lane that wrote all four required package files was reported EMPTY-BURST FAILED.

nodes.label: Claude lane half-wiring
nodes.rationale: Half-wiring is worse than absence because it fails late — after the readiness gate, the worktree and queue admission — with 'unknown worker vendor', which reads like a config typo rather than a missing feature. The package forces the finish-or-remove decision and refuses the third option.

nodes.label: adapter_caps records verified CLI version
nodes.rationale: Vendor CLIs move under us: agy self-updates and moved 1.1.7 to 1.1.8 during the session this package was written. A flag set is a claim about a version, so a silent update turns a verified adapter into an unverified one with no signal unless the version is recorded and compared.

nodes.label: Frozen grok and codex implement argv
nodes.rationale: A refactor with one functional addition (the audit verb). A reviewer finding an unspecced argv difference should read it as a defect in this package, not an improvement.

nodes.label: evidence-contracts sole-ownership boundary
nodes.rationale: Before the amendment both packages claimed lib/evidence.sh and vendor-multiround.sh, which would have let incompatible helper semantics land twice. evidence-contracts implements; this package is a declared consumer supplying only adapter_implement_argv and adapter_caps.

nodes.rationale: The cap is 1 because the rule says so, not because the vendor looks risky. The plausible argument for a higher start (Go binary, per-project state, worktree-per-lane) is the same argument that would have been made for claude before the .claude.json finding; plausible arguments about concurrency safety are wrong often enough to have cost real incidents.

nodes.label: agy isolation dilemma: isolated or authenticated, not both
nodes.rationale: Two read-only probes 2026-07-28: GEMINI_CLI_HOME is a no-op for this CLI, and HOME=$T agy models relocates all state but returns rc 1 'Please sign in'. There is no topology that is simultaneously isolated and authenticated without moving credential material into each lane home.
nodes.norm_label: agy isolation dilemma: isolated or authenticated, not both

nodes.label: Shared-mutable-state monitor (SQLite plus WAL companions)
nodes.rationale: Existing monitors watch config corruption, lock freeze, auth invalidation and containment leakage — all scoped to the assumption each lane owns its own root. A shared SQLite database with -wal/-shm companions is a fifth failure surface and it fails quietly.

nodes.label: Entitlement is not authentication
nodes.rationale: For a vendor whose plan determines which models exist, a credential can be perfectly valid and unable to serve the model the auditor is pinned to. The auditors-run-at-highest-reasoning doctrine would then be unmet invisibly, while the resulting audit carries full weight in the gate.

nodes.label: Silent model downgrade is the dangerous exhaustion case
nodes.rationale: Of the three ways a quota-exhausted round can end — clean nonzero exit, hang on an interactive choice, silent downgrade to a smaller model — the third corrupts the record, because it produces an audit verdict the gate consumes at full weight from a model the architect did not choose. Defence: pin the model, record the model used, report a mismatch.
nodes.norm_label: silent model downgrade is the dangerous exhaustion case

nodes.label: Rejected: report quota as a number
nodes.rationale: Quota accounting differs per vendor (tokens, requests/day, requests/minute, seats) and a Foreman-computed number will drift from the vendor's own. What Foreman can report reliably is the observed entitlement — which models the credential can actually reach.

nodes.label: vendor_authed rc-collapse defect
nodes.rationale: Four distinct world-states — genuinely signed out, bound expired, socket/network failure, changed output matching nothing — all map onto return 1. Only the first is fixed by the login instruction the caller prints for all four; an unknown reported as a definite negative is a wrong diagnosis, not a conservative one.

nodes.label: Same shape as the lock-primitive defect
nodes.rationale: lock-primitive-hardening separates FM_LOCK_NO_ATOMIC_PRIMITIVE (disproved) from FM_LOCK_PROBE_UNTRUSTED (unproven). vendor_authed is that distinction with the second code missing. Failing closed is retained; diagnosing closed is removed.
nodes.norm_label: same shape as the lock-primitive defect

nodes.label: declared versus probed evidence classes
nodes.rationale: One predicate cannot serve four vendors: claude and codex ship status verbs, grok and agy do not. The asymmetry belongs in a table, not in per-vendor branches accumulating in one function — that is what let the grok branch drift into different failure semantics from its neighbours.

nodes.label: A changed banner degrades to unknown
nodes.rationale: A banner is a presentation detail the vendor may change in any release, not an interface contract. The two failure directions are asymmetric: reading absence-of-negative as success reports a signed-out vendor ready and fails later and more expensively; reading absence-of-positive as failure is today's bug.
nodes.norm_label: a changed banner degrades to unknown

nodes.label: The preflight must not call update
nodes.rationale: claude update installs with no dry-run flag and codex update exposes only --enable/--disable/--config; invoking either to answer 'are we current?' would upgrade a vendor CLI underneath a running release gate, after the gate's evidence was collected. Only grok update --check --json is non-mutating.
nodes.norm_label: the preflight must not call update

nodes.label: Currency as a pinned version floor
nodes.rationale: Comparing against a floor in env/reference-manifest.toml makes 'current' mean what this release requires rather than whatever the vendor shipped today — a moving target no reproducible gate can bind to. The floor is a minimum, never an assertion the resolved version was validated.
nodes.norm_label: currency as a pinned version floor

nodes.label: Setup false negative on an authenticated grok
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-07-29T14:25Z: foreman-setup.sh --profile soft printed grok not_authenticated and SETUP: NOT-READY while grok models returned exit 0 with the signed-in banner in 2.4s against a 10s bound, on a box running two concurrent Codex sessions. Setup blocked a release round on a working vendor.
nodes.norm_label: setup false negative on an authenticated grok

nodes.label: Checker-soundness thesis
nodes.rationale: A checker that cannot distinguish 'disproved' from 'could not be determined' reports the wrong one, loudly. This is the release's own thesis applied to the Setup stage.

nodes.label: Projection as a pure function of recorded inputs
nodes.rationale: Three properties follow and are the entire safety argument: it is regenerable (so the downstream store is a materialisation, not a system of record), it is verifiable (correctness becomes re-project-and-diff), and it has nowhere to put a model. Property 3 is why this is a projector and not an extractor — an extractor would have the same inputs and be free to be wrong.
nodes.norm_label: projection as a pure function of recorded inputs

nodes.label: Determinism hazards and their closing rules
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical re-projection is easy to claim and easy to lose. Enumerated hazards: wall-clock output, locale-dependent sort, hash-map iteration order, computed floats, environment leakage, non-deterministic git output, partial writes. --check is the enforcement and runs in the docs gate.
nodes.norm_label: determinism hazards and their closing rules

nodes.label: Sibling file, not rows inside graph.json
nodes.rationale: graphify --update rebuilds from the filesystem, so an injected record not derivable from a file on disk is unspecified under an incremental rebuild; injected lineage would be destroyed on a routine refresh, precisely when the ids it references change. Secondary: a 2.6 MiB tracked blob written at round frequency is a merge-conflict magnet the repo already has a scar from.
nodes.norm_label: sibling file, not rows inside graph.json

nodes.label: Rejected: graphify exporter plugin and neo4j/cypher interchange
nodes.rationale: Exporters are not a real extension point (a fork or upstream PR is required), and the graph exports drop source_file, source_location, confidence_score, hyperedges and communities — five fields survive. The audit trail is the thing being built, so an export that destroys it is not an option at any convenience.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: graphify exporter plugin and neo4j/cypher interchange

nodes.label: Symbol-refinement rule with file fallback
nodes.rationale: Step 4 (path-keyed unrepresented placeholder) exists because graph coverage is partial by measurement — 358 distinct source_file values against 471 tracked files, about 76%. A placeholder that says 'not in the graph' is honest; a silently dropped edge is a hole nothing reports.

nodes.label: Rename with lineage, never delete-plus-create
nodes.rationale: graphify ids are path-derived, so a file move re-IDs the file node and every symbol in it, making an id change ambiguous between move and delete-plus-create. Projecting it as delete-plus-create severs every historical modified edge from the thing it described — precisely the lineage this plane exists to hold.

nodes.label: graphify_version stamp on every record
nodes.rationale: An id-space migration is not hypothetical — upstream #1504 widened the stem recipe from immediate-parent to full path — and graph.json does not record the producing version, so without the stamp a cross-version id comparison is a wrong answer instead of a detectable error.

nodes.label: Deliberate divergence from R1's asymmetric publication rule
nodes.rationale: R1 pushes only improvements to the DAG, giving ~18x value density. Foreman's motivating queries are questions about the failures, which a DAG of successes cannot answer. What is adopted is the separation, not the discarding: every record carries an outcome status, so value density is paid at query time by a filter rather than at write time by a deletion.
nodes.norm_label: deliberate divergence from r1's asymmetric publication rule

nodes.label: The honest cannot-answer list
nodes.rationale: Every item is a gap in the inputs, not in the projector, and each names what would close it: spec identity (content-hash specs at dispatch), rework causality (record an addresses reference), cross-lane grouping (emit a task/spec id), human decisions, why a symbol changed (a permanent boundary), finding identity under rewording, non-durable rounds, unrepresented files, line history across a move, and truthfulness of the log itself.

nodes.label: Rejected: line numbers as identity
nodes.rationale: source_location drifts on every edit and is the unstable half of the knowledge-plane id space. Identity is the graphify node id — path plus symbol, content-independent, NFKC-normalised, casefolded — and line numbers are carried as provenance only.

nodes.label: Refused: re-modelling git commit ancestry as graph edges
nodes.rationale: Git already answers children, leaves, lineage and diff; duplicating ancestry into the projection buys nothing and adds a synchronisation failure mode. Commit references are shas, and the sha is the join to git.
nodes.norm_label: refused: re-modelling git commit ancestry as graph edges

nodes.label: Checkpoint-SHA to source_file bridge
nodes.rationale: A checkpoint is a real git commit, so git diff-tree --name-only over its SHA yields repository-relative paths that are already graphify's node key. No model, no embedding, no extraction, no inference — the reason it has not been built is that nothing writes the result anywhere.

nodes.label: No LLM may author the work plane
nodes.rationale: Measured LLM structure authorship: taxonomy F1 0.02-0.66, axioms 0.03-0.36, with a gibberish ablation showing lexical-prior matching rather than structural reasoning. Foreman's run and lane identifiers are opaque strings — exactly the adversarial input for a lexical matcher.
nodes.norm_label: no llm may author the work plane

nodes.label: No edges between runs in events.jsonl
nodes.rationale: seq and cursors are per-run; there is no index over runs, no parent-run pointer, no shared identifier between two lanes racing the same spec, and no cross-run key on a finding. So the release's motivating questions are archaeology across per-run JSON files that wt-cleanup eventually archives.
nodes.norm_label: no edges between runs in events.jsonl

nodes.label: ubuntu-latest as the practical WSL proxy
nodes.rationale: No first-party WSL GitHub Actions runner exists; ubuntu-latest (LF line endings, real bash userland) is the documented, practical stand-in for exercising WSL-shaped bash behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: ubuntu-latest as the practical wsl proxy

nodes.label: Explicit shell: bash for pipefail
nodes.rationale: The implicit non-Windows-runner default shell does not enable pipefail, so a step must declare shell: bash for set -o pipefail semantics to take effect — directly relevant because the sibling package is closing a pipefail-related bug class.

nodes.label: CI bash runs --noprofile --norc
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions bash steps never source ~/.bashrc — the same non-interactive shell shape as a foreman lane — so CI must put tool directories on PATH via its own setup steps and never assume a profile file ran.

nodes.label: Keep the windows-latest job narrow
nodes.rationale: windows-smoke.yml already covers install.ps1's Windows-native path, and windows-latest + shell: bash is framed as the Git-Bash half rather than a second WSL proxy; lint plus line-endings keeps CI time reasonable while still catching a CRLF/pipefail regression on the Windows-native shell path.

nodes.rationale: This package encodes the finished surface of the other packages rather than a moving target: it needs a build step to invoke and a line-endings test to run.

nodes.rationale: Treat 'launcher present on WSL' as a Setup-stage deliverable, not an operator-remembered manual step: skip silently when the binary exists, skip with a logged warning when bun is absent since bun absence is itself a separate tool-check finding.

nodes.label: Frozen launcher_absent degraded fallback
nodes.rationale: v0.2.7.5 explicitly froze this fallback as documented, tested contract surface; other packages and tests depend on the exact {kind:degraded,reason:launcher_absent} payload. This package works upstream of that path — make the absence rare and loud, not redesign the fallback.

nodes.rationale: Not a broken-code bug: the launcher build and the resolvers are already correct. launcher/dist/ is gitignored and build:posix is never invoked by bootstrap-wsl.sh, foreman-setup.sh or CI, so a fresh WSL clone silently runs lanes without the pidns kill-cascade that v0.2.7.5 built.
