nodes.label: wsl-preflight.sh: one script, two call sites
nodes.rationale: Detects WSL via /proc/version and exits 0 immediately off-WSL, so it is a zero-cost no-op on Windows/Git-Bash and native Linux CI. Called from foreman-setup.sh once and from lane-run.sh at lane start before any timestamped event is written, so a refusal never lets a lane begin writing under a /mnt/* FOREMAN_HOME.
nodes.norm_label: wsl-preflight.sh: one script, two call sites

nodes.label: /mnt/* FOREMAN_HOME hard refusal
nodes.rationale: The one hard invariant: store_dir/events.jsonl/stream.ndjson must live on a native filesystem for fsync integrity, and no runtime guard exists today. Scoped to /mnt/* specifically so it never fires for the legitimate Windows Git-Bash /c/... path shape.

nodes.label: WSL clock jitter guard (timedatectl set-ntp false)
nodes.rationale: WSL 2.1.1 fixed the severe sleep/resume drift that motivated the original design; the residual problem is ~1-2s dual-NTP jitter from systemd-timesyncd racing Hyper-V host time sync, whose documented fix is timedatectl set-ntp false inside the distro.
nodes.norm_label: wsl clock jitter guard (timedatectl set-ntp false)

nodes.label: Scheduled-Task clock resync demoted to optional
nodes.rationale: Demoted, not deleted: some operators may still want proactive resync, so wsl-clock-resync-task.xml stays as documented, optional tooling rather than something the preflight installs or depends on. It was the largest built-but-not-connected gap — referenced by nothing.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled-task clock resync demoted to optional

nodes.label: Conditional cross-boundary networking check
nodes.rationale: Mirrored networking is recommended, not required, because it is still receiving upstream port-tracking fixes as of 2.9.3/2.9.4; NAT plus localhostForwarding remains a valid warned-not-blocked configuration. The ::1-not-forwarded gotcha is warned about regardless of mode.

nodes.label: /mnt/c Windows shim shadowing WSL-native binaries
nodes.rationale: Same class as the already-fixed WSL codex PATH leak (appendWindowsPath=false), documented per-machine but not yet a repo-tracked guarantee. This package only detects and warns; the persistence fix belongs to the sibling wsl-tool-path-persistence package.

nodes.label: wsl-preflight change
nodes.rationale: Foreman silently depends on unchecked WSL environment invariants; one preflight script is needed before any of them can silently bite a lane.

nodes.label: /mnt/c filesystem boundary invariant
nodes.rationale: 9P/DrvFs is 2-20x slower and lacks the fsync guarantees the event-log crash-safety model needs, so FOREMAN_HOME under /mnt/* is a hard refusal.

nodes.label: WSL clock-drift pivot to residual dual-NTP jitter
nodes.rationale: The severe sleep/resume drift was fixed upstream in WSL 2.1.1 (microsoft/WSL#10006), so the heavy resync-task mechanism is no longer the right primary tool; the residual bug is ~1-2s dual-NTP jitter fixed by timedatectl set-ntp false.
nodes.norm_label: wsl clock-drift pivot to residual dual-ntp jitter

nodes.label: ::1-not-forwarded localhost gotcha
nodes.rationale: localhostForwarding (default true) makes NAT-mode callbacks work but ::1 is never forwarded; only IPv4 127.0.0.1 binds cross the boundary.

nodes.label: Windows-shim tool-resolution shadowing
nodes.rationale: grok/codex/bun/node can resolve to a /mnt/c Windows shim that shadows the intended WSL-native binary.

nodes.label: wsl-preflight.sh
nodes.rationale: Detects WSL via grep -qi microsoft /proc/version so it is a zero-cost no-op off WSL; wired into foreman-setup.sh (Setup) and lane-run.sh lane-start (Use).

nodes.label: FOREMAN_ALLOW_MNT_HOME override
nodes.rationale: A hard refusal with no escape hatch is a behavior break, so the /mnt refusal is overridable with a loud warning; the worktree stays a separate warn-only perf check.

nodes.label: realpath -m FOREMAN_HOME resolution
nodes.rationale: realpath -m handles a not-yet-created directory and symlinks; cd "$FOREMAN_HOME" && pwd requires the directory to already exist.

nodes.label: wslinfo --networking-mode detection
nodes.rationale: Prefer wslinfo --networking-mode (WSL >= 2.0.9) when present, falling back to a heuristic; warn-only, never fatal.

nodes.label: tests/wsl-preflight.bats
nodes.rationale: Covers off-WSL no-op, the /mnt refusal, the override, worktree warn-only, and that the Git-Bash /c/... shape never triggers refusal.

nodes.label: Requirement: preflight refuses an unsafe FOREMAN_HOME before any event-log write
nodes.rationale: Ordering is load-bearing: the refusal must land before any timestamped event is written, and applies to FOREMAN_HOME only because the fsync concern is specific to the event log.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: preflight refuses an unsafe foreman_home before any event-log write

nodes.label: Requirement: preflight warns on a stale WSL build
nodes.rationale: WSL < 2.1.1 predates the upstream drift fix; the warning is non-fatal and pairs with the residual dual-NTP jitter recommendation.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: preflight warns on a stale wsl build

nodes.label: Requirement: preflight warns on cross-boundary networking and tool-resolution risk
nodes.rationale: Conditional (WHERE a cross-boundary localhost dependency is configured) and warn-only, because neither networking mode nor a shimmed tool is provably fatal to every lane.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: preflight warns on cross-boundary networking and tool-resolution risk

nodes.label: wsl-seam-doctrine change
nodes.rationale: Field-learned Windows<->WSL seam rules exist as scattered partial doctrine rather than one uniform codified set, and the exec-bit trap has no guard at all.

nodes.label: Vendor-agnostic browser-callback auth doctrine
nodes.rationale: State the rule once, vendor-agnostically, so it automatically covers grok or any future vendor whose auth flow gains a browser/localhost-callback shape instead of re-deriving doctrine per vendor after the fact.

nodes.label: WSL daemon-lifecycle doctrine (restart-on-demand)
nodes.rationale: systemd=true does NOT keep the WSL VM alive, so lane-queue.sh ensure's existing respawn-if-absent is the supported model rather than a persistent daemon; document, do not change.

nodes.label: Docker Desktop WSL2 backend doctrine
nodes.rationale: Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend is the supported/verified container host; a native docker-ce install on WSL conflicts with the Desktop-managed daemon per Docker's own docs.

nodes.label: Exec-bit trap (all tracked files mode 100644)
nodes.rationale: git ls-files -s shows all 445 tracked files at 100644; harmless only because every script is invoked bash foo.sh and install.sh's chmod glob happens to cover today's scripts - one direct-exec new script away from a WSL-only Permission denied Windows can never surface.

nodes.label: lane_platform() *NT* case-arm drift
nodes.rationale: Three case "$(uname -s)" sites exist; lib/launch.sh:30 and worker-run.sh:296 include *NT* but lane-run.sh's lane_platform() does not - one-site drift, not repo-wide inconsistency, so consolidation is optional and low-risk.

nodes.label: Doctrine-first packaging decision
nodes.rationale: Three of four sub-areas need no code change because the underlying mechanisms are already correct; the gap is unwritten doctrine, so only the exec-bit guard and the optional platform consolidation touch code.

nodes.label: tests/exec-bit.bats
nodes.rationale: Asserts every tracked script invoked by direct exec is git mode 100755 or [[ -x ]]-guarded; makes the exec-bit rule executable instead of tribal.

nodes.label: Extensionless shebang-script scan class
nodes.rationale: Extensionless scripts (review-package, sdd-workspace, task-brief) are the class that hid the crlf-extensionless-hardening exec-bit trap, so the scan must not be limited to *.sh.

nodes.label: Requirement: browser-callback auth flows on WSL are operator-foreground
nodes.rationale: The local callback server dies the moment the launching shell detaches, so an orchestrator-launched detached login can never complete.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: browser-callback auth flows on wsl are operator-foreground

nodes.label: Requirement: the pueue daemon on WSL is restart-on-demand, not persistent
nodes.rationale: WSL VM idle-shutdown drops the daemon regardless of systemd=true, so respawn-on-demand is the only model that needs no Windows-side keep-alive handle.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: the pueue daemon on wsl is restart-on-demand, not persistent

nodes.label: Requirement: every directly-exec'd tracked script is executable-or-guarded
nodes.rationale: Either git mode 100755 or an [[ -x ]] guard at the call site; the documented remedy is "call via bash or add +x".
nodes.norm_label: requirement: every directly-exec'd tracked script is executable-or-guarded

nodes.label: wsl-tool-path-persistence change
nodes.rationale: Correct vendor-CLI tool resolution on WSL is an operator-remembered manual export today rather than a Setup guarantee.

nodes.label: ~/.foreman/env.sh (foreman-owned env file)
nodes.rationale: Persistence lives in an env file sourced by the lane launcher, not ~/.bashrc, so correct resolution is a property of how foreman launches lanes rather than something the operator must remember to export.

nodes.label: Non-interactive shells skip ~/.bashrc
nodes.rationale: Any PATH fix that only lives in a profile file never reaches a lane's non-interactive shell - fixing it via profile files would silently fail for exactly the lanes that need it most.

nodes.label: PATH ordering wins regardless of appendWindowsPath
nodes.rationale: appendWindowsPath=false stays an optional per-machine optimization; prepending WSL-native dirs means even a leaking distro resolves foreman-managed binaries first.
nodes.norm_label: path ordering wins regardless of appendwindowspath

nodes.label: grok readiness-probe / unit-test decoupling
nodes.rationale: timeout 10 grok models is the only exit-code-based auth signal grok has, so it stays as the live probe while unit tests move to a deterministic shim - a unit test SHALL NOT require network reachability.

nodes.label: /c/root/.local PATH snippet (Git-Bash-only)
nodes.rationale: The snippet is repeated as canonical guidance in ROADMAP.md:126 and several specs/plans but is a Git-Bash path shape and simply wrong on WSL.

nodes.label: write_authed_grok_shim seam
nodes.rationale: A deterministic always-authenticated grok stub answering --version and grok models; generalized so every unit-test path uses it while live-binary tests stay skip-guarded.

nodes.label: Requirement: vendor CLIs resolve WSL-native without relying on ~/.bashrc
nodes.rationale: Holds even when a /mnt/c Windows npm-shim path appears earlier on the inherited PATH.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: vendor clis resolve wsl-native without relying on ~/.bashrc

nodes.label: Requirement: grok-readiness UNIT tests do not depend on live grok reachability
nodes.rationale: Live network reachability is the wrong dependency for a unit test; real-binary cases stay skip-guarded and never required for the unit suite to pass.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: grok-readiness unit tests do not depend on live grok reachability

nodes.label: Foreman documentation site (dogfood)
nodes.rationale: Static single-page dogfood site; must stay aligned with skills/foreman/SKILL.md (default soft pipeline and the four roles).

nodes.label: Foreman site single-page docs
nodes.rationale: Scroll-spy is a small inline script - no external JS - so the page stays self-contained.

nodes.label: "The smart model judges. Other models type."
nodes.rationale: The one-line framing of Foreman's cost-discipline routing: the expensive session model emits judgment, cheaper cross-vendor lanes emit code.
nodes.norm_label: "the smart model judges. other models type."

nodes.label: Evidence contract (HEAD + status digests)
nodes.rationale: Implementer wrappers record HEAD and status digests before and after every run and flag unauthorized git activity; deletions/renames return as ARCHITECT_ACTIONS because the implementer must never retry them itself.

nodes.label: Fable Advisor pattern (soft-routing lineage)
nodes.rationale: Contributes architect cost discipline, five-part specs, Grok/Codex implementer agents and advisor-at-boundaries; shipped first as a Claude Code plugin by DannyMac180/fable-advisor.

nodes.label: Original Foreman design (hard-harness lineage)
nodes.rationale: Contributes worktrees, host evidence, independent checks, cold-diff audit, deterministic gate, vendor adapters and the WSL2 reference environment.

nodes.label: Vendored reference skills register
nodes.rationale: Third-party skills are vendored for a self-contained Foreman install and must never be modified locally - update by re-vendoring from upstream.

nodes.label: Vendored-skill content hash procedure
nodes.rationale: Hash is computed over sorted NUL-delimited paths with CR stripped so a CRLF checkout does not change the digest; local-overlay files (*.local.md, cookie vaults) are excluded at vendor time and never committed.

nodes.label: Foreman skill (architect/worker orchestration)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate merge of two complementary patterns - soft-mode routing and the hard harness - rather than a fork of either alone; the orchestrator owns judgment and almost never types implementation code.

nodes.label: Setup & Environment -> Use -> Cleanup lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Three ordered stages on both Windows and WSL; Use never starts until Setup reports READY for every lane it needs.

nodes.label: Setup & Environment stage
nodes.rationale: Owns tool-check, bootstrap and all vendor authentication, but never authenticates anything itself - device/interactive auth is always an operator action Setup only instructs. Idempotent.

nodes.label: Use stage (auth-readiness gate)
nodes.rationale: Enforced as a real gate, not a report: lane-run.sh refuses to spawn a not-ready vendor's command before touching the worktree lock or emitting any event, so "grok wasn't signed in" is always a Setup-stage finding.

nodes.label: Cleanup stage (foreman-cleanup.sh)
nodes.rationale: Ordered teardown that composes rather than reimplements wt-cleanup.sh; dirty-safe (uncommitted worktrees preserved, reports archived first) and never sweeps the host-wide gate.lock.

nodes.label: Soft mode (default)
nodes.rationale: Always works with no Docker/harness dependency; routes via agents/CLI and verifies in-session.

nodes.label: Hard mode (opt-in harness)
nodes.rationale: For untrusted/autonomous workers, PR-bound or security-sensitive work; all security-critical enforcement lives in scripts, not prompts.

nodes.label: Cost discipline (prime directive)
nodes.rationale: The session model is the most expensive lane, so it emits judgment not volume, keeps context lean, and reasons once before handing off.

nodes.label: Graph before files
nodes.rationale: Query the committed graphify graph with a token budget before reading sources; hop to files via source_location only where detail is needed.

nodes.label: Five-part spec contract
nodes.rationale: Implementers share none of the architect's conversation context; a spec you cannot finish writing means the decision is not made.

nodes.label: Deciding rule (implement routing)
nodes.rationale: Route on how much the outcome depends on judgment the spec cannot capture; a same-family implementer as the architect is a downgrade that must be stated explicitly.

nodes.label: Deciding rule (audit routing)
nodes.rationale: Send a cold diff plus acceptance criteria to a read-only auditor for multi-file or security-sensitive work; skip only for trivial mechanical edits when the user opts out.

nodes.label: Cross-vendor invariant (auditor vendor != worker vendor)
nodes.rationale: Never use the implementer lane to audit itself; if Codex implemented, architect review or a non-OpenAI audit substitutes and the substitution is stated, never silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Implement rounds default to worktrees
nodes.rationale: The main checkout is never an implementer target; results land through wt-merge.sh staged by default.

nodes.label: Durable rounds (v0.2.5 dispatch doctrine)
nodes.rationale: An implement round is lane-run.sh --round owning CMD -> gate -> attempt-fresh report assert -> round_done, dispatched through the queue so an agent that backgrounds-and-stops cannot strand it.

nodes.label: Verdict-to-action audit policy
nodes.rationale: Confirm the policy once, not per round: WARNING with only low-severity residuals is architect-discretion mergeable, unresolved medium+ asks the user, BLOCKED never auto-merges.

nodes.label: Reports are claims, not evidence
nodes.rationale: "Should work" or no command output is not done; wrong code goes back as a corrected spec to the cheap lane rather than being hand-patched by the architect.

nodes.label: Hard-mode task loop (INIT->PLAN->IMPLEMENT->CHECK->AUDIT->GATE->PR)
nodes.rationale: The host commits the worker's diff after the worker exits and CHECK/AUDIT run from that pristine commit; the gate fails closed if the audit CLI is missing.

nodes.label: Commitment boundaries (advisor consult)
nodes.rationale: Architecture/migration/API-shape decisions, a problem that resisted two distinct attempts, or declaring a multi-step deliverable done; act on the verdict or surface disagreement, never silently ignore it.

nodes.label: Reporting and claim discipline
nodes.rationale: Companion number, sigma before claim, and uncomputable/zero-denominator honesty are standing doctrine, not optional style; linted in shadow mode by default.

nodes.label: GraphStore port
nodes.rationale: Round 1 ships the port contract and the files-only implementation; adapter, schema freeze, ingest, concurrency and runbooks are deferred.

nodes.label: TerminusDB is a regenerable materialisation, never the system of record
nodes.rationale: GP-1..GP-5 carry no store dependency; the package serves persistent cross-run versioned query consumers only, so a DB-less files-only fallback must always exist.
nodes.norm_label: terminusdb is a regenerable materialisation, never the system of record

nodes.label: files_only default backend
nodes.rationale: No DB, no container, no network; reports time_travel, branch_merge and cross_run_query all unavailable, and an unset materialisation root means in-memory.

nodes.label: Backend-agnostic contract suite
nodes.rationale: Soundness is proven both ways: the suite must PASS against files_only and must FAIL against the deliberately broken stub.

nodes.label: Lineage queries under an emptiness contract
nodes.rationale: attempts_from_round, unevaluated_leaves and claims_contradicting are returned under an expect_empty wrapper so an empty result is asserted, not assumed.
nodes.norm_label: lineage queries under an emptiness contract

nodes.label: Optional capability protocol (query before use)
nodes.rationale: Consumers must query capabilities and degrade if absent rather than assume time-travel/branch-merge/cross-run query exists.

nodes.label: Default auditor (codex-auditor, GPT-5.6 Sol, read-only)
nodes.rationale: Auditors run at the highest reasoning level in a read-only sandbox because judgment is the point and audit is where deep reasoning pays off.

nodes.label: Auditor vendor != worker vendor invariant
nodes.rationale: Grok implements -> Codex Sol audits is the default pair; hard mode always audits with a vendor different from the worker.

nodes.label: Six audit dimensions
nodes.rationale: Acceptance, regressions, tampering, security, quality and prompt injection - tampering explicitly covers tests/CI/lockfile/harness-config edits.

nodes.label: Prompt-injection dimension (diff is untrusted data)
nodes.rationale: Diff and repo text are treated as untrusted data, and auditor output itself is untrusted input to the architect/gate rather than final authority.

nodes.label: Documentation & comments dimension (tag: docs)
nodes.rationale: BLOCKED is appropriate when documentation misstates behavior, WARNING for gaps and staleness; doctrine must be readable cold by a reader with no conversation context.

nodes.label: Audit verdict schema (APPROVED/WARNING/BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Findings are a flat list with a severity enum plus file/line/summary/evidence; the verdict maps differently in soft mode versus the hard gate.

nodes.label: Durable lanes
nodes.rationale: Instrumentation for long implementer rounds: nothing an agent produces is ever lost, progress is observable while it works, and stalls escalate instead of being silently waited on.

nodes.label: Event log (events.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Append-only single source of truth - every event lands here first, atomically, before anything else sees it; every other substrate is a disposable rebuildable view.

nodes.label: Worktree checkpoints (refs/checkpoints/<lane>)
nodes.rationale: Taken via an isolated index so the agent's own HEAD/index is never touched; each checkpoint SHA is recorded in a checkpoint event.

nodes.label: Reasoning-stream persistence (.harness/stream.ndjson)
nodes.rationale: The CLI's streaming JSON is teed to disk as it arrives so a mid-turn crash still leaves every completed tool call on disk.

nodes.label: NATS/JetStream one-way transport
nodes.rationale: Deliberately one-way (log -> NATS, never back) with Nats-Msg-Id dedup and cursor advance only after a validated PubAck, so a lost or wiped stream never loses data still in events.jsonl.

nodes.label: v1 stall watchdog (RUNNING -> STALLED -> DEAD)
nodes.rationale: Keyed on age of the lane's last liveness event and debounced by consecutive stalled ticks to avoid flapping; on DEAD it prints a kill+retry hint and exits 3 - a hint, never an automated kill.

nodes.label: resume.sh (snapshot-heavy, replay-light)
nodes.rationale: Agents are non-deterministic, so resume restores worktree state and the recorded next state rather than replaying logic.

nodes.label: Shared config loader (cfg_load / cfg_get)
nodes.rationale: Precedence is dedicated env var > TOML > built-in default; a malformed config warns once on stderr and falls back to defaults rather than aborting a caller.

nodes.label: Native-filesystem rule for durable state
nodes.rationale: store_dir, events.jsonl and stream.ndjson must live on a native filesystem and never /mnt/c/... for fsync integrity; CRLF from Windows jq.exe is stripped at every read boundary rather than assumed away.

nodes.label: lib/lock.sh lock helper
nodes.rationale: Callers never inline mkdir spin-loops; mechanism trust is earned only from a host inventory probe (syscall or pinned-mechanism evidence), never from a version string.

nodes.label: uutils mkdir is non-atomic on Ubuntu 26.04 hybrid coreutils
nodes.rationale: uutils mkdir does a userspace statx then create; 57 mutual-exclusion violations were measured across 15 rounds with 8 racers, refuting the historical "mkdir is atomic on Git Bash and WSL" claim.
nodes.norm_label: uutils mkdir is non-atomic on ubuntu 26.04 hybrid coreutils

nodes.label: Flat lock rule (no nesting, no ordering)
nodes.rationale: A stated lock ordering is standing permission to nest, and a deliberately-nesting configuration deadlocks at 5 steps under the formal model - so nested acquisition is refused outright.
nodes.norm_label: flat lock rule (no nesting, no ordering)

nodes.label: Lock timeout policy (refuse, never fail-open)
nodes.rationale: An expired bounded spin refuses with a named error; there is no fail-open path into a critical section, and a refused index update leaves index.json byte-identical.

nodes.label: el_compact serialized compaction
nodes.rationale: A unique temp file name does not fix a concurrent-append race, so compaction holds .seq.lock across snapshot and write-back and abandons if the log cannot be shown unchanged.

nodes.label: Owner-aware stale-lock reclamation
nodes.rationale: Per-lock and owner-aware, never a directory sweep, never while a live holder cannot be ruled out, never when the mechanism is indeterminate - and never silent.

nodes.label: Lock-atomicity pin register
nodes.rationale: An empty pin register is deliberate when no real trace was captured - a fabricated digest is worse than an unreachable fallback, so msys2-git-bash durable lanes are unavailable rather than silently locked out.

nodes.label: Decision-lineage event vocabulary
nodes.rationale: audit_verdict, finding, finding_outcome, gate_decision and late usage are additive free-string types requiring no library change; finding_outcome never rewrites the original finding.

nodes.label: Event-payload safety rule
nodes.rationale: Payloads carry hashes, ids, counts and references - never prompt text, diff text or file contents; emit failures log to stderr and never change a gate or round outcome.

nodes.label: durable-preflight.sh dependency check
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for which durable-lanes dependencies are present, printing install hints rather than failing opaquely later; the NATS bats suite skips visibly rather than silently passing.

nodes.label: Five-part spec template
nodes.rationale: Objective/Files/Interfaces/Constraints/Verification copied into every soft-mode delegation and hard-mode task handoff.

nodes.label: Standing constraints (copy into every spec)
nodes.rationale: Git writes banned, no deletions/renames (they go to ARCHITECT_ACTIONS), worktree-only writes, no network unless granted, and docs/comments are part of the deliverable.

nodes.label: Spec quality bar
nodes.rationale: If Interfaces or Verification cannot be filled in, architect work is unfinished; one task per spec when files overlap, parallelize only independent specs.

nodes.label: EARS phrasing (required for Grok-bound specs)
nodes.rationale: Fixed clause order and a closed keyword set measurably reduce implementer drift across the six patterns (ubiquitous, event-driven, state-driven, optional, unwanted, complex).

nodes.label: Reference set index
nodes.rationale: SKILL.md's References section stays authoritative for the skill body; this index is the cross-linked lifecycle-stage map for readers arriving from README or docs/USAGE who want the detail behind a claim.

nodes.label: Soft-mode lane table
nodes.rationale: Maps each lane to its producer model, Claude agent and headless CLI form so a lane is never invoked under another vendor's name.

nodes.label: Default pairing (Grok implements, Codex Sol audits)
nodes.rationale: The architect re-runs checks between implement and audit; if Codex implemented, codex-auditor must not be called and the substitution is stated explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: default pairing (grok implements, codex sol audits)

nodes.label: Grok worker flags (soft)
nodes.rationale: --prompt-file rather than shell-interpolating large specs; --allow Write/Edit auto-approves file writes only while shell stays gated; single-burst prompt files mean write-first specs.

nodes.label: grok --permission-mode acceptEdits is silently ignored
nodes.rationale: The CLI accepts the flag value then ignores it, so every write is prompt-cancelled while the model narrates success - a zero-change evidence digest is the cancelled-writes signal.

nodes.label: Grok headless recipe (lane-run)
nodes.rationale: --output-format json, --always-approve, a fresh per-round --session-id and --no-auto-update (required in any automated environment); GROK_HOME is set per lane and never shared.

nodes.label: Grok auth doctrine (Setup-stage only)
nodes.rationale: grok login --device-code is browser-free (alias of --device-auth) or XAI_API_KEY; a Use lane requested while Setup reports grok NOT-READY is refused at the door and never attempts its own auth.

nodes.label: grok lane secrets-refusal scan
nodes.rationale: WHILE Grok Build's whole-repo-upload behavior is unrefuted, lane-run.sh scans worktree source for .env files and private-key material and refuses the lane before ever spawning grok.

nodes.label: Codex auth doctrine (headless vs interactive)
nodes.rationale: --device-auth falls back to a localhost:1455 callback whose server dies when the launching shell detaches, so it must be operator-run in a persistent foreground shell; headless uses --with-api-key piped on stdin, never as an argument.

nodes.label: Codex reasoning-effort policy
nodes.rationale: Implementers run medium because the spec determines the outcome and high reasoning is wasted wall-clock risking the 600s timeout; auditors always run high because judgment is the point.

nodes.label: Codex auditor flags (read-only)
nodes.rationale: --sandbox read-only is mandatory (never workspace-write for audit) and git status --porcelain must show no auditor mutations after the run.

nodes.label: Grok as verified default-eligible implementer
nodes.rationale: The 2026-07-18 live authenticated T5b destructive-concurrency run came back GREEN at N=2 and N=3, raising grok's pueue cap to 3; eligibility does not change the standing-era default pairing.

nodes.label: Missing CLI -> STATUS: unavailable, never substitute
nodes.rationale: Silently substituting the host model under another lane's name would fake cross-vendor independence, so a missing CLI reports unavailable with an install hint instead.
nodes.norm_label: missing cli -> status: unavailable, never substitute

nodes.label: Hard-mode vendor adapters
nodes.rationale: Adapters normalize run_worker to an event log plus result envelope and run_audit to a verdict JSON; Grok emits streaming-json while Claude emits stream-json.

nodes.label: .foreman/config.toml lane configuration
nodes.rationale: Worker vendor must differ from the orchestrator in hard mode and audit vendor must differ from the worker; an empty audit vendor auto-prefers codex when the worker is grok.

nodes.label: Known limits per CLI (soft, headless)
nodes.rationale: Grok has no headless shell approver so it cannot delete/rename/chmod or run commands and may narrate success without writing; codex workspace-write blocks network installs; neither has conversation context.

nodes.label: Orchestration hardening (v0.2.5)
nodes.rationale: Operator doc for what v0.2.5 adds on top of the v0.2.0 durable-lanes foundation; everything is derived from merged script headers and code, with cited file paths as the authoritative source.

nodes.label: foreman-launch launcher contract
nodes.rationale: A compiled self-contained TypeScript-on-Bun binary owns a spawned command's whole process tree instead of leaving that to bash job control; exit 124 is timeout, 125 is launcher error.

nodes.label: Graded stop (no cooperative phase)
nodes.rationale: CTRL_BREAK is impossible via Bun.spawn and CMD's stdin is already /dev/null, so there is no cooperative-shutdown phase to attempt - wait --grace then hard-kill via TerminateJobObject or SIGKILL to the process group.

nodes.label: Frozen heartbeat schema
nodes.rationale: launcher_pid is the kill-shot target, pid is CMD's root child and POSIX pgid, job_id is the Windows Job Object handle or the same value as pid on POSIX; a final alive:false line closes the file.

nodes.label: --detach handoff (heartbeat-file reset)
nodes.rationale: The heartbeat file is emptied before self-re-exec because a stale line from a prior --detach run could false-succeed the handoff poll; the detached copy becomes the sole writer.

nodes.label: Nested Job Objects (one level validated)
nodes.rationale: Round ownership creates a launcher-spawning-launchers chain; a bats case confirms killing the outer launcher kernel-reaps the inner launcher's own job, but only one nesting level is validated.

nodes.label: POSIX pidns-init teardown
nodes.rationale: Self-re-exec under unshare --pid --mount-proc --fork --kill-child makes the launcher PID 1 of a fresh namespace, so kernel pidns semantics reap the whole tree including setsid-detached escapees a pgid-only kill would miss; probe-then-fallback logs a DEGRADED marker, never silently.

nodes.label: NTSTATUS masking (accepted ambiguity)
nodes.rationale: A Windows child dying with an NTSTATUS code surfaces byte-masked as a small exit code that can collide with a legitimate one; there is no reliable recovery, so it is documented rather than silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Never stdbuf the launcher
nodes.rationale: stdbuf's LD_PRELOAD is rewritten to Windows form at the msys->native exec boundary, so CMD's own bash dies dlopen-ing a "C:" string while lane-run.sh still exits 0; the launcher already forwards stdio unbuffered so stdbuf is redundant anyway.

nodes.label: Round ownership (lane-run.sh --round)
nodes.rationale: round_done fires only when the gate exits 0 and the report is attempt-fresh (mtime newer than the round's prompt event, or an attempt-id marker), so a prior round's report can never satisfy the predicate.

nodes.label: watch.sh v2 typed-state machine
nodes.rationale: Typed states (QUEUED, STARTING, RUNNING_IMPL, VERIFYING, WAITING_CHILD, AGENT_ABANDONED, SUCCEEDED/FAILED) wrap the frozen v1 machine; VERIFYING gets its own larger bound because verifying is not stalled.

nodes.label: Liveness is heartbeat + event log, never file mtime
nodes.rationale: A bats gate writes scratch to /tmp, so a lane running only its own test file produces zero worktree writes for the whole gate phase - the exact blind spot a worktree-mtime probe hits.
nodes.norm_label: liveness is heartbeat + event log, never file mtime

nodes.label: WATCH_OWNERSHIP_WAIT round-watcher doctrine
nodes.rationale: The value is milliseconds: deployments must arm 25000 to match lane_emit_ownership's ~20s bound, because a bare 25 means 25ms and defeats the window; the shipped 3000 default only protects frozen v1 wall-clock bats scales.

nodes.label: pueue admission control (lane-queue.sh)
nodes.rationale: Fixed group topology created idempotently by ensure, with misc's parallelism set explicitly rather than inheriting pueue's incidental default.

nodes.label: gate group host-wide bats mutex
nodes.rationale: Concurrent bats suites corrupting wall-clock tests was the most frequent failure class in bugeventlog.md; parallel=1 makes serialization structural instead of relying on discipline, removing the human-judgment failure point.

nodes.label: Per-shell pueue quoting layer
nodes.rationale: argv boundaries never survive pueue add, and PowerShell quote-doubling silently deletes a quote under POSIX quoting - so the dialect is chosen once per add from the client binary and an unrecognized shell_command fails fast rather than guessing.

nodes.label: pueue-absent degraded fallback
nodes.rationale: add degrades to a foreground spawn with a stderr degraded marker while ensure/status/kill fail loudly; the fallback keys strictly on binary absence so a daemon that dies after ensure fails loudly, never silently.

nodes.label: Vendor config isolation (LANE_VENDOR)
nodes.rationale: The mapped vendor home is exported once before CMD is spawned on both spawn branches and normalized via cygpath -m, replacing reliance on bash's disk-state-dependent msys->native conversion (Bun #12970 strips backslashes from env values).

nodes.label: T5b real-vendor destructive concurrency verdict
nodes.rationale: Caps are raised only to a green recorded N (grok 3, codex 2) and never on fake-shim plumbing tests alone; the protocol is manual, destructive and never gated into CI, and codex N=3 stays unrun.

nodes.label: Merge-freshness gate (merge-gate.sh)
nodes.rationale: record emits a merge_base event (degraded to HEAD when origin/main is absent) and check verifies resolvability, ancestry and staleness; it prints one line and never rebases or force-merges - no auto-salvage.

nodes.label: Corrupt event log yields a clean NOT_MERGEABLE
nodes.rationale: T7 hardening: pre-fix, an unguarded pipeline assignment's nonzero rc tripped set -e before the empty-sha check ever ran, turning a torn log line into an uncontracted script abort.
nodes.norm_label: corrupt event log yields a clean not_mergeable

nodes.label: wt-merge.sh porcelain -z hardening
nodes.rationale: The add-list is built from status --porcelain because naming a genuinely ignored path in a pathspec errors; the NUL-delimited read with core.quotePath=false carries exact original bytes so an unusual filename is not re-added under an octal-escaped wrong name.

nodes.label: Auto-resume supervisor (lane-supervise.sh)
nodes.rationale: A single sweep with no internal poll loop and no new state store, run on a fixed external interval; it classifies each lane's latest round as the structural suffix of its events from the last prompt, since most event types carry no attempt id.

nodes.label: ABANDONED predicate and never-rules
nodes.rationale: ALIVE means the owning pid answers kill -0 or the lane.lock directory exists; a launcher-absent round has no recoverable worktree pointer and is deliberately out of scope - never blind-resume without a known worktree, and a dirty-tree refusal never counts toward the retry cap.

nodes.label: [audit.policy] config keys
nodes.rationale: Closes the 2026-07-16 merge-gate-semantics item where a standing "merge when approved" instruction collided with a WARNING because no doctrine distinguished which WARNINGs were architect-discretion-mergeable.

nodes.label: Closed-allowlist config loader
nodes.rationale: A key present in only one of the TOML parser case statement or the env-var table silently no-ops, so every new key must be added to both.

nodes.label: [audit.policy] is doctrine-only, not wired into gate-eval.sh
nodes.rationale: A real wire-in needs resolved-vs-unresolved finding bucketing that verdict.schema.json has no field for, and the gate never fails on a bare WARNING today - so it is deliberately left a v0.3.0 consumer, stated rather than silently assumed.
nodes.norm_label: [audit.policy] is doctrine-only, not wired into gate-eval.sh

nodes.label: git-guards.sh repo-local guard bundle
nodes.rationale: Idempotently applies five repo-LOCAL settings including maintenance.auto=false, which stops the reactive gc.autoDetach background fork competing for the object-DB lock mid-commit.

nodes.label: Deliberate refusal of git maintenance start
nodes.rationale: Probing showed it installs real host-wide Windows Scheduled Tasks that ignore HOME redirection when they later run, so it is untestable and unrevertable from a bootstrap script; register alone is inert, so git-guards.sh itself is the throttled foreman-owned maintenance tick.
nodes.norm_label: deliberate refusal of git maintenance start

nodes.label: git_retry bounded exponential backoff
nodes.rationale: Rides out a transient index.lock from a concurrent process; the exit status must be captured as if cmd; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi because an if with no else that takes its false branch itself exits 0, and the command must be the if's own condition or set -e aborts on the first failure.

nodes.label: wt_sweep_stale_locks
nodes.rationale: Removes only 0-byte, older-than-threshold *.lock files - never a non-empty or fresh lock a live process may hold - and runs at lane start in both wt-new.sh and lane-run.sh.

nodes.label: Scoped GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS / GIT_ASK_YESNO
nodes.rationale: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is scoped to two read-only polls and never the worktree-add write path; GIT_ASK_YESNO=false is safe lane-wide because it only affects an interactive retry prompt that would otherwise hang with no TTY.

nodes.label: wt-cleanup.sh SIGINT-before-remove ordering
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing after the 2026-07-16 shutdown-ordering failure: SIGINT (escalating to SIGKILL, since plain SIGINT is unreliable on this Windows/MSYS host) always precedes git worktree remove, and only for a worktree actually about to be removed.

nodes.label: Windows Defender exclusion doctrine
nodes.rationale: Real-time scanning of .git internals is a measured stall/unlink cause, but modifying exclusions needs elevation this harness does not assume - so a wildcard *-wt-* parent-directory exclusion is documented operator guidance, not automated.

nodes.label: Hard-mode shipped path (worker-run.sh + pr-open.sh)
nodes.rationale: Heartbeats batch-mirror into the event log in a single post-exit pass (no background tail/FIFO/lock race), add -A precedes the diff so untracked files are captured, and only a host-side stage commits.

nodes.label: launcher-only profile (env -i allowlist)
nodes.rationale: From-scratch env allowlist gives process/filesystem/home isolation but explicitly NOT network isolation - the worker shares the host's network stack.

nodes.label: container profile (devcontainer + default-deny egress)
nodes.rationale: A .git-less archive copy runs with capabilities dropped, read-only rootfs and no docker.sock; narrowing is a default-deny iptables OUTPUT policy with a two-host allowlist applied as root before gosu-dropping. Sync-back must be delete-aware and exclude .git, which --delete would otherwise remove.

nodes.label: pr-open.sh token-safe PR path
nodes.rationale: Refuses without an explicit PAT (no ambient-credential fallback) and on non-HTTPS github remotes; pushes via a 0700 GIT_ASKPASS helper unlinked afterwards so the token never appears in process argv, and never runs gh pr ready.

nodes.label: Mandatory usage.source field
nodes.rationale: vendor_reported / estimated / unavailable: with unavailable the numeric fields are absent, never zero, and estimated figures never mix into a total without their own subtotal.

nodes.label: 2026-07-29 vendor usage-reporting probe
nodes.rationale: grok 0.2.114 yields no stable per-round usage object in the harness path, codex 0.146.0 is partial (exec --json can emit it but default argv does not guarantee it), claude 2.1.x has no harness-facing channel - so unavailable is the honest default.

nodes.label: Structured model identity (requested_alias + cli_version)
nodes.rationale: What the run asked for and what the binary reported are recorded as separate fields because they are not the same thing.

nodes.label: Known limits carried into v0.3.0
nodes.rationale: codex N=3 unrun, audit.policy unenforced by the gate, one-level nesting validation, and a bats-scale WATCH_OWNERSHIP_WAIT default that is not the deployment recommendation.

nodes.label: Git worktrees as the multi-agent isolation primitive
nodes.rationale: One object store, many checkouts: each agent gets its own directory and branch so there are no file collisions, and the architect consolidates reports before cleanup.
nodes.norm_label: git worktrees as the multi-agent isolation primitive

nodes.label: Worktree fan-out lifecycle
nodes.rationale: tool-check -> wt-new (flock-serialized, because git worktree add has a known lock race) -> parallel agents -> per-tree reports -> wt-consolidate -> decide -> wt-merge -> wt-cleanup.

nodes.label: Architect rules for parallel fan-out
nodes.rationale: Partition first (never parallelize same-file writers), spawn independent agents in one turn, consolidate before trusting any single report, and never mount the run-dir secrets into untrusted workers.

nodes.label: foreman.worktree-report.v1 schema
nodes.rationale: Every agent must write FOREMAN_REPORT.md/.json in its own tree before exit; the audit role may nest the standard verdict/findings inside it.

nodes.label: Host run dir outside every worktree
nodes.rationale: Reports are copied to ~/.foreman/runs/<RUN_ID>/ so the audit trail is durable independent of worktree lifetime, and secrets never sit inside a worker-visible tree.
nodes.norm_label: host run dir outside every worktree

nodes.label: Stateful / live-target profile
nodes.rationale: When runtime state lives outside the checkout, a fresh worktree has none of it, so an implementer either fails immediately or silently drifts against a target it cannot exercise; read-only roles are usually still fine in a tree.

nodes.label: soft_mode.target = live guard
nodes.rationale: wt-new.sh reads the key before any worktree is created and refuses with EXIT_CONFIG when it resolves to live; the default (absent or any other value) behaves exactly as before.

nodes.label: Live-target trade-off (correctness vs isolation)
nodes.rationale: Buys correctness against real external state at the cost of parallel-lane isolation and durable worktree checkpoints - one lane at a time, changes land straight in the working checkout, and it is never a substitute for hard mode's containment.

nodes.label: Reference environment (Windows + WSL2)
nodes.rationale: WSL2 Ubuntu is a co-equal fully-provisioned environment running the same three-stage lifecycle identically to Windows, with WSL-native tooling rather than a subset.

nodes.label: soft / hard / full profiles
nodes.rationale: env/reference-manifest.toml is the source of truth for which tools each profile requires.

nodes.label: Pre-implementation gate (architect duty)
nodes.rationale: Inventory -> report -> install (ask once) -> re-check, and only then write specs and spawn implementers; never start an implementer or hard INIT while must-tools are missing. Auth is never automated.

nodes.label: /usr/local/bin symlink strategy
nodes.rationale: Every WSL-native binary is symlinked into /usr/local/bin, which precedes /usr/bin in WSL's compiled-in PATH even under env -i, so tools resolve the same for a non-interactive, non-login invocation that never sources ~/.bashrc.

nodes.label: Codex auth: headless vs interactive (v0.2.8.1)
nodes.rationale: --device-auth's localhost:1455 callback is documented here specifically to explain why it must stay operator-run; it is NOT a headless option, and headless auth pipes the key on stdin.

nodes.label: appendWindowsPath=false interop fix
nodes.rationale: The default true leaked the Windows npm shim onto WSL's PATH, so codex crashed on a win32-gated optional dependency the Linux runtime can never satisfy; the fix is a WSL-native @latest install (forcing per-platform optionalDependency re-resolution) plus disabling the leak. Re-probe with wsl --shutdown, which is a VM restart, not data loss.

nodes.label: No Windows tool needs the WSL interop PATH
nodes.rationale: foreman-launch.exe is resolved relative to the repo root rather than by PATH lookup, and the staged pueue.exe / lychee.exe paths are Windows-host-context only - never reached through interop.
nodes.norm_label: no windows tool needs the wsl interop path

nodes.label: .wslconfig tuning (processors, memory, autoMemoryReclaim)
nodes.rationale: processors=20 reserves host CPU headroom as a wall-clock-flake mitigation for concurrent bats suites - it reduces, not replaces, contention alongside the gate mutex; memory=64GB stays as a host-starvation guard and virtiofs is deliberately not enabled.

nodes.label: Mirrored networking + dnsTunneling (verified active)
nodes.rationale: Verified by three independent signals: wslinfo reports mirrored, ip addr shows the host's real adapters instead of a single NAT'd eth0, and resolv.conf's 10.255.255.254 is the dnsTunneling proxy sentinel rather than a NAT gateway.

nodes.label: sparseVhd retroactive conversion refused
nodes.rationale: The setting only governs newly created disks; converting this pre-existing ext4.vhdx needed --allow-unsafe after a data-corruption warning, and a data-corruption warning is not a call to override silently.

nodes.label: env/wsl-clock-preflight.sh (reactive guard)
nodes.rationale: A drifted guest clock would corrupt the event log's timestamp-ordering invariants, so past a threshold it resyncs or refuses rather than letting a timestamped write proceed; a fully injectable clock seam lets tests mock skew without touching the real system clock. Not yet wired into lane start.

nodes.label: env/wsl-clock-resync-task.xml (proactive resume hook)
nodes.rationale: Fires on the standard resume-from-sleep power event; XML validated but deliberately NOT live-registered because Register-ScheduledTask is a persistent host-wide change - document the blocker, do not force it. Hardcoding -u root also makes it default-user-migration safe.

nodes.label: root -> non-root migration inventory
nodes.rationale: Inventory only, so the follow-up change starts from probe-verified facts rather than guesses: /root is 0700 so all ten /usr/local/bin symlinks would silently dangle, docker group membership and NOPASSWD sudo are root-implicit, and no non-root human account exists yet.

nodes.label: Re-provision-as-new-user migration shape
nodes.rationale: chown -R of a 4.6G multi-project home is higher risk than re-running the skip-if-present idempotent bootstrap as the new user, which reprovisions foreman's tools under the new $HOME without touching root's copies; FOREMAN_HOME is already $HOME-relative so the risk is losing run history, not a code dependency on /root.

nodes.label: Release metrics reference
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for metric definitions and claim discipline; it names formulas, companions, misreadings, gaming vectors and sample floors but deliberately does not compute anything.

nodes.label: Two uncomputable render forms
nodes.rationale: Blocked input and zero denominator are distinct strings, and neither is a pass, a target met, an improvement or a zero; a blank cell, placeholder 0/0%/100%, n/a or omitted row is not a valid render.

nodes.label: Sigma definition and minimum sample sizes
nodes.rationale: Sigma is the standard deviation across repeated measurement windows of unchanged code; there is no single global n, and until enough windows exist comparative language is forbidden.
nodes.norm_label: sigma definition and minimum sample sizes

nodes.label: v0.2.9 active metric set
nodes.rationale: M2/M3/M4/M7/M8 active, M1/M6 excluded, M5 owned elsewhere, M9-M13 deferred - and a report must not describe the active set as fully computed, since two of the five depend on partial usage/phase fields.

nodes.label: M1 - first-pass gate rate
nodes.rationale: Excluded from v0.2.9 because its companion - architect-authored share of merged lines - has no instrumentation, and without it an architect hand-editing the bulk of a change is invisible.

nodes.label: M2 - rounds-to-green distribution
nodes.rationale: The three figures (p50, p90, abandoned fraction) ARE the companion structure - publishing p50 alone hides a long tail and lets hard tasks be culled before they inflate p90.

nodes.label: M3 - cost per merged change
nodes.rationale: Counts every attempt including abandoned ones; unavailable usage means absent numerics, never $0, and a winning-attempt-only figure must be labelled M3-optimistic and never published as M3.

nodes.label: M4 - wall-clock split by phase
nodes.rationale: Five MECE buckets because the four named phases alone are not exhaustive; the explicit unaccounted bucket is what exposes idle time folded into implement.

nodes.label: M5 - cross-vendor auditor unique-catch rate (pointer only)
nodes.rationale: No aggregate form is ever permitted: counter-evidence shows ~2 effective independent votes across nine frontier models, with aggregation recovering at most ~11% of an 8-22pp deficit, so a collapsed aggregate would erase the differentiation the multi-vendor design must prove or refute.
nodes.norm_label: m5 - cross-vendor auditor unique-catch rate (pointer only)

nodes.label: M6 - escaped-defect rate per 1k merged lines
nodes.rationale: Excluded: no mechanical defect-to-merge linkage exists, and merges younger than the fixed trailing 14-day window must be excluded entirely rather than counted as clean.
nodes.norm_label: m6 - escaped-defect rate per 1k merged lines

nodes.label: M7 - lane mortality per 100 lane-starts
nodes.rationale: Computable today from alert kinds over ownership events, but it includes intentional cancels and tightened timeouts - so the maintainer-initiated vs unattended split is mandatory to stop fail-fast ops work reading as fragility.

nodes.label: M8 - evidence completeness
nodes.rationale: Artifact presence and schema validity only - an empty-but-valid verdict passes it, so it must never be read as audit thoroughness; the report must state whether the event or interim file basis was used.

nodes.label: M9 - verdict distribution (deferred)
nodes.rationale: More APPROVED may mean weaker auditors, not better quality; softening the auditor prompt is the gaming vector.

nodes.label: M10 - auditor-architect agreement (Cohen's kappa) (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Blocked by a real gap: the architect ship decision is not yet a structured event, and high kappa can mean the architect is rubber-stamping the auditor rather than that audits are redundant.

nodes.label: M11 - flake rate (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Low flake may mean shallow tests, and deleting flaky tests is the gaming vector caught by a test-count delta companion.

nodes.label: M12 - budget consumed vs declared (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Declared budget is not yet a standard event field, and under-budget means nothing when usage is mostly unavailable.

nodes.label: M13 - prediction-hold rate (deferred)
nodes.rationale: No prediction instrumentation exists, and a high hold rate under self-selected easy tasks says nothing about planning accuracy.

nodes.label: Claim discipline (standing rules)
nodes.rationale: Companion number, sigma before claim, smaller-than-sigma is noise, uncomputable is not a result, zero denominator is not a pass, no automated gaming classification, and a blocked string must name a package that still exists.

nodes.label: metrics-lint.sh (shadow by default)
nodes.rationale: Enforces companion adjacency, sigma-before-claim, uncomputable honesty and zero-denominator guards; ships in shadow mode (report and exit 0) so adoption never blocks a build until enforce is chosen.
