nodes.norm_label: sdd task-scoped review dispatch implementation plan

nodes.label: Per-Session Secret Key (A1)
nodes.rationale: A Host allowlist only defends the loopback browser confused-deputy; a direct remote client sends the expected Host, so the allowlist is theater for remote exposure. A random crypto.randomBytes(32) token carried as ?key and bootstrapped into a per-port HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie authenticates clients uniformly across loopback, SSH tunnel and direct-remote, and also defeats DNS rebinding.

nodes.label: Host Allowlist Dropped, WS Origin Retained (A2)
nodes.rationale: Subsumed by the secret key: one mechanism closes WS injection, DNS-rebinding reads and cross-origin WS. No BRAINSTORM_ALLOWED_HOSTS. The browser Origin check is still kept after session auth so a cross-origin localhost tab cannot ride the companion cookie.
nodes.norm_label: host allowlist dropped, ws origin retained (a2)

nodes.label: Null WebSocket Payload Crashes Server (A3)
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse('null') yields null and null.choice throws outside the try/catch that wraps decodeFrame, so any local client can kill the process. Fix is the minimal guard if (event && event.choice); a top-level try/catch or uncaughtException handler would mask other bugs.

nodes.label: Frame-Length Bound in decodeFrame (A4)
nodes.rationale: MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD_BYTES of 10MB is already enforced before any Buffer.alloc, so the action is to verify the issue against current dev and close it rather than re-implement.

nodes.label: Dotfile Screens Rejected (B1)
nodes.rationale: macOS/ExFAT resource-fork files like ._screen.html pass an endsWith('.html') filter and can sort newest, serving binary metadata as the mockup. All four read sites must reject names starting with a dot.

nodes.label: stop-server.sh Can Kill a Reused PID (B2)
nodes.rationale: After a reboot or PID wraparound the pid file can point at an unrelated process that would then be SIGKILLed. Ownership must be proven before signalling, and the script must fail closed with stale_pid when it cannot be proven.
nodes.norm_label: stop-server.sh can kill a reused pid (b2)

nodes.label: WebSocket Reconnect Backoff and Status Indicator (B3)
nodes.rationale: A fixed 1s reconnect timer with no onerror handler plus a hardcoded 'Connected' status shows a live indicator over a dead socket. Fix is exponential backoff 500ms to 30s cap and a --status-color custom property so JS can drive Connected/Reconnecting/Disconnected.
nodes.norm_label: websocket reconnect backoff and status indicator (b3)

nodes.label: Configurable Idle Timeout and WS Close on Shutdown (C1)
nodes.rationale: A hardcoded 30-minute idle timeout kills the server mid-question while the user thinks, and shutdown() never closes upgraded sockets so an open browser can keep the process alive.
nodes.norm_label: configurable idle timeout and ws close on shutdown (c1)

nodes.label: Server Death Invisible to User and Agent (C2)
nodes.rationale: Neither the browser nor the agent learns that the companion exited, so both keep acting on stale state; a tombstone marker plus a paused overlay makes death observable.
nodes.norm_label: server death invisible to user and agent (c2)

nodes.label: Alpine.js Vendoring Dropped (E3)
nodes.rationale: Vendoring an interactive-mockup framework reintroduces the supply-chain cost the zero-dependency server removed, so the PR is dropped rather than merged.

nodes.label: Task: Helper Uses Stored Key For Reconnect
nodes.norm_label: task: helper uses stored key for reconnect

nodes.label: RED/GREEN Task Loop
nodes.rationale: Every task adds failing tests first, verifies RED, implements the minimal change, then verifies GREEN, so the plan leaves automated evidence for each security claim instead of prose assertions.

nodes.label: Task: Server Instance ID Ownership Proof
nodes.norm_label: task: server instance id ownership proof

nodes.label: Skip-Aware, Fixed-Port Test Hardening
nodes.rationale: Tests must assert they started on the expected fixed port so they cannot silently pass against a fallback process, and symlink/hardlink assertions must skip rather than fail on hosts (Windows-like) that cannot create usable links.

nodes.label: Chunk-by-Chunk Plan Review Loop
nodes.rationale: Plans are reviewed per chunk (delimited by '## Chunk N' headings, each under 1000 lines) so each chunk is self-contained enough to review independently and the reviewer can compare it against the spec path it is handed.

nodes.label: Review Loop Termination and Disagreement Handling
nodes.rationale: No hard iteration cap; reviewers are advisory rather than blocking. Escalate to the human after 5 loop iterations, 3 iterations of the same disagreement, or 2 malformed reviewer outputs.
nodes.norm_label: review loop termination and disagreement handling

nodes.label: Browser Displays, Terminal Converses
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's execution model is turn-based and cannot listen on two channels in one turn, so blocking TaskOutput seized the TUI and made the browser the only input channel. Splitting roles - browser as interactive display, terminal as always-unblocked conversation channel - removes background tasks, polling and timeout management entirely.

nodes.label: Per-Screen .events Interaction Stream
nodes.rationale: One JSON object per line, append-only within a screen and cleared when a new HTML file is detected, so the agent sees the user's whole exploration path rather than only the final selection and never inherits stale events.

nodes.label: Deletion of wait-for-feedback.sh
nodes.rationale: Its only job was bridging server stdout events to the agent; the .events file does that directly, so the polling script and its 600s timeout / 30-minute cap logic are deleted.

nodes.label: Comment-Placeholder Content Injection
nodes.rationale: Anchoring injection on a regex over the feedback-footer div breaks when that div is removed; a single CONTENT comment marker replaced by string substitution is simpler and survives template reformatting.

nodes.label: Zero-Dependency server.js
nodes.rationale: Vendoring 714 node_modules files (express, ws, chokidar) into git freezes dependencies out of security patches and commits unaudited third-party code; a single ~300-line file on Node built-ins removes that supply-chain risk. The file doubles as a require()-able module so WebSocket protocol functions can be unit-tested.

nodes.label: RFC 6455 Text-Frame-Only Subset
nodes.rationale: Binary frames, fragmentation, permessage-deflate and subprotocols are deliberately skipped: they are unnecessary for small localhost JSON messages, and extensions/subprotocols are negotiated in the handshake so never advertising them means they are never active.

nodes.label: fs.watch With Per-Filename Debounce
nodes.rationale: fs.watch replaces chokidar because it is reliable for a single flat directory on macOS, Linux and Windows; a ~100ms per-filename debounce suppresses the duplicate events those platforms emit. New files clear .events, changes do not.

nodes.label: server-started JSON and .server-info File
nodes.rationale: The same startup JSON is written to a file as well as stdout so agents can recover port, url and screen_dir when the server was backgrounded and stdout is hidden.

nodes.label: Read-Only Git Environment Detection
nodes.rationale: Three side-effect-free commands (git-dir, git-common-dir, branch --show-current) classify the workspace. git-dir != git-common-dir is preferred over show-toplevel because submodules would produce a false positive, and cd && pwd -P normalizes the relative-vs-absolute git-common-dir result plus macOS /tmp symlinks.

nodes.label: Detached-HEAD Handoff Payload
nodes.rationale: In a Codex App workspace-write sandbox, checkout -b, push and gh pr create are all blocked, so the skill cannot offer the normal menu. It instead commits, prints the HEAD sha with a loss warning, and hands the user a suggested branch name and commit message for the host application's own controls.

nodes.label: Late-Detected Sandbox Fallback
nodes.rationale: If detection says a normal repo but 'git worktree add -b' then fails on a Seatbelt permission error, treat it as a restricted environment discovered late and fall back to the already-in-workspace behavior instead of aborting.

nodes.label: Detect State, Not Platform
nodes.rationale: Sniffing environment variables to identify the harness needs maintenance for every new harness; git-dir != git-common-dir is a stable git primitive since 2.5 (2015), works universally, and needs zero upkeep as new harnesses appear.

nodes.label: Provenance-Based Worktree Ownership
nodes.rationale: Whoever created the worktree owns cleanup. Paths under .worktrees/ or worktrees/ belong to superpowers; .claude/worktrees/, ~/.codex/worktrees/ and .gemini/worktrees/ belong to the harness and are left alone, which prevents phantom state in both directions.

nodes.label: Defer to Native Harness Worktree Tools
nodes.rationale: Claude Code, Codex App, Gemini CLI and Cursor all ship native worktree support with their own paths and lifecycles, so the skill duplicates, conflicts, or creates invisible state. It keeps the git fallback only for harnesses that lack native support.
nodes.norm_label: defer to native harness worktree tools

nodes.label: Consent-as-Authorization Bridge
nodes.rationale: EnterWorktree's own description restricts it to explicit user requests, and tool descriptions override skill instructions, so the skill must state that the user's Step 0.5 consent IS the authorization the tool requires.

nodes.label: Explicit Native Tool Naming
nodes.rationale: TDD disproved the abstract 'you know your own toolkit' phrasing: agents anchored on the concrete git commands in the fallback step (2/6 pass). Naming EnterWorktree, WorktreeCreate, /worktree and --worktree turns interpretation into factual lookup and reached 50/50 across GREEN and PRESSURE tests; file splitting proved unnecessary.

nodes.label: Submodule Guard
nodes.rationale: git-dir != git-common-dir is also true inside submodules, so show-superproject-working-tree must be checked before concluding 'already in a worktree'.

nodes.label: Instruction-File Neutralization (Phase B)
nodes.rationale: Each harness reads its own instruction file, so naming CLAUDE.md as if it were the only one is a Claude-Code-centric assumption. The generic phrase 'your instructions file' is used in prose and the per-platform reference docs name the concrete filename.

nodes.label: Phase B Carve-Outs
nodes.rationale: The using-superpowers priority list already names all three files inclusively and is making a real claim; CREATION-LOG paths are historical fact; CLAUDE_MD_TESTING.md is a worked example whose whole point is CLAUDE.md content, so normalizing it defeats the example.

nodes.label: Agent-Neutral Prose (Phase A)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI's vendored fork attempted a wholesale rewrite that was actively wrong - rewriting historical attribution paths, model names and platform install instructions. Phasing by reference category, with a mixed second/third-person substitution chosen per sentence, removes incidental platform-centric prose without repeating that mistake.

nodes.label: CSO to SDO Rename
nodes.rationale: Claude Search Optimization becomes Skill Discovery Optimization; landed as its own mechanical first commit so it is trivially revertible if the term is reconsidered.

nodes.label: Phase A Claude Carve-Outs
nodes.rationale: Model names (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus), filenames and URLs, the branded 'Claude Code' runtime name, and dated historical artifacts under docs/ all stay as-is; rewriting them rewrites history or breaks real product references.

nodes.label: Alphabetical Platform Ordering (Phase C)
nodes.rationale: After prose and config refs were neutralized the remaining platform-leaning signal was layout. Strict alphabetical ordering of both listings is verifiable byte-for-byte (section moves only, anchors still resolve) and leaves Claude Code first by alphabetical chance.

nodes.label: evals/ Canonical Eval Harness
nodes.rationale: Drill was already the de facto harness and migration momentum existed, so the full source, scenarios, fixtures, prompts and backends move in-repo under evals/ while the internal Python package keeps the name 'drill' to keep the diff small.

nodes.label: Drill Actor/Verifier Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Drives real tmux sessions with an LLM actor as simulated user and an LLM verifier over the transcript, reporting pass/fail per scenario across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot CLI.

nodes.label: Per-File Bash Test Deletion Gate
nodes.rationale: A bash test is deleted only when every assertion it makes maps to a verify.assertions or verify.criteria entry in a named drill scenario; commit-message claims of replacement are not evidence. Default is keep.

nodes.label: tests/ vs evals/ Split
nodes.rationale: tests/ answers 'does the plugin's non-LLM code work' (bash + node + python unit/integration); evals/ answers 'do agents behave correctly on real LLM sessions'. Keeping the boundary explicit and documented stops the two from silently absorbing each other.

nodes.label: Task-Scoped Per-Task Review
nodes.rationale: Per-task quality reviewers inherited a merge-readiness template ending in 'Ready to merge?', which licensed branch-scale breadth on one-task diffs - measured at 4-8x the cost of spec reviewers, one running 50+ Bash commands over 200 seconds. Per-task reviews become diff-first with justified broadening while the final branch review keeps full breadth.

nodes.label: Diff-Scope Guard
nodes.rationale: 'Only read files in this diff. Do not crawl the broader codebase' kept spec reviewers at 6-16 tool calls and 14-65 seconds; the guard existed in the spec prompt but was never carried over to the quality prompt.

nodes.label: Merged Single Task Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Per-dispatch overhead dominated cost (3 spin-ups per task each re-deriving the diff, controller coordination half the dollars), so the separate spec and quality stages became one reviewer reading the diff once and returning two verdicts. Result on go-fractals: 47.5 min / 15.7M / $13.55, blind-judged 9/10 vs baseline 7/10.

nodes.label: Turn Count Beats Token Price
nodes.rationale: 678 of 1197 subagent turns were haiku, and cheap models took 2-3x the turns on multi-step work, so a mid-tier floor for multi-step dispatches is cheaper than the lower per-token price.

nodes.label: Reviewer Severity Calibration
nodes.rationale: Important means cannot-trust-until-fixed and now explicitly names merge-blocking maintainability damage (verbatim duplication, swallowed errors, assertion-free tests); Minor findings are pasted into the final review for triage. Reviewer skepticism extends to the implementer's own design rationales.

nodes.label: No Redundant Reviewer Test Runs
nodes.rationale: No reviewer ran heavy tests autonomously - every expensive run traced to an open-ended controller-written directive. So the fix is a test budget plus controller prompt guidance, not narrowing what re-reviewers read; full re-reviews deliberately stay at full reading breadth.

nodes.label: Negative-Instruction Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Measured 2026-06-10: prohibitions work for discrete directives and read-at-decision-time recognition, but backfire on composition when the model has its own agenda for the output - 'don't restate the brief' scored 4.4 re-typed values, worse than no guidance (3.6), while a positive recipe hit 3.0 with zero variance. Adding nuance clauses to a winning recipe makes it worse, and ties go to the shorter phrasing because Codex re-reads SKILL.md ~500x per long session.

nodes.label: Phrase-Level Tripwire
nodes.rationale: Self-checks on concrete tokens ('if the prompt you are writing contains X, stop') fire reliably; 3 exist across the skill set and all are kept.

nodes.label: Recognition Table
nodes.rationale: Red-Flags and rationalization tables are read at decision time rather than composition time, which is the category that measurably works; 14 exist and all are kept.

nodes.label: Relocating the No-Placeholders List to Self-Review
nodes.rationale: The banned-pattern tokens are genuinely load-bearing: writing-plans' Self-Review cites them as its scan inventory, so a naive swap to a positive recipe breaks that reference and discards good tripwire tokens. Predicted winner V2 keeps a positive composition recipe at compose time and moves the same tokens wholesale into the review-time scan - from the category that primes into the category that detects.
nodes.norm_label: relocating the no-placeholders list to self-review

nodes.label: Strict-Cost Experiment Ladder
nodes.rationale: Objective is dollars per plan-execution with wall-clock unconstrained. Every rung ships only with its own gate evidence and dies on any quality regression; gates run N=5 because single-run gates were the campaign's weakest methodology.

nodes.label: Cheapen Mechanics, Never Judgment
nodes.rationale: Judgment failures are rare-event, high-blast-radius and largely invisible to pass/fail gates, so 'the cheap model usually gets it right' is not acceptance evidence. Named judgment points (BLOCKED handling, cannot-verify-from-diff adjudication, dispatch curation, severity calibration, false-positive calls, escalate-to-human recognition) must move up-tier, be decided once at plan time, or the rung dies.

nodes.label: Fresh Subagent Per Task Thesis
nodes.rationale: Dispatch-time task batching is counter-thesis - it pollutes the fresh-context property and coarsens the per-task gates - so it is deliberately kept off the ladder. The thesis-compatible route to the same dispatch economics is plan-time task right-sizing.

nodes.label: L1 Plan-Side Crispness
nodes.rationale: The plan is upstream of every cost: task count sets dispatch count, ambiguity sets review-loop count, completeness sets implementer exploration. Final attribution: the cost win belongs to opus-written complete-code plans, not the guidance - hand-written prose fixture plans were unrepresentative and ~2x costlier to execute - so the writing-plans PR claims fidelity and variance reduction, not dollars.

nodes.label: Structured Global Constraints Section
nodes.rationale: Version floors and naming/platform rules live in design prose and reach reviewers only if the controller remembers to paste them - a go 1.26.1 floor violation shipped because none did. A fixed heading makes them mechanically extractable so task-brief can append them to every brief automatically, removing a controller responsibility.

nodes.label: Companion Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Assets are screen content, the session key, state/events (which the agent reads as user feedback) and local session files. In scope: a malicious tab on another localhost port, a page that can reach but should not authenticate to the companion, a direct remote client on a non-loopback bind, and leakage via history/referrers/committed state. Out of scope by design: malicious agent-authored screen HTML and malicious same-origin vendored JS, since sandboxing those needs an iframe+message-bridge architecture beyond this pass.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Keyed Loads
nodes.rationale: GET /?key=<token> returns a tiny bootstrap page that sets the cookie, stores the key in tab-scoped sessionStorage and location.replace('/'), so the visible screen URL is bare '/'. This keeps the key out of the address bar, history and referrer surface while leaving a reconnect credential that survives same-port restarts.

nodes.label: WebSocket Same-Origin Enforcement
nodes.rationale: A cross-origin localhost page could open a cookie-authenticated WebSocket and write attacker-controlled choices into state/events once the real page had set the cookie. Upgrades now require valid auth AND, when an Origin header is present, Origin === 'http://' + host; non-browser clients may omit Origin but still need the key.

nodes.label: sessionStorage Reconnect Credential
nodes.rationale: In headed Chrome, after a same-port/same-token restart the browser stopped presenting the cookie, leaving the tab stuck on the tombstone until a manual reload. helper.js reads the tab-scoped key and appends it to the WebSocket URL, falling back to cookie-only for already-loaded pages.

nodes.label: Realpath Containment for /files/*
nodes.rationale: /files/* served symlinks pointing outside content/, including one to state/server-info containing the keyed URL. Both CONTENT_DIR and the requested file are resolved with realpathSync and only descendants are served; path.basename stays so nested paths remain unsupported.

nodes.label: Leak-Reduction Headers
nodes.rationale: Referrer-Policy no-referrer, Cache-Control no-store, X-Frame-Options DENY, CSP frame-ancestors none and CORP same-origin are added, but a restrictive script-src CSP is deliberately omitted because the companion injects inline helper JS and future screens may load same-origin vendored libraries.

nodes.label: Root Screen Containment
nodes.rationale: The root GET / selection path bypassed the /files/* guard, so a symlink or hardlink under content/ could still leak state/server-info. getNewestScreen() must reuse the same regular-file-inside-content-dir boundary, including rejecting link counts above one where the platform reports them, and fall back to the waiting page when nothing safe remains.

nodes.label: Fallback Token Isolation
nodes.rationale: Reusing a persisted .last-token on port fallback creates two live same-project servers sharing one bearer key. Token source becomes explicit: an env BRAINSTORM_TOKEN is an operator override so occupancy must fail closed; a loaded .last-token is discarded and a fresh unpersisted token generated for the fallback process.

nodes.label: Stop-Server Instance-ID Ownership Proof
nodes.rationale: start-server.sh passes an inert --brainstorm-server-id=<id> argument (shell/MSYS-safe alphabet, owner-only state file) purely as process-ownership evidence, not a credential. stop-server.sh signals only when that exact full argv token is present - via /proc/<pid>/cmdline, else wide ps - so it can never kill an unrelated node server.cjs.

nodes.label: Inherited Security Invariants
nodes.rationale: The fixup explicitly preserves rather than revisits the prior pass: owner-only .last-token and server-info, fallback tokens never persisted, port-named HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies scoped to /, WS auth plus Origin checks, no-Origin clients allowed only with the key, and same-origin screen JS still trusted.

nodes.label: Evals Submodule Rebase and Evidence Discipline
nodes.rationale: The branch carried an older evals submodule bump handled separately, so it must be rebased away and the PR body must cite external eval evidence exactly - repo commit, scenario path, command, artifact id, RED/GREEN outcome - rather than implying the bump is part of this PR.
nodes.norm_label: evals submodule rebase and evidence discipline

nodes.label: run-hook.cmd Polyglot Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs hooks through the system default shell (CMD on Windows, bash elsewhere). One generic dispatcher is a polyglot: Windows executes the batch block and exits with 'exit /b', while Unix shells swallow that block as a no-op heredoc and exec the named script. The doc defers to the code as authoritative.

nodes.label: Windows .sh Auto-Prepend Hazard
nodes.rationale: Claude Code on Windows automatically prepends 'bash' to any command containing .sh in its path, which hijacks the dispatcher invocation; giving hook scripts no extension is what prevents it.

nodes.label: Silent Exit When No Bash Is Found
nodes.rationale: After trying both Git for Windows paths and PATH, the dispatcher exits 0 rather than erroring so the plugin keeps working for users without Git Bash - hook context injection is skipped gracefully. It also drops -l and cygpath: scripts must be self-contained, and bash handles the Windows path directly.
nodes.norm_label: silent exit when no bash is found

nodes.label: Brainstorming Hard Gate
nodes.rationale: No implementation skill, code, scaffolding or other implementation action before a design is presented and approved - for every project regardless of perceived simplicity, because 'simple' projects are where unexamined assumptions waste the most work. The only terminal transition is writing-plans.

nodes.label: Inline Spec Self-Review
nodes.rationale: A fresh-eyes pass over the written spec for placeholders, internal contradictions, scope and two-way ambiguity - fixed inline with no re-review loop, then handed to the user as a review gate.

nodes.label: Just-in-Time Visual Companion Offer
nodes.rationale: The companion is offered at the first question that would genuinely be clearer shown than described, in its own message - never upfront, and never at all if no visual question arises.

nodes.label: Design for Isolation and Clarity
nodes.rationale: Units should have one purpose, well-defined interfaces and independent testability. This also serves the agent directly: it reasons better about code it can hold in context at once, and its edits are more reliable when files are focused, so a large file is a signal of doing too much.

nodes.label: Scope Decomposition Check
nodes.rationale: Flag multi-subsystem requests before spending questions refining details of a project that needs decomposing; each sub-project then gets its own spec, plan and implementation cycle.

nodes.label: Spec Reviewer Calibration
nodes.rationale: Only flag what would cause real problems during planning - missing sections, contradictions, two-way ambiguity. Wording preferences, stylistic nits and uneven section detail are not issues; approve unless gaps would produce a flawed plan.

nodes.label: Visual-vs-Terminal Decision Test
nodes.rationale: Decide per question, not per session: would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it? A question merely about a UI topic is not automatically visual - 'what kind of wizard do you want' is conceptual (terminal), 'which of these wizard layouts feels right' is visual (browser).

nodes.label: Visual Companion Loop
nodes.rationale: Confirm the server is alive (server-info present, server-stopped absent), write a freshly named HTML file with a file-creation tool rather than a heredoc, end the turn with the URL and a text summary, then merge the terminal reply with state_dir/events next turn. Push a waiting screen to unload the browser when the conversation returns to the terminal.

nodes.label: Complete Session-Key URL
nodes.rationale: The server rejects any request without the key, so the whole url field must be handed over - never stripped to a bare host:port. The key gates HTTP and WebSocket access so a stray tab or another machine on the network cannot read screens or inject events; after first load the cookie carries it.

nodes.label: Content Fragments vs Full Documents
nodes.rationale: Files starting with DOCTYPE or html are served as-is with only the helper injected; anything else is wrapped in the frame template, gaining the header, theme CSS, status and interactive infrastructure. Fragments are the default; full documents only when total page control is needed.

nodes.label: Per-Platform Server Launch Modes
nodes.rationale: The server must survive across turns, but environments differ: the script self-backgrounds on Claude Code, switches to foreground on Windows and under CODEX_CI because Codex reaps detached processes, and Copilot CLI needs --foreground with an async bash shell. Where stdout is lost, state/server-info is the fallback for URL and port.

nodes.label: --project-dir Persistence and Same-Port Restart
nodes.rationale: Passing the project root persists mockups under .superpowers/brainstorm/ and lets a restart reuse the same port, so the user's open tab reconnects itself instead of needing a new URL. Without it files land in /tmp and get cleaned up, and .superpowers/ must be gitignored.

nodes.label: One Agent Per Independent Domain
nodes.rationale: Agents must never inherit the session's context or history - the dispatcher constructs exactly what each needs, which keeps them focused and preserves the coordinator's own context. Only genuinely independent domains qualify: related failures, exploratory debugging and shared state all argue for a single investigation.

nodes.label: Agent Prompt Structure
nodes.rationale: Focused scope, self-contained context (paste the actual error messages and test names), explicit constraints so the agent does not refactor everything, and a named expected output - otherwise the coordinator cannot tell what changed.

nodes.label: Parallel Dispatch in One Response
nodes.rationale: Multiple dispatch calls in one response run concurrently; one per response is sequential. Integration then requires reading each summary, checking for conflicting edits, and running the full suite because agents can make systematic errors.

nodes.label: Stop and Ask on Blocker
nodes.rationale: Stop immediately on a missing dependency, failing test, unclear instruction, critical plan gap or repeated verification failure - ask rather than guess, and never force through a blocker.

nodes.label: Prefer Subagent-Driven Development
nodes.rationale: Superpowers works materially better with subagents, so on platforms that support them (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, Copilot CLI) subagent-driven-development should be used instead of this single-session skill.

nodes.label: Four-Option Finishing Menu
nodes.rationale: Exactly four structured options (merge locally, push and PR, keep as-is, discard) with no added explanation, because an open-ended 'what next?' is ambiguous. Discard requires a typed confirmation.

nodes.label: Provenance-Gated Worktree Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Cleanup runs only for merge and discard - options 2 and 3 keep the worktree alive for PR iteration. Only worktrees under .worktrees/ or worktrees/ are removed; harness-owned ones cause phantom state if touched. Merge must succeed before removal, removal must precede branch deletion (git branch -d fails while a worktree references the branch), and the removal must run from the main repo root or it fails silently.

nodes.label: Pre-Menu Test Verification Gate
nodes.rationale: Tests are run and must pass before any option is offered, and again on the merged result - otherwise the flow merges broken code or opens a failing PR.

nodes.label: Six-Step Feedback Response Pattern
nodes.rationale: Read → understand → verify → evaluate → respond → implement one at a time, because verification before implementation keeps technical correctness ahead of social comfort.

nodes.label: Ban on Performative Agreement
nodes.rationale: Phrases like 'You're absolutely right!' or any gratitude expression are banned because actions speak: the fix in the code is the acknowledgment, and praise before verification signals compliance rather than evaluation.

nodes.label: Clarify All Unclear Items Before Implementing Any
nodes.rationale: Feedback items may be related, so partial understanding produces wrong implementation; stop and clarify everything before touching anything.
nodes.norm_label: clarify all unclear items before implementing any

nodes.label: YAGNI Check for Reviewer-Suggested Features
nodes.rationale: When a reviewer asks to 'implement properly', grep for actual usage first — an uncalled endpoint should be removed, not built out; both you and the reviewer report to the human partner.

nodes.label: Reasoned Technical Pushback
nodes.rationale: External feedback is suggestions to evaluate, not orders to follow; push back with technical reasoning when a suggestion breaks functionality, violates YAGNI, or conflicts with the partner's architectural decisions.

nodes.label: Review Early, Review Often
nodes.rationale: A reviewer subagent gets precisely crafted context rather than the session's history, which keeps it focused on the work product and preserves the requester's own context for continued work.

nodes.label: Issue Severity Calibration (Critical/Important/Minor)
nodes.rationale: Not everything is Critical; miscalibrated severity destroys the signal. Accurate praise before issues is included deliberately so the implementer trusts the rest of the feedback.

nodes.label: Read-Only Review Constraint
nodes.rationale: Reviewers must never move HEAD or mutate the index of the checkout under review; if another revision is needed, add a separate temporary worktree so the implementer's workspace is never disturbed.

nodes.label: Fresh Subagent Per Task
nodes.rationale: Subagents should never inherit the controller's session history; a precisely constructed context keeps them focused and preserves the controller's context for coordination.

nodes.label: Model Selection by Task Complexity
nodes.rationale: Use the least powerful model that can do the role, but turn count beats token price: the cheapest models take 2-3x the turns on multi-step work, so a mid-tier model is the floor for reviewers and prose-spec implementers. An omitted model silently inherits the session's most expensive one.

nodes.label: File Handoffs for Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Anything pasted into a dispatch or printed back stays resident in the controller's context and is re-read every turn; briefs, reports, and review packages move as files so bulk text never enters context (a real dispatch hit 42k chars of which 99% was pasted history).

nodes.label: Durable Progress Ledger
nodes.rationale: Conversation memory does not survive compaction and controllers have re-dispatched entire completed task sequences — the most expensive observed failure. The ledger at .superpowers/sdd/progress.md plus git log is the recovery map, trusted over recollection.

nodes.label: Implementer Status Handling (DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Never ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry unchanged — if the implementer is stuck, something must change (context, model, task size, or the plan).
nodes.norm_label: implementer status handling (done / done_with_concerns / needs_context / blocked)

nodes.label: Pre-Flight Plan Review
nodes.rationale: Scan the plan once for self-contradictions and for anything the plan mandates that the review rubric calls a defect, and batch them into one question to the human — rather than one interrupt per discovery mid-plan.

nodes.label: No Pre-Judging Reviewer Findings
nodes.rationale: Never tell a reviewer what not to flag or pre-rate a severity; phrases like 'do not flag' or 'at most Minor' in a dispatch mean the controller is sparing itself a review loop. Let the reviewer raise it and adjudicate in the loop.

nodes.label: Global Constraints Block as Reviewer Attention Lens
nodes.rationale: Copy binding requirements verbatim from the plan's Global Constraints — exact values, formats, and stated relationships — because the template already carries the process rules; the constraints block is for what this project's spec demands.
nodes.norm_label: global constraints block as reviewer attention lens

nodes.label: scripts/review-package
nodes.rationale: Writes commit list, stat summary, and full diff with context to one uniquely named file so the reviewer needs one Read and the diff never enters the controller's context. BASE must be the recorded pre-dispatch commit, never HEAD~1, which silently truncates multi-commit tasks.

nodes.label: scripts/task-brief
nodes.rationale: Extracts one task's full text to a file so the brief is the single source of requirements and the implementer never reads the whole plan.

nodes.label: Continuous Execution Without Check-Ins
nodes.rationale: 'Should I continue?' prompts and progress summaries waste the partner's time — they asked for the plan to be executed. Only BLOCKED, genuine ambiguity, or completion justify stopping.

nodes.label: Resolving Reviewer ⚠️ Cannot-Verify Items
nodes.rationale: Requirements living in unchanged code or spanning tasks cannot be judged from one diff; the controller holds the cross-task context the reviewer lacks and must resolve each item before marking the task complete.

nodes.label: One Fix Subagent for the Whole Findings List
nodes.rationale: Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.
nodes.norm_label: one fix subagent for the whole findings list

nodes.label: Implementer Self-Review (Completeness/Quality/Discipline/Testing)
nodes.rationale: Fresh-eyes self-review catches issues before handoff, but never replaces actual review — both are required.

nodes.label: In-Over-Your-Head Escalation Contract
nodes.rationale: Bad work is worse than no work, so escalating is explicitly unpenalized; the controller can add context, upgrade the model, or split the task. Never silently produce work you are unsure about.

nodes.label: RED/GREEN TDD Evidence in Report
nodes.rationale: The implementer's report is the test evidence because reviewers will not re-run tests; it must carry the commands and the failing-then-passing output.

nodes.label: Focused-File Code Organization Rule
nodes.rationale: An agent reasons best about code it can hold in context at once and edits more reliably in focused files; but files must not be split on the agent's own initiative — report DONE_WITH_CONCERNS instead.

nodes.label: Do Not Trust the Implementer's Report
nodes.rationale: The report is unverified claims; design rationales like 'left it per YAGNI' are the implementer grading their own work, and a stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity.
nodes.norm_label: do not trust the implementer's report

nodes.label: Spec Compliance Verdict (Missing/Extra/Misunderstood)
nodes.rationale: Two independent verdicts — spec compliance and code quality — prevent both under-building and over-building from passing as done.

nodes.label: Diff-Scoped Review Method
nodes.rationale: The diff's context lines ARE the changed files, so the reviewer must not crawl the codebase; inspecting outside the diff is allowed only for a concrete named risk (lock ordering, API contract, shared mutable state), one focused check per risk.

nodes.label: Reviewers Do Not Re-Run the Suite
nodes.rationale: The implementer already ran the tests with TDD evidence for exactly this code; a reviewer runs a focused test only for a specific unanswered doubt, and recommends heavy validation rather than performing it.
nodes.norm_label: reviewers do not re-run the suite

nodes.label: Plan-Mandated Finding
nodes.rationale: If the plan mandates something the rubric calls a defect, it is still an Important finding labeled plan-mandated: the plan's authorship does not grade its own work, and the human decides which governs.

nodes.label: Skill Bulletproofing Against Rationalization
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS/NEVER wording, 'even if faster' clauses, structural gates, and deliberate redundancy are chosen to resist pressure; the strongest device is the anti-patterns section, because seeing the exact shortcut you were about to take listed as wrong creates cognitive friction.

nodes.label: Testing Skills With Subagents
nodes.rationale: Four validation scenarios (academic, time pressure, complex system, failed first fix) probe whether the skill survives the conditions that produce rationalization.

nodes.label: Debugging Iron Law: No Fixes Without Root Cause Investigation
nodes.rationale: Symptom fixes are failure; systematic debugging is faster than guess-and-check thrashing (15-30 min vs 2-3 hours, 95% vs 40% first-time fix rate), so the process is not sacrificed under time pressure.
nodes.norm_label: debugging iron law: no fixes without root cause investigation

nodes.label: Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
nodes.rationale: One hypothesis at a time and the smallest possible change, because multiple simultaneous fixes make it impossible to isolate what worked.

nodes.label: Three-Failed-Fixes Means Wrong Architecture
nodes.rationale: When each fix reveals new coupling elsewhere or demands massive refactoring, that is not a failed hypothesis but a wrong architecture; stop and question fundamentals with the human instead of attempting fix #4.

nodes.label: Component-Boundary Diagnostic Instrumentation
nodes.rationale: In multi-component systems, logging what enters and exits each boundary once reveals WHICH layer breaks, so investigation narrows to that component instead of guessing across the stack.

nodes.label: Partner Signals You're Doing It Wrong
nodes.rationale: Phrases like 'Is that not happening?', 'Stop guessing', and 'Ultra-think this' are diagnostic of assumed-not-verified reasoning; they mean return to Phase 1.
nodes.norm_label: partner signals you're doing it wrong

nodes.label: Legitimate 'No Root Cause' Exit
nodes.rationale: Truly environmental or external issues get documented investigation plus retry/timeout handling and monitoring — but 95% of 'no root cause' claims are incomplete investigation.

nodes.label: Condition-Based Waiting
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary delays encode a guess about timing, so tests pass on fast machines and fail under load or in parallel CI; wait on the actual condition instead. Fixed 15 flaky tests, 60%→100% pass rate, 40% faster.

nodes.label: waitFor polling helper
nodes.rationale: Polls every 10ms (1ms wastes CPU), always carries a timeout with a descriptive error, and calls the getter inside the loop so state is never stale.

nodes.label: When an Arbitrary Timeout IS Correct
nodes.rationale: Legitimate only when testing timed behavior itself: first wait for the triggering condition, then wait a duration derived from known intervals, with a comment justifying the number.
nodes.norm_label: when an arbitrary timeout is correct

nodes.label: Defense-in-Depth Validation
nodes.rationale: A single validation point gets bypassed by different code paths, refactors, and mocks. Single validation says 'we fixed the bug'; layered validation makes the bug structurally impossible.

nodes.label: Layer 3: Environment Guards
nodes.rationale: Context-specific dangers (git init outside tmpdir during tests) need a guard that only fires in that context, catching cases entry validation and business logic both miss.

nodes.label: Layer 4: Debug Instrumentation
nodes.rationale: Stack-trace logging before the dangerous operation is the forensic layer that identifies structural misuse when the other three layers fail.

nodes.label: Root Cause Tracing
nodes.rationale: Bugs manifest deep in the call stack, and the instinct to fix where the error appears treats a symptom; trace backward to the original trigger and fix at the source. Only fix at the symptom point when backward tracing dead-ends.

nodes.label: Empty projectDir Case Study
nodes.rationale: An empty cwd resolved to process.cwd() and ran git init in the source tree; the five-level trace ended at a top-level variable read before beforeEach, fixed by making tempDir a throwing getter plus four defense layers.

nodes.label: Stack Trace Instrumentation for Tracing
nodes.rationale: Use console.error not the logger in tests (loggers may be suppressed), log before the dangerous operation rather than after failure, and include cwd/env/timestamps with new Error().stack.

nodes.label: find-polluter.sh bisection script
nodes.rationale: When an artifact appears during a suite but the culprit test is unknown, run tests one-by-one and stop at the first polluter.

nodes.label: Academic Test: Systematic Debugging
nodes.rationale: No-pressure comprehension baseline: answers must be quoted from the skill, establishing that the rules are readable before testing whether they hold under pressure.

nodes.label: Pressure Test 1: Emergency Production Fix
nodes.rationale: Pits the process against quantified revenue loss ($15k/min) and manager pressure, with a plausible 'compromise' option, to see whether cost framing produces rationalization.

nodes.label: Pressure Test 2: Sunk Cost + Exhaustion
nodes.rationale: Four hours of escalating sleep() guesses plus fatigue and personal plans test whether sunk cost and exhaustion license a 'good enough' timeout with a TODO.

nodes.label: Pressure Test 3: Authority + Social Pressure
nodes.rationale: A senior engineer's experience claim, tech-lead approval, and a room that wants the call to end test whether deference overrides Phase 2's 'read the reference completely'.

nodes.label: TDD Iron Law: No Production Code Without a Failing Test First
nodes.rationale: If you didn't watch the test fail you don't know it tests the right thing. Code written before its test must be deleted outright — kept as 'reference' it gets adapted, which is testing after.
nodes.norm_label: tdd iron law: no production code without a failing test first

nodes.label: Verify RED — Watch It Fail Correctly
nodes.rationale: The test must fail because the feature is missing, not because of a typo or an error; a test that passes immediately is testing existing behavior.
nodes.norm_label: verify red — watch it fail correctly

nodes.label: GREEN — Minimal Code Only
nodes.rationale: Write just enough to pass; options objects and configurable backoff nobody asked for are YAGNI violations that the test never forced.

nodes.label: Tests-First Answers 'What Should This Do?'
nodes.rationale: Tests written after are biased by the implementation — they verify remembered edge cases rather than discovered ones, and passing immediately proves nothing. Coverage without the failure proof is not TDD.

nodes.label: Sunk Cost Fallacy on Untested Code
nodes.rationale: The hours are already gone; the real waste is keeping code you cannot trust. Working code without real tests is technical debt.
nodes.norm_label: sunk cost fallacy on untested code

nodes.label: Hard to Test Means Hard to Use
nodes.rationale: Complicated test setup or needing to mock everything is a design signal (too coupled, interface too complex), not a testing problem — listen to the test.
nodes.norm_label: hard to test means hard to use

nodes.label: Testing Anti-Patterns
nodes.rationale: Mocks are tools to isolate, not things to test; strict TDD structurally prevents every anti-pattern here.

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern: Testing Mock Behavior
nodes.rationale: Asserting on a *-mock test ID verifies the mock is present, not that the component works — it tells you nothing about real behavior.

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern: Test-Only Methods in Production Classes
nodes.rationale: A destroy() used only by tests looks like production API, is dangerous if ever called, and confuses object lifecycle with entity lifecycle; cleanup belongs in test utilities.
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: test-only methods in production classes

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern: Mocking Without Understanding Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Mocking a high-level method can remove a side effect the test depends on, so the test passes for the wrong reason; mock the actual slow/external operation at the lowest level instead.

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern: Incomplete Mocks
nodes.rationale: Partial mocks hide structural assumptions and fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field; mirror the complete real response schema, not just the fields this test uses.

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern: Integration Tests as Afterthought
nodes.rationale: 'Implementation complete, ready for testing' is not complete — testing is part of implementation.

nodes.label: Pre-Mock Gate Function
nodes.rationale: Before mocking anything, enumerate the real method's side effects and whether the test depends on them; if unsure, run with the real implementation first and add minimal mocking after observing what is needed.

nodes.label: using-git-worktrees (skill)
nodes.rationale: Detect existing isolation first, then native tools, then git fallback — never fight the harness.

nodes.label: Step 0: Detect Existing Isolation
nodes.rationale: GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON means a linked worktree, so creating another would nest; but the same comparison is true inside submodules, hence the show-superproject-working-tree guard.

nodes.label: Prefer Native Worktree Tools
nodes.rationale: Native tools (EnterWorktree, /worktree, --worktree) handle placement, branch creation, and cleanup; using git worktree add instead creates phantom state the harness cannot see or manage. This is named the #1 mistake.

nodes.label: Step 1b: Git Worktree Fallback
nodes.rationale: Directory priority is explicit user instruction > existing project-local .worktrees/ or worktrees/ (.worktrees wins) > default .worktrees/, so conventions are never silently overridden.

nodes.label: Worktree Directory Ignore Verification
nodes.rationale: git check-ignore must pass before creating a project-local worktree, otherwise worktree contents get tracked and committed into the repository.

nodes.label: Step 3: Verify Clean Test Baseline
nodes.rationale: Without a green baseline you cannot distinguish new bugs from pre-existing failures; report failures and get explicit permission before proceeding.

nodes.label: Sandbox Permission Fallback
nodes.rationale: If worktree creation is denied by the sandbox, say so plainly and work in the current directory rather than retrying or silently proceeding.

nodes.label: using-superpowers (skill)
nodes.rationale: Invoke any plausibly relevant skill before any response or action, including clarifying questions — a 1% chance it applies is enough, and it can be discarded after reading.

nodes.label: Skill Priority: Process Before Implementation
nodes.rationale: Process skills set the approach and implementation skills carry it out; 'let's build X' starts with brainstorming, 'fix this bug' starts with systematic-debugging.

nodes.label: Skill-Skipping Rationalization Table
nodes.rationale: Thoughts like 'I need more context first' or 'I remember this skill' are the observed excuses; skills tell you HOW to explore and they evolve, so the check precedes information gathering.

nodes.label: Platform Adaptation via Reference Files
nodes.rationale: Skills speak in actions rather than tool names, so each harness gets a reference file mapping those actions onto its real tools.

nodes.label: Instruction Precedence Order
nodes.rationale: User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) override skills, which override default behavior; a dispatched subagent ignores this skill entirely.

nodes.label: Task Artifact (Antigravity todo substitute)
nodes.rationale: Antigravity has no todo tool and manage_task governs background processes, so checklists live in a markdown task artifact that must be re-read before each step once the conversation grows long.

nodes.label: Codex multi_agent Feature Flag
nodes.rationale: spawn_agent/wait_agent/close_agent only exist with [features] multi_agent = true, which is what subagent-driven-development and dispatching-parallel-agents require; implementer and reviewer agents must be closed when done.

nodes.label: Read-Only Git Environment Detection
nodes.rationale: GIT_DIR vs GIT_COMMON reveals an existing linked worktree and an empty BRANCH reveals detached HEAD, meaning branch/push/PR cannot happen from the sandbox.

nodes.label: Codex App Finishing Handoff
nodes.rationale: When the sandbox blocks branch/push, the agent commits everything and hands off through the App's Create-branch or Hand-off-to-local controls, still supplying suggested branch names, commit messages, and PR text.

nodes.label: pi-subagents package
nodes.rationale: Pi core ships no subagent tool; if none is installed, execute sequentially or say the capability is missing — never fabricate Task calls.

nodes.label: Markdown/TODO.md Task List Fallback
nodes.rationale: Pi core ships no task-list tool, and older Superpowers docs referencing TodoWrite should be read as the generic task-tracking action.

nodes.label: Verification Iron Law: No Completion Claims Without Fresh Evidence
nodes.rationale: Claiming completion without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency; if the command was not run in this message, the claim cannot be made. Drawn from 24 failure memories where trust was broken and undefined functions shipped.
nodes.norm_label: verification iron law: no completion claims without fresh evidence

nodes.label: Verification Gate Function
nodes.rationale: Identify the proving command, run it fully and fresh, read the whole output and exit code, confirm it supports the claim, and only then speak; skipping a step is lying rather than verifying.

nodes.label: Insufficient Proxies for Verification
nodes.rationale: A passing linter is not a compiler, a previous run is not this run, and an agent's success report is not a VCS diff — each claim has exactly one command that proves it.

nodes.label: Red-Green Verification of a Regression Test
nodes.rationale: A regression test is only proven by reverting the fix and confirming the test fails, then restoring; passing once shows nothing about whether it catches the bug.
nodes.norm_label: red-green verification of a regression test

nodes.label: Expressions of Satisfaction Count as Claims
nodes.rationale: The rule binds paraphrases, synonyms, and implications — 'Great!', 'should work now', or any wording implying success is covered, so spirit governs over letter.
nodes.norm_label: expressions of satisfaction count as claims

nodes.label: writing-plans (skill)
nodes.rationale: Write for a skilled developer with zero context for the codebase, questionable taste, and weak test-design instincts; that assumption is what forces exact paths, complete code, and expected command output.

nodes.label: Plan Global Constraints Section
nodes.rationale: Project-wide requirements with verbatim exact values live in one section because every task's requirements implicitly include it, and task implementers only ever see their own brief.

nodes.label: File Structure Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Map files before tasks because that is where decomposition is locked in: one responsibility per file, files that change together live together, split by responsibility not technical layer.

nodes.label: Task Right-Sizing
nodes.rationale: A task is the smallest unit worth its own test cycle and a fresh reviewer's gate: fold setup and docs into the task that needs them, and split only where a reviewer could reject one task while approving its neighbor.

nodes.label: Bite-Sized Step Granularity
nodes.rationale: Each step is one 2-5 minute action, and the canonical sequence (write failing test, watch it fail, minimal code, watch it pass, commit) bakes the TDD cycle into the plan itself.

nodes.label: Task Interfaces Block (Consumes/Produces)
nodes.rationale: An implementer sees only their own task, so exact signatures and return types of neighbouring tasks must be declared here or they cannot integrate.

nodes.label: No Placeholders Rule
nodes.rationale: TBD, 'add appropriate error handling', and 'similar to Task N' are plan failures because tasks may be read out of order and an agent cannot recover the missing content; code steps require actual code blocks.

nodes.label: Plan Self-Review Checklist
nodes.rationale: Three passes run by the author, not a subagent: spec coverage, placeholder scan, and type consistency (clearLayers() in Task 3 vs clearFullLayers() in Task 7 is a bug). Fix inline, no re-review.

nodes.label: Execution Handoff Choice
nodes.rationale: After saving the plan, offer subagent-driven (recommended, fresh subagent per task) or inline executing-plans, so the execution model is a human decision rather than a default.

nodes.label: Multi-Subsystem Scope Check
nodes.rationale: Each plan must produce working testable software on its own, so specs spanning independent subsystems get split into one plan per subsystem.

nodes.label: Plan Reviewer Calibration
nodes.rationale: Only flag what would make an implementer build the wrong thing or get stuck; wording and nice-to-haves are advisory and must not block approval, so the gate stays about buildability.

nodes.norm_label: the iron law: no skill without a failing test first

nodes.label: Superpowers Logo Mark (Small Variant)
nodes.rationale: Brand identity glyph for the Superpowers skill library, authored as a pure-vector SVG so a single asset serves README headers, docs, and app icons without raster variants.

nodes.label: Paired Orbital Arc Glyphs
nodes.rationale: Two mirrored crescent/hook forms sweep diagonally around the center, each built from a tapered inner wedge plus a thin outer swoosh, reading as a single continuous orbit rather than two separate shapes.

nodes.label: Central Nucleus Dot
nodes.rationale: A near-perfect ellipse (rx 28.95, ry 28.76) at the optical center anchors the composition and gives the surrounding arcs something to orbit; the sub-pixel rx/ry asymmetry is a drawing-tool artifact, not intent.

nodes.label: 180-Degree Rotational Symmetry
nodes.rationale: The two arc groups are exact point reflections of one another through the center, so the mark is orientation-neutral and stays legible when rotated or flipped.

nodes.label: Monochrome Flat-Fill Construction
nodes.rationale: All five shapes are fill-only paths with no stroke, no gradient, no filter and no explicit fill color, so the glyph inherits currentColor and renders identically on light and dark backgrounds; strokes would thin out and gradients would band at favicon size.

nodes.label: Small-Size Icon Variant
nodes.rationale: The -small filename plus the reduced shape count (five paths, ~1.7 KB) indicates a deliberately simplified sibling of a fuller logo lockup, trading detail for legibility at 16-32 px.

nodes.label: 512x512 Square ViewBox
nodes.rationale: A square viewBox with no width/height attributes lets the consumer scale the mark freely; artwork occupies roughly the middle 70% of the canvas, leaving built-in padding for icon safe areas.

nodes.label: Orbit / Atom Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Arcs circling a nucleus evoke an atom or orbital diagram - energy and composable capability - which fits a library whose premise is many small skills revolving around one core agent.

nodes.label: Alternate Reading: Interlinked Chain Link
nodes.rationale: The two hooked arcs also read as two interlocking chain links or an open infinity loop; the SVG carries no title, desc, or metadata, so which reading the designer intended cannot be confirmed from the source.

nodes.label: Illustrator Export Provenance (Calque_1)
nodes.rationale: The root element id Calque_1 is the French-locale default layer name from Adobe Illustrator, and the minified single-line output with two-decimal path coordinates matches an Illustrator SVG export rather than hand-authored markup.
